papers.title: Decoupling cellular complexity: Comparative mass transport analysis of wild-type and mutant PhoE in nanoreactors.
papers.abstract: Precise control of substrate transport across compartment boundaries is critical for the design of enzymatic nanoreactors, yet selective and tunable molecular flux remains a major bottleneck in confined reaction systems. Outer membrane porins offer a promising solution, as their transport properties can be modulated through protein engineering. Among these, the moderately anion-selective porin PhoE from Escherichia coli is an attractive candidate due to its defined pore architecture. Several PhoE mutants have previously been described and analyzed, predominantly in whole-cell assays. However, such systems limit the quantitative resolution of substrate transport, as specific flux cannot easily be disentangled from expression levels, membrane insertion efficiency, and variations in the amount of functional protein. To overcome these limitations, we employed enzyme-loaded nanoreactors as a minimal and well-defined platform to directly quantify PhoE-mediated substrate flux independent of cellular complexity. Wild-type PhoE was compared to mutants exhibiting distinct transport behaviors in bacterial cells, with F111C showing approximately 50% lower transport. Additionally, we designed and characterized the novel deletion mutant PhoEΔ102-107, which exhibited 2.4-fold higher transport than wild-type PhoE. The bottom-up synthetic biology system enabled a direct comparison of specific transport rates, demonstrating the potential of these variants for transport tuning in engineered enzymatic nanoreactors. Complementary molecular dynamics simulations provided structural insight into the molecular basis of the observed transport behavior of the PhoE mutants.
papers.authors: Scherer M, S R V, Wegner D, Marburger M, Schober R, Schäfer M, Chowdhury R, Castiglione K.

papers.title: DecoyOpt: A two-stage pipeline for decoy-aware enzyme discrimination and EC number prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient EC number prediction is essential for elucidating the catalytic roles of enzymes. Although similarity-based and deep learning-based approaches have advanced this task, they often fail to distinguish active enzymes from closely related decoys inactivated by local functional-site mutations, leading to high false-positive rates (FPRs). We propose DecoyOpt, a two-stage pipeline for decoy-aware enzyme discrimination and EC number prediction. Specifically, we generated putatively inactive functional-site decoys using ESM3 and evaluated 16 protein language models across three splits. An MLP trained with classification and ranking losses distinguishes enzymes from unannotated proteins and decoys before a contrastive learning model assigns EC numbers to predicted enzymes. On the most stringent GraphPart 40% split, DecoyOpt achieves an MCC of 0.899 and a D0 decoy FPR of 6.17%, outperforming retrained baselines. Across all splits, it outperforms these baselines in EC number prediction on the full test set while maintaining performance close to CLEAN on the enzyme subset. It also correctly annotates all four wild-type enzymes and rejects all eight inactive or nearly inactive variants. We believe that DecoyOpt has potential for annotating uncharacterized proteins and their variants, with applications in genomics, synthetic biology, and biocatalysis.
papers.authors: Liu T, Deng J, Wang X, Chen K, Zhang D, Siu SWI.
papers.status: 预印本 · 未经同行评审

papers.title: Diffusion integrity testing of small-area sterilizing-grade membrane filters in single-use assemblies.
papers.abstract: Sterile filtration represents the final critical step in biomanufacturing, where a sterilizing-grade membrane filter removes microbial contamination from the drug product - making filter integrity verification essential. While bubble point and gas-liquid diffusion tests are established non-destructive methods for hydrophilic membranes, diffusion testing offers high sensitivity to small defects and operates at lower test pressures. However, applying diffusion testing to small-area filters integrated into closed single-use assemblies remains challenging because pressure changes measured by automated integrity testers can arise not only from membrane diffusion, but also from assembly-related effects such as gas-permeable tubing, upstream volume and thermal equilibration. For low-area devices, these background contributions can become comparable to or greater than the membrane signal, reducing test sensitivity and complicating interpretation. This work presents a practical method for implementing diffusion-based integrity testing of small-format sterilizing-grade filters in final sealed single-use assemblies. The approach quantifies assembly-specific background contribution and incorporates it into an adjusted diffusion specification, allowing membrane-specific diffusion to be resolved without altering the assembled system. By accounting for system-derived measurement noise, the method enables reliable end-user integrity assessment of closed assemblies that cannot be reconfigured to reduce upstream volume or replace high-permeability tubing materials.
papers.authors: Alembath A, Hersey J.

papers.title: Efficient Bioproduction of Citric Acid in Aspergillus niger.
papers.abstract: Citric acid is the most widely produced organic acid in industrial biotechnology, with a global annual output exceeding 2 million tons and broad applications across the food, pharmaceutical, chemical, and environmental sectors. Despite more than a century of industrial development since the discovery of citric acid fermentation by Aspergillus niger in 1917, current production systems are approaching critical bottlenecks in strain performance, process efficiency, and environmental sustainability. Increasing evidence indicates that citrate overproduction is not governed by a single metabolic pathway but emerges as a multi-constraint-driven systems phenomenon involving coordinated regulation of metabolism, cellular physiology, and environmental conditions. Recent advances in systems biology and synthetic biology have enabled a paradigm shift from empirical optimization to rational and programmable biomanufacturing. The integration of multi-omics data with genome-scale metabolic models has substantially deepened the understanding of citrate overflow metabolism. In parallel, the development of CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing, dynamic gene regulation systems, and promoter engineering has enabled precise and multiplexed rewiring of metabolic networks. Targeted engineering strategies focusing on carbon uptake, mitochondrial metabolism, citrate transport, and morphology regulation have demonstrated that high-level production requires coordinated multi-layer optimization rather than single-gene modifications. At the process level, emerging strategies, including immobilized fermentation, in situ product recovery, and the utilization of alternative non-food feedstocks, are being increasingly integrated with engineered strains to enhance productivity and sustainability. These advances collectively point toward a transition from conventional fermentation to a multi-scale, integrated biomanufacturing framework. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent progress in citric acid biomanufacturing, covering the evolution of industrial A. niger strains, systems-level mechanisms of citrate accumulation, synthetic biology-enabled tool development, rational chassis engineering strategies, and process intensification approaches. Finally, we discuss future directions, including dynamic metabolic control, artificial intelligence-assisted design, and circular biorefinery systems, aiming to establish a fully integrated, intelligent, and sustainable paradigm for next-generation citric acid production.
papers.authors: Zheng X, Sun J, Zheng P.

papers.title: Enhancing Bacterial Secondary Metabolite Yields Using Non-Biological Inducers: Blind metabolic engineering.
papers.abstract: Bacteria secondary metabolites are widely used in many industries, including pharmaceutical, food, agricultural, and cosmetics. Abiotic stresses are a low-cost and easy approach to enhance the accumulation of these metabolites. On the other hand, rational metabolic engineering strategies are limited by the unknown metabolic burden, incomplete pathway knowledge, and biosafety concerns associated with genetically modified microorganisms (GMMs). This review surveys abiotic stress-driven strategies to boost secondary metabolite production in bacterial strains. It systematically analyzes how key abiotic stress-osmotic, oxidative, pH, solvent, and radiation-reshape microbial metabolism and secondary metabolite biosynthetic pathways. The main idea of this review is to elucidate the interconnected network linking diverse stress stimuli to bacterial molecular defense mechanisms, and to explore the potential applications of this crosstalk in the rational design of metabolic engineering approaches. According to the collected evidences from various studies, abiotic stresses are able to induce a significant enhancement in the production of a wide-range of secondary metabolites including pigments, fatty acids, enzymes, antibiotics, organic acids, amino acids, and alcohols in the industrially-important bacterial strains. This review emphasizes that response to abiotic stresses is significantly strain-depended and metabolite-depended, which highlights the necessity of customization of stress regimens toward specific strains and secondary metabolites.
papers.authors: Bagoghli N, Boroujeni NR.

papers.title: High-level de novo biosynthesis of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate in Bacillus licheniformis by systems engineering.
papers.abstract: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP), the active form of vitamin B6, is an essential cofactor with broad applications in the pharmaceutical and food industries. However, its microbial production is hindered by intracellular toxicity, tight metabolic regulation, degradation, and limited export. This study aimed to develop an efficient de novo PLP production platform in Bacillus licheniformis by integrating metabolic, transporter, and enzyme engineering strategies. We first assessed PLP tolerance and found that B. licheniformis tolerated exogenous PLP exposure, suggesting its potential as a production host. A xylose-inducible system was then introduced to dynamically control PLP synthase expression, thereby minimizing the adverse effects of early PLP accumulation. Subsequently, PLP biosynthesis was enhanced by improving the supply of ribose 5-phosphate, glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate, and glutamine through modular pathway optimization. In parallel, PLP degradation was reduced and a heterologous transporter was introduced to promote extracellular PLP accumulation. Furthermore, protein engineering of the PLP synthase complex was performed to improve its catalytic efficiency. The resulting strain produced 1.5 g/L PLP with a productivity of 20.8 mg/L/h in a 5-L bioreactor, the highest titer reported for microbial de novo PLP production. This work offers new insight into boosting microbial PLP production and holds considerable potential for industrial applications.
papers.authors: Wang S, Mao S, Zhang D, He Y, Wang F, Hu J, Cai D, Li L, Wang D, Zhu J, Chen S.

papers.title: Intellectual property rights and the global exchange of molecular plant technologies.
papers.abstract: The global intellectual property regime for plants is structurally misaligned with the molecular tools on which climate-resilient agriculture now depends. As gene editing, synthetic biology, and Digital Sequence Information (DSI) become central to breeding drought-, heat-, and salinity-tolerant crops, these same technologies are increasingly enclosed within dense patent thickets, trade rules that go beyond the minimum standards of the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS), commonly called TRIPS-plus rules, and costly regulatory requirements. Using doctrinal legal analysis, a patent-landscape review, and product-level case studies, we show how this architecture generates a "Market Power Effect," whereby a small group of firms can set prices, stack royalties, and control access to enabling technologies, effectively sidelining public breeders, small laboratories, and climate-vulnerable states. We develop the concept of "legal resilience" to capture the idea that molecular resilience in biotech crops is meaningless without legal structures that allow rapid, equitable diffusion of adaptive traits. Empirically, we link rising CRISPR-related patents, escalating licensing and compliance costs, and corporate concentration to stagnant yield growth, persistent human undernourishment, and an emerging form of digital biopiracy that existing access and benefit-sharing instruments cannot contain. We also examine the position of large middle-income innovators, China in particular, which do not fit the conventional North-South division and whose domestic policy choices are pushing toward stronger rather than weaker protection. On this basis, we propose a polycentric reform package: a climate-utility model tier for incremental local adaptations; a multilateral DSI benefit-sharing fund financed by small levies on commercial seed sales; compulsory humanitarian patent pools for abiotic stress-resistance technologies; regional molecular hubs that pair laboratories with pro-bono freedom-to-operate support; and sustained support for the existing network of genebanks and community seed systems as a practical counterweight to the hazard of genetic uniformity. Our central claim is that genetic resilience must be treated as an essential facility for human food security, not merely as a tradable private asset.
papers.authors: Haider A, Khan A, Szeberényi A.

papers.title: Mechanistic role of functional bacterial amyloids (FuBAs) in inflammatory responses, ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) impairment, and cross-seedings with host amyloids.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are characterized by disruption of protein homeostasis, aggregation, inflammation, and neuronal resilience, with age affecting disease susceptibility. Bacterial amyloids, such as curli, Fap, TasA, and phenol-soluble modulins, are functional amyloids that aid in biofilm formation and potentially interact with host proteins and innate immune pathways. They are cross-β-sheet proteins that interact with other proteins from different species, and experimental data show that some bacterial amyloids promote the aggregation of amyloid-β and α-synuclein. Various fuBA effects along the gut-brain axis depend on microbial production, retention in the gut, barrier integrity, clearance from the system, immune status, and tissue susceptibility. The activation of innate immune mechanisms, such as Toll-like receptor signaling, by FuBAs or related microbial signals could lead to inflammation and oxidative stress. The ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) is another aspect of cellular protein quality control that could be further compromised by increased amyloid burden. To date, direct FuBA-mediated proteasome inhibition remains poorly established. To this end, this review separates direct evidence, indirect effects of aggregation/inflammatory stress, and mechanistic precedents from studies on human amyloid. Structural biology, immunology, and proteostasis research will be combined, and FuBAs will be investigated as potential upstream modulators of the neurodegenerative proteinopathies. We assess whether FuBAs directly influence UPS function in intestinal, peripheral, or neural compartments, and discuss possible therapeutic strategies, including microbiome modulation, barrier repair, immunomodulation, and proteasome stimulation. FuBAs can alter neuronal proteostasis in both amyloid-related disorders and other neurodegenerative processes, but not necessarily act as triggers of these processes.
papers.authors: Vashishth S, Ambasta RK, Kumar P.

papers.title: Next-generation nanocellulose-based smart biomaterials: advances, functionalization strategies, and sustainable biomedical applications.
papers.abstract: Nanocellulose has emerged as a versatile platform for smart biomaterials because of its high mechanical strength, tunable surface chemistry, and biocompatibility. These properties have supported its incorporation into a wide range of biomedical materials, but many conventional nanocellulose-based systems remain predominantly passive, functioning mainly as structural or supporting components. The growing interest in smart biomaterials reflects the need for materials that can respond to changes in their environment and thereby provide more dynamic control over biomedical functions. This review examines the transition of cellulose nanocrystals, cellulose nanofibrils, and bacterial nanocellulose towards responsive and potentially adaptive biomedical platforms. The structural and molecular characteristics underlying responses to chemical, physical and electromechanical stimuli are examined, together with their application in responsive biomedical systems. Attention is also given to the sustainability-performance trade-off arising when chemical modification, synthetic polymers, or inorganic nanomaterials are introduced to increase functionality, as well as to translational barriers related to material variability, biological stability, reproducibility, safety and standardisation. Finally, emerging approaches based on synthetic biology, genetic engineering and artificial intelligence/machine learning are examined for their potential to improve the predictability and programmability of nanocellulose production and design. By relating material structure and processing to responsiveness, biomedical function, sustainability, and translational potential, this review highlights the opportunities and limitations that will shape the progression of smart nanocellulose from proof-of-concept materials towards clinically relevant biomedical platforms.
papers.authors: Edo GI, Omoathebu EE, Orogu JO, Ainyanbhor IE, Makia RS, Oghroro EEA, Owheruo JO, Yousif E, Jikah AN, Akpoghelie PO, Essaghah AEA, Fuwape IA, Umar H, Ahmed DS, Alamiery AA, Said MA.

papers.title: Reprogramming flavonoid glycosylation by bridging advanced biocatalysis and systems synthetic biology.
papers.abstract: Flavonoid glycosides exhibit profound pharmacological and nutritional value, yet their industrial-scale acquisition is severely hampered by low abundance in plant extracts and the stereochemical complexity of chemical synthesis. Synthetic biology offers a sustainable alternative, while the deployment of natural plant uridine diphosphate-dependent glycosyltransferases (UGTs) is intrinsically bottlenecked by low catalytic efficiency, poor stability, and severe intracellular metabolic competition. This review systematically explores the paradigm shifts in the biomanufacturing of these complex molecules, highlighting how the methodological evolution in UGT discovery has evolved from traditional sequence homology to multi-omics and AI-driven predictive models. Multidimensional engineering of UGTs spanning from active-site remodeling to distal allosteric regulation and computational-design is elucidated to precisely manipulate catalytic efficacy, enzyme stability, substrate promiscuity, and catalytic regioselectivity. Bridging the gap between optimized biocatalysts and robust microbial cell factories requires critical systems metabolic engineering strategies, including the rewiring of intracellular UDP-sugar flux, the elimination of catabolic sinks, and the deployment of spatiotemporally decoupled microbial consortia. Cell-free synthesis cascades offer a highly controllable alternative to circumvent in vivo physiological constraints. A strategic roadmap for future research emphasizes AI-driven de novo enzyme design, autonomous single-cell dynamic regulation, and the valorization of lignocellulosic biomass to achieve unprecedented atom economy. Ultimately, this integrated framework provides a scalable, multidimensional blueprint for the sustainable and green biomanufacturing of high-value flavonoid glycosides.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Zhang J, Pan Y, Liu G, Yao Y.

papers.title: SeekRBP: Leveraging Sequence-Structure Integration with Reinforcement Learning for Receptor-Binding Protein Identification.
papers.abstract: Motivation Receptor-binding proteins (RBPs) initiate viral infection and determine host specificity, serving as key targets for phage engineering and therapy. However, the identification of RBPs is complicated by their extreme sequence divergence, which often renders traditional homology-based alignment methods ineffective. While machine learning offers a promising alternative, such approaches struggle with severe class imbalance and the difficulty of selecting informative negative samples from heterogeneous tail proteins. Existing methods often fail to balance learning from these "hard negatives" while maintaining generalization. Results We present SeekRBP, a sequence-structure framework that models negative sampling as a sequential decision-making problem. By employing a multi-armed bandit strategy, SeekRBP dynamically prioritizes informative non-RBP sequences based on real-time training feedback, complemented by a multimodal fusion of protein language and structural embeddings. Benchmarking demonstrates that SeekRBP consistently outperforms static sampling strategies. Furthermore, a case study on Vibrio phages validates that SeekRBP effectively identifies RBPs to improve host prediction, highlighting its potential for large-scale annotation and synthetic biology applications. Availability The source code of SeekRBP is available via: https://github.com/Saillxl/SeekRBP.
papers.authors: Luo X, Ou-Yang L, Shen Y, Guan J, Cai D, Zhang J, Xing G, Sun Y, Shang J.

papers.title: Synthetic biology for sustainable abundance: biomining, electromicrobial production, and hyper-engineerable microbes.
papers.abstract: Over the next few decades, there is a compelling need to build a new sustainable energy infrastructure to replace the fossil fuel system that we have relied on since the 1700s. This infrastructure must not only replace what exists but also far exceed its capabilities, delivering more power to more people to meet the growing demands from both developing and advanced economies. But how do we increase energy use without harming the Earth? Biology drives the Earth's geochemical cycles, operating with far greater elemental and energy fluxes than all of human civilization. This suggests that synthetic biology could solve at least some of our environmental problems while providing access to much greater energy. However, leveraging biology remains a formidable challenge, in part because we do not yet understand nearly enough about the basic science underlying the biological systems that bring the most unusual and useful capabilities to sustainability and energy. This challenge is not unique to biology and sustainability - groundbreaking technologies of the past have required not only curiosity-driven basic research but also use-inspired basic research. Over the past decade, our lab has discovered new basic science needed to build synthetic biology technologies and established itself as a leader in sustainability and synthetic biology. This review summarizes breakthroughs from our lab over the past decade in three key areas: biomining, electrically driven metabolism, and hyper-engineerable microbes.
papers.authors: Vengerova G, Barstow B.

papers.title: Synthetic Biology-Based Biomanufacturing: Current Status and Future Prospects.
papers.abstract: Biomanufacturing, which utilizes biological systems to produce chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and materials, has undergone transformative changes in recent decades, evolving from traditional genetic engineering-based production systems to new platforms based on synthetic biology. This chapter provides an in-depth overview of the development of biomanufacturing under the influence of synthetic biology and discusses various tools and strategies of artificial intelligence for pathway design, construction, and optimization, which play a crucial role in overcoming the limitations of traditional methods. However, data barriers, insufficient model interpretability, and generalizability challenges remain the current major bottlenecks. In the future, with interdisciplinary integration and technological iteration, synthetic biology will drive the evolution of biomanufacturing towards a sustainable bioeconomy, ultimately forming a new paradigm of green and low-carbon industrial production.
papers.authors: Yao TT, Li HM, Zhong JJ, Tang YJ.

papers.title: The road ahead for stem cell therapies in type 1 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Aims Type 1 diabetes results from autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells. Although exogenous insulin remains the standard treatment, it does not restore physiological glucose regulation. Differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells into β-cells offers a scalable alternative to cadaveric islet transplantation and has progressed rapidly over the past decade, resulting in nine clinical trials at various stages of completion. Despite this progress, durable graft function remains constrained by two major challenges: the absence of key islet microenvironment components, such as vasculature, extracellular matrix and supporting cell types and continued vulnerability to autoimmune and alloimmune rejection. Methods & results This review considers emerging technological approaches to overcome these barriers. Bioengineered niches, including multilineage organoids, functionalized hydrogels, decellularized matrices and bioprinting, aim to recreate the native islet microenvironment, while synthetic biology approaches, such as hypoimmune gene editing, CRISPR-based transcriptional control and stimulus-responsive survival circuits, seek to enhance grafts' resilience. Computational and single-cell approaches, including gene regulatory network analysis and digital twin frameworks, are beginning to provide predictive tools for benchmarking differentiation quality and forecasting graft outcomes. Conclusion Together, these complementary strategies, potentially tailored to individual patients, represent a realistic path towards safer, more effective and durable β-cell replacement therapies for type 1 diabetes.
papers.authors: Gasa R, Sancho R, Spagnoli FM.
papers.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

papers.title: Upgrading yeast-based low-carbon biomanufacturing by harnessing a universal in vivo evolution system.
papers.abstract: Non-conventional yeasts are emerging as key cell factories in low-carbon biomanufacturing, but unlocking their full potential requires optimizing complex traits, such as substrate utilization and high-level protein expression, through in vivo genome-wide evolution. To address this, we developed a universal plasmid vector deploying a DNA Helicase-Activation-Induced Cytidine Deaminase (Helicase-AID) for genome-wide base editing. This system enables cross-species mutagenesis in diverse yeasts, including Yarrowia lipolytica, Pichia pastoris, and Kluyveromyces marxianus. We demonstrated that MCM5-AID base editing efficiency in Y. lipolytica is time-dependent, achieving a cumulative mutation rate of 3.13 × 10 -5 mutations per base pair (bp -1 ) over 432 h. Using this system, we evolved Y. lipolytica variants exhibiting a 37.77% increase in maximum specific growth rate on acetate, alongside altered starch production ranging from -92.96% to 17.45%. Crucially, we utilized this platform to activate the silent expression of heterologous proteins, overcoming a persistent bottleneck in microbial strain engineering. Evolutionary, transcriptomic and genomic analyses showed that evolved Y. lipolytica variants exhibited enhanced accumulation of Cas13x, a naturally difficult-to-express protein, via reduced proteolytic degradation. In contrast, evolved P. pastoris variants gained the ability to express previously silent thaumatin through significant transcriptional upregulation, enhanced protein folding, and increased amino acid biosynthesis. Ultimately, this universal in vivo evolution system provides a robust platform for genome-directed evolution across diverse industrial yeast species, accelerating the systematic exploration of their potential in low-carbon biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: Duan S, Shi Z, Wang X, Rong W, Peng G, Yun L, Liang S, Chen Q, Xiao A, Liu S, He H, Abuhena MD, Liu W, Ma H, Lin Y, Liao X, Wang G.

papers.title: A review of the inhibitory waste metabolites produced during mAb biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell culture underpins commercial manufacturing of most therapeutic monoclonal antibodies, yet productivity and product quality remain constrained by inhibitory metabolic by-products that accumulate across batch, fed-batch, and perfusion processes. While lactate and ammonium have historically dominated monitoring and control strategies, untargeted metabolomics and stable-isotope tracing have substantially expanded the inventory of bioprocess-relevant inhibitors. This review synthesizes current understanding of 17 inhibitory metabolites spanning eight metabolic pathways. These include branched-chain amino acid catabolites (isobutyrate, isovalerate, and 2-hydroxyisocaproate), aromatic amino acid derivatives (phenyllactate, indole-3-carboxylate), nucleotide-pathway by-products (cytidine monophosphate, guanosine monophosphate, and succinyladenosine), and apoptosis-correlated species such as glycerol-3-phosphocholine and oxidized glutathione. Reported concentration thresholds are compiled for better-studied inhibitors, while correlative evidence linking accumulation to apoptosis, reduced productivity, and altered glycosylation is summarized. We evaluate the analytical workflow combining LC-MS and NMR for discovery, Raman spectroscopy for in-line monitoring, and stable-isotope tracing for pathway validation. Control strategies are critically compared across three tiers: media and feed reformulation (amino acid limitation, dynamic pH, or oxygen-uptake-rate-driven feeding), targeted and multiplex genetic engineering (BCAT1 knockout, combined LDHA/PDK editing), and keto-acid precursor substitution. We close by identifying concrete gaps, chiefly the absence of cell-line-independent inhibition thresholds, and argue that coupling genome-scale metabolic models with PAT data is the logical next step toward predictive, closed-loop mAb manufacturing.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Morris C, Hoang D, Xu J, Borys MC, Yoon S.

papers.title: Bioinspired dynamic self-assembling condensates driven by liquid-liquid phase separation for therapeutic system innovation and applications: A review.
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), a key biophysical phenomenon in cellular physiology and pathology, profoundly influences cellular homeostasis and disease progression. Notably, the development of biomimetic intervention strategies based on LLPS principles has emerged as a frontier in disease therapy. This review systematically elucidated the molecular basis and regulatory networks of LLPS, with particular emphasis on its emerging applications in therapeutic development: (1) precise interventions targeting the dynamic properties of pathogenic condensates, offering breakthrough tools for tackling refractory diseases; (2) construction of next-generation responsive delivery platforms by harnessing phase transition and dynamic assembly properties, enabling spatiotemporally precise treatment; and (3) LLPS-powered intelligent biomimetic artificial cells, expanding the boundaries of synthetic biology. We further provided an in-depth analysis of urgent challenges, including decoding of LLPS core mechanisms, the difficulty in selectively distinguishing pathological from physiological condensates, the bottleneck of precise controllability in delivery systems, limited in vivo stability and immunogenicity data of LLPS-based delivery systems, and challenges in engineering controllability and large-scale production. Finally, we outlined potential future research directions, suggesting that integrating LLPS studies with multidisciplinary approaches could provide new strategies and technical support to address these challenges.
papers.authors: Li M, Sun J, Wang H, Zhao B, Zhang Y, Lv J, Zhou H, Shi S, Zhang W, An J, Wu Z, Li S.

papers.title: Choice of annotation data significantly impacts automated reconstruction of genome-scale metabolic networks
papers.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models are valuable tools for studying metabolism in many applications, such as metabolic engineering or understanding human disease. However, curated models are available for only a limited number of organisms, and generating high-quality models for additional organisms remains a challenge. To help address this challenge, several software tools have been developed that can produce draft models in an automated fashion, but the quality of these draft models lags behind manually curated ones. Thus, there is still a need to improve these tools. Previous work has focused primarily on developing better methods for each step in the reconstruction process, such as gene annotation and gap-filling. Here, we focus on the data that underlies these methods, such as known connections between protein sequence and function. We find that changing the source of reconstruction data has a substantial impact on the contents and predictions of generated models. In fact, the source of data can have a bigger impact than the choice of reconstruction method. Additionally, we show that the reconstruction process is sensitive to the accuracy of gene annotations in the reconstruction data. Finally, we demonstrate the importance of having functional annotation data from an organism that is closely related to the one for which a model is being built. These observations highlight the importance of reconstruction data and identify principles that should be considered when selecting data for reconstruction tools. Author Summary Genome-scale metabolic models are helpful tools for studying the chemical reactions that take place inside of cells. Unfortunately, building these models is challenging. Past efforts have produced software tools that can build metabolic models in an automated fashion; however, the quality of models produced by these tools is still lower than manually curated models. Rather than focusing on the algorithms or methods in these tools, we instead explore the importance of the data that these tools rely on, which we call “reconstruction data”. We show that building models with different reconstruction data can have a bigger impact on the quality of the models than using a different method. Additionally, we demonstrate that the quality of generated models is sensitive to both the accuracy of the data and the organisms that are represented in the data. These results emphasize the importance of reconstruction data and indicate that focusing more attention on reconstruction data has the potential to substantially improve the quality of automated network reconstruction.
papers.authors: Bates BA, Papin JA.
papers.status: 预印本 · 未经同行评审

papers.title: CRISPR-Based Metabolic Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Sustainable Bio manufacturing: A Systematic analysis of 1,000 Studies (2012–2026)
papers.abstract: Abstract CRISPR genome editing and microbial metabolic engineering now work hand in hand. That pairing has changed sustainable bio manufacturing in real ways. This review pulls together 1,000 peer-reviewed articles from 2012 to 2026. They come from 201 journals. We mapped how the field evolved, how the technology diversified, which host chassis researchers prefer, what product classes they target, and where in the world the work gets done. Our approach mixed bibliometric, feature engineering, and multivariate statistics. That includes principal component analysis, hierarchical clustering, co-occurrence network analysis, and correlation mapping. We tracked the CRISPR variant landscape, host chassis distribution, product class priorities, and geographic concentration of research output. The temporal analysis shows a shift. Early work explored many CRISPR variants. Recent work focuses on applications. Mean CRISPR variants per article dropped from 2.42 in 2018 to 1.40 in 2026. Our findings give a quantitative roadmap of where the field is heading. They also point to emerging opportunities in non-conventional yeast, filamentous fungi, and cyanobacterial chassis for sustainable bio manufacturing.
papers.authors: Zeeshan N, Afzal T, Ahmed Z, Abid I.
papers.status: 预印本 · 未经同行评审

papers.title: Modulation of the general stress response impacts protein expression, energy economy, and heterogeneity in virtually non-dividing yeast cultures.
papers.abstract: Microbial cells adapt their physiology when growth is restricted by nutrient limitation, balancing survival with the capacity to produce proteins. Here, we investigated this adaptation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by comparing retentostat cultures, in which specific growth rates reached below 0.001 h⁻¹, of a reference strain (ScNTi001) and a ∆ msn2 ∆ msn4 mutant (ScNTm001). We show that general stress-response transcription factors Msn2 and Msn4 are crucial for maintaining energy efficiency and for survival under this extreme calorie restriction. Their absence increased population heterogeneity and reduced viability, underscoring a role beyond merely stress resistance. To understand (heterologous) protein expression dynamics, we monitored how a stress-inducible promoter (P HSP12 ) and a constitutive promoter (P TEF1 ) impacted protein levels. The P HSP12 remained active at moderate to low growth rates, but expression sharply dropped below 0.001 h⁻¹, whereas the P TEF1 sustained protein expression, with activity linked to specific glucose uptake rates rather than growth rate. This decoupling revealed a trade-off: although P TEF1 -driven ymNeongreen-specific production rates were 70% higher in the absence of ∆ msn2 ∆ msn4 , overall product yields were 13% lower. Importance This study demonstrates how Msn2 and Msn4 govern cellular robustness under extreme nutrient-limited conditions at near-zero growth rates. It also guides promoter selection strategies for growth-independent production processes. More broadly, this study shows that retentostats can be used as a valuable tool to dissect stress-response pathways, survival mechanisms, and growth-independent expression systems in microbial cell factories.
papers.authors: Temelli N, Raats SAC, Lucheti PR, Weusthuis RA, Bisschops MMM.

papers.title: Reading and rewiring natural-product biosynthesis in microbial hosts with genetically encoded biosensors.
papers.abstract: Covering: 2000 to 2026Natural products (NPs) are structurally diverse bioactive molecules with broad applications in pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and other high-value sectors. Microbial cell factories provide programmable platforms for NP production, but their performance is often constrained by dynamic bottlenecks that are not readily inferred from end-point titers, including limited precursor or cofactor supply, toxic intermediate accumulation, inefficient heterologous enzyme function, and competition with host metabolism. Genetically encoded biosensors translate NP molecules, pathway-relevant metabolites, or cellular states into measurable, selectable, or regulatory outputs. Here, we critically examine biosensor design principles and distinguish the variable detected, recognition modality, output, and implementation format. We then assess how direct product sensing, pathway-state monitoring, dynamic regulation, enzyme screening, genome-wide perturbation, and growth-coupled evolution can support microbial NP engineering. Emphasis is placed on the correspondence between sensor output and the intended engineering objective. This framework clarifies when biosensors can provide actionable information for rewiring NP-producing microbial hosts.
papers.authors: Ki M, Eun H, Park J, Prabowo CPS, Kim D, Lee SY.

papers.title: Reduced methoxine formation by a sulfhydrylase variant identified through adaptive laboratory evolution of engineered Methylorubrum extorquens.
papers.abstract: Streamlining metabolic pathways in microbes is a key strategy in metabolic engineering, often intended to channel evolution toward predictable outcomes. Here, Methylorubrum extorquens PA1 was rationally engineered by deleting redundant formate dehydrogenase operons (fdh234) to focus adaptive laboratory evolution on the remaining formate oxidation step under methanol stress. Genome sequencing identified a MetY-1 Y57D substitution in all five endpoint isolates from one evolving population, while the retained formate dehydrogenase operon carried no detected mutation. In vitro biochemical assays with purified MetY-1 showed that Y57D shifted the methoxine dose-response relative to the wild-type enzyme; at 5% (v/v) methanol the wild-type enzyme accumulated 0.386 ± 0.085 µM methoxine, whereas methoxine remained below the 0.025 µM detection limit for Y57D. A homocysteine-equivalent thiol signal, measured with Ellman reagent, remained detectable for both enzymes under the tested conditions. These results support a fine-tuning model for the product specificity of MetY-1 under methanol. The findings identify this specificity as a candidate point at which methanol toxicity may be mitigated; the contribution of the Y57D substitution to cellular growth was not tested here.
papers.authors: Lee GM, Song DU, Ryu H, Kim J, Park S, Lee H, Kim D.

papers.title: Senescence-targeted engineered CAR-T immunotherapy: advances, challenges and perspectives for engineered senolytic immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence acts as a core driver of chronic diseases and tissue degeneration. Conventional small-molecule senolytics face critical limitations including poor target specificity and off-target toxicity when eliminating heterogeneous senescent cell populations. This review systematically discusses senescence-targeted engineered chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T immunotherapy, which achieves targeted clearance of pathological senescent cells by recognising specific surface markers. It summarises target-antigen evaluation frameworks, analyzes aged immunosuppressive microenvironment barriers and corresponding engineering strategies, and outlines composite efficacy assessment systems and tiered biomarker-monitoring workflows. Key translational bottlenecks such as imperfect antigen specificity and immune escape are also addressed. Preclinical studies verify organ function restoration and healthspan extension, while clinical evidence remains limited. Future integration of CAR-T technology with smart nanocarriers, synthetic biology and artificial intelligence will promote its clinical translation for senescence-associated disorders.
papers.authors: Liu J, Shao W, Ye Q.

papers.title: Targeted Deletions Uncover Previously Uncharacterised C 1 -fixing Cluster Genes as Essential for Autotrophy in Clostridium autoethanogenum
papers.abstract: Recycling carbon oxides from industrial off-gases and gasified organic waste using gas fermentation offers a sustainable route for biomanufacturing of fuels and chemicals. Acetogens are attractive biocatalysts here and fix CO and CO 2 via the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway (WLP). However, the incomplete functional annotation of the associated C 1 -fixing gene cluster limits rational engineering of acetogen cell factories. Here, we investigated five highly conserved but previously uncharacterised C 1 -fixing cluster genes to quantify their contributions to the growth of the model-acetogen Clostridium autoethanogenum using targeted CRISPR/Cas9-mediated single-gene deletions, physiological characterisation, comparative computational structural analyses, CRISPRi, and functional genomics. Importantly, we identified acsV , lpdA , cooC, and cooC2 as essential for autotrophy but not heterotrophy, whereas deletion of gcvH reduced autotrophic growth and shifted carbon flux from acetate towards 2,3-butanediol. Amino acid supplementation experiments and computational analyses indicate that lpdA and gcvH do not primarily function in glycine or serine biosynthesis but instead fulfil specialised roles in WLP-associated C 1 and redox metabolism. Furthermore, genetic and physiological analyses showed that the two CooC-family ATPases, CooC and CooC2, have non-redundant roles in growth, with only cooC2 deletion impairing heterotrophy. Acetate supplementation tests revealed that Δ acsV cells retained metabolic activity despite abolished autotrophy, and computational analyses suggest a likely role for acsV in ATP-dependent corrinoid activation. Surprisingly, CRISPRi-mediated repression of acsV was translationally buffered, resulting in altered carbon partitioning without impairing autotrophy. Together, our findings provide insights into the physiological importance of the C 1 -fixing cluster genes in acetogens and support their metabolic engineering as gas-fermenting cell factories.
papers.authors: Nwaokorie UJ, Vorontsova M, Shaikh KM, Reinmets K, Valgepea K.

papers.title: The synthetic biology frontier: engineered oncolytic viruses and viral vectors for next-generation cancer therapy and gene delivery.
papers.abstract: Viruses are no longer used merely as naturally occurring tools for gene transfer or as blunt cytolytic agents. Researchers are rewriting their genomes, capsids, tropisms, regulatory elements, and payloads to create therapeutic systems that sense disease, execute conditional programs, and remodel pathological tissue. In oncology, engineered oncolytic viruses (OVs) can combine tumor-selective replication with immunogenic cell death, antigen release, and local immune stimulation. In parallel, viral-vector engineering, particularly AAV and LVs, is addressing central limitations of gene delivery: the prevalence of pre-existing neutralizing antibodies, the difficulty of systemic administration and repeat dosing (AAV), and the manufacturing bottleneck of ex vivo cell therapies (LV). The clinical record is encouraging but uneven: T-VEC has shown that an engineered herpes simplex virus can improve durable responses in selected melanoma lesions, while G47Δ/teserpaturev and newer armed HSV platforms provide evidence of feasibility, safety, and occasional durable responses in difficult solid tumors. Lentiviral vector-based in vivo CAR-T cell generation, exemplified by KLN-1010/inMMyCAR and related first-in-human programs, signals a paradigm shift away from ex vivo manufacturing. However, the broader field has not converted its large preclinical literature into a proportional number of clinically meaningful, systemically deployable medicines. The main bottlenecks remain delivery, tumor heterogeneity, immune clearance, suboptimal pharmacodynamic biomarkers, manufacturing complexity, resistance, and the difficulty of proving benefit for products with delayed or immunologically mediated effects. This review examines the synthetic biology toolkit for programmable viral therapeutics through a unified engineering framework that integrates OVs, AAV, and LVs by design principle rather than by vector class. We discuss tumor-selective promoters, microRNA detargeting, retargeted capsids and ligands, attenuation, genome-scale assembly, immune-stimulatory payloads, bispecific and trispecific engagers, logic-gated circuits, safety switches, serodivergent AAV capsids, biomimetic cloaking, cell carriers, biomaterial delivery systems, and in vivo CAR-T generation. Our central thesis is that the next generation of viral medicines will be selected not by the most elaborate genome, but by the most coherent alignment of five measurable success factors: tumor selectivity, immune remodeling, delivery and biodistribution, controllable safety, and manufacturability. The emerging paradigm is therefore programmable viral therapeutics: context-sensitive biological medicines designed to operate within the constraints of human tumors and human immunity.
papers.authors: Alsharedeh RH, Aljabali AAA, Obeid MA, Alqudah A, Gammoh O, Qnais E, Mishra V, Mishra Y, El-Tanani M.

papers.title: Biotechnology has outgrown the organism.
papers.abstract: Synthetic biology increasingly produces hybrid constructs that blur the boundaries of organism-based biosafety regulation. We propose using the term 'biological entity', defined by its capacity to interact meaningfully with biological systems or to facilitate biological processes, as an initial screening category before regulatory classification, enabling more coherent and proportionate oversight.
papers.authors: Bouchaut B, Asveld L.

enrichment.titleZh: 生物技术已超越“生物体”的范畴
enrichment.abstractZh: 合成生物学日益产生各种混合构建体，使以生物体为基础的生物安全监管边界变得模糊。我们提出使用“生物实体”这一术语，以其能否与生物系统发生有意义的相互作用，或促进生物过程为定义依据；在确定监管分类之前，将其作为初步筛选类别，从而实现更加协调且适度的监管。

papers.title: Harnessing plant redox networks and bacterial modulation for next-generation abiotic stress resilience in crops.
papers.abstract: Abiotic stresses such as drought, salinity, heavy metals, heat, and cold disrupt cellular redox homeostasis, resulting in the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and oxidative damage that negatively affect plant growth and productivity. Under controlled conditions, lower level of ROS act as signaling molecule, whereas, at elevated levels with biotic and abiotic stress factors, causes cellular damage. This review critically examines the molecular mechanisms involved in redox homeostasis in plants, including both enzymatic and non-enzymatic antioxidant systems. The integrated roles of phytohormone signaling and plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB) in regulating ROS metabolism, boosting antioxidant capacity, and enhancing abiotic stress tolerance are further discussed. Mechanistic insights into plant stress adaptation are provided by evaluating recent advances in transcriptional regulation, epigenetic modification, and redox-associated regulatory networks. Moreover, we review the contributions of multi-omics approaches toward understanding redox regulation and identifying key molecular components involved in stress resilience. Finally, emerging applications of synthetic biology and artificial intelligence are explored as potential tools for engineering redox regulatory networks to accelerate the development of climate-resilient crops. Overall, this review provides an integrated mechanistic framework outlining how redox biology, PGPB interactions, and next-generation engineering strategies can be combined to enhance crop resilience and sustainable agricultural productivity under future environmental shifts.
papers.authors: Sarkar RK, Bhattacharyya A, Sarkar S, Pramanik B, Dutta S, Debnath S, Paul A, Bhattacharya K, Upadhyay SK, Rani A, Koolman L, Panneerselvam P, Santoyo G, Mitra D.

papers.title: Biomimetic Nanosystems as Emerging Catalysts for Translational Innovation in Healthcare.
papers.abstract: Biomimetic nanosystems are engineered platforms at the nanoscale range that emulate selected structural and compositional features to reproduce their advantageous interactions with the complex biological environments. These systems, inspired by the biological cell membrane(s), have emerged as a promising technology with a variety of biomedical applications. However, they are still in their early stage of clinical development. Biomimetic nanosystems may be produced by incorporating the desired nanoparticles into synthesized membrane(s). Such nanosystems exhibit greater immunocompatibility, immune evasion, and extended circulation times. Therefore, this study examines the latest advancements in the design and engineering of biomimetic nanosystems, focusing on membrane insertion/integration, hybridization, surface functionalization and modification, and metabolic engineering that could enhance the multifunctionality, hybrid membrane engineering, stimulus-responsive behavior, and scalability of these systems. The unique characteristics of these nanosystems have been investigated and applied in various fields, including medicine delivery, vaccine research, antidote(s) manufacturing, imaging, and sensing, which are critically discussed. Furthermore, this review has summarized the practical challenges related to translation, such as stability, reproducibility, functionality, regulatory complexity, and efficacy. This review also highlights both the opportunities and limitations of these emerging platforms and outlines key directions for the development of clinically relevant nanomedicine. As a result, this study serves as the foundation for future research into the multifunctional nanobiomimetic system.
papers.authors: Singhal S, Mandal S, Gupta A.

enrichment.titleZh: 仿生纳米系统：推动医疗健康转化创新的新兴力量
enrichment.abstractZh: 仿生纳米系统是纳米尺度的工程化平台，通过模拟特定的结构和组成特征，重现其与复杂生物环境之间的有利相互作用。这些受生物细胞膜启发的系统已成为一种具有多种生物医学应用前景的技术，但仍处于临床开发的早期阶段。仿生纳米系统可通过将所需的纳米颗粒整合入合成膜而制备。这类系统表现出更高的免疫相容性、更强的免疫逃逸能力以及更长的循环时间。因此，本研究考察了仿生纳米系统设计与工程化的最新进展，重点关注膜插入与整合、杂合化、表面功能化与修饰，以及代谢工程；这些策略有望增强系统的多功能性，改进杂合膜工程，并提高刺激响应性和可规模化能力。这些纳米系统的独特特征已在药物递送、疫苗研究、解毒剂制造、成像和传感等多个领域得到研究与应用，本文对这些应用进行了批判性讨论。此外，本综述总结了转化过程中面临的实际挑战，包括稳定性、可重复性、功能性、监管复杂性和有效性。综述还强调了这些新兴平台的机遇与局限，并概述了开发具有临床应用意义的纳米药物的关键方向。因此，本研究为未来开展多功能纳米仿生系统研究提供了基础。

papers.title: Decoupled electro-biosynthesis of high-value bioproducts from CO 2 and N 2 .
papers.abstract: The conversion of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and nitrogen (N 2 ) into high-value bioproducts offers a promising pathway for sustainable chemistry, food, and material production. However, existing approaches remain constrained by narrow product scopes, inefficient biological fixation, and poor scalability. Here, we present a spatially decoupled electro-biosystem that converts CO 2 and N 2 into poly-γ-glutamic acid (γ-PGA), while co-generating microbial biomass with cell-protein valorization potential. A Cu-N 2 single-atom catalyst and plasma processes generate methane and nitrate from CO 2 and N 2 , providing highly reduced carbon and oxidized nitrogen sources. The engineered methanotrophs heterologously expressing γ-PGA biosynthesis genes were designed to convert methane and nitrate into γ-PGA with a molecular weight of up to 700 kDa. Systematic optimization of carbon, nitrogen, and energy fluxes boosted γ-PGA titer by 125% to 142.84 mg L -1 in a 30 L bioreactor, accompanied by 9.47 g L -1 of cell protein. Importantly, the modular design allows the outputs of the electrocatalytic and plasma-assisted units to be adjusted according to the measured carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen demands of the biological module, thereby supporting supply-demand matching across the spatially decoupled system. Techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment identify key determinants of process economics and indicate the potential environmental benefits of the electro-biosystem, respectively. This study demonstrates a decoupled platform for high-value bioproduct production, providing a modular basis for process scale-up and advancing customizable, air-derived biomanufacturing from CO 2 and N 2 .
papers.authors: Hou Q, Dai Y, Zhang C, Gao Z, Guo S, Li C, Zheng T, Huang X, Xia C, Fei Q.

papers.title: kinGEMs: A robust and scalable framework for resource-constraint models through stochastic tuning of deep learning-predicted kinetic parameters.
papers.abstract: The construction of accurate enzyme-constrained genome-scale models (ecGEMs) remains a critical challenge in systems biology, limited by sparse kinetic data and the need for biologically meaningful representations. This work presents an integrated framework combining CPI-Pred, a deep learning model to predict kinetic parameters (kcat) from sequence and compound embeddings, with kinGEMs, a pipeline to incorporate these uncertainty-aware parameters into ecGEMs for metabolic optimization. By leveraging representations at multiple scales, the approach captures sequence, structure, and kinetic data to enhance model generalizability and accuracy. Rigorous benchmarking demonstrates the framework's capability to predict growth rates and fluxes that are consistent with experimental observations and measured proteome fractions, reduce median flux variability by several folds, and yield better-constrained metabolic models by explicitly accounting for the uncertainty inherent in ML-predicted kinetic parameters. kinGEMs successfully generated ecGEMs for 93 models spanning a phylogenetically diverse set of organisms including Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, mycobacteria, parasitic protists, fungi, and mammalian cell lines. These innovations breakdown the barrier to application of ecGEMs to non-model organisms and open new avenues for metabolic engineering and synthetic biology in more industrially relevant hosts.
papers.authors: A Barghout R, Chiñas Serrano L, Sanchez-Lengeling B, Mahadevan R.

enrichment.titleZh: kinGEMs：通过随机调优深度学习预测的动力学参数，构建稳健且可扩展的资源约束模型框架
enrichment.abstractZh: 准确构建酶约束的基因组尺度模型（ecGEMs）仍是系统生物学的一项关键挑战，主要受限于动力学数据稀缺，以及模型表征需要具备生物学意义。本研究提出一个整合框架，将CPI-Pred与kinGEMs相结合：CPI-Pred是一种根据序列和化合物的嵌入表示预测动力学参数（kcat）的深度学习模型；kinGEMs则是一套将这些考虑了不确定性的参数整合进ecGEMs、用于代谢优化的流程。该方法利用多个尺度的表征，整合序列、结构和动力学数据，提高模型的泛化能力与准确性。严格的基准测试表明，该框架能够预测与实验观察结果及实测蛋白质组比例一致的生长速率和通量，使通量变异范围的中位数降低数倍，并通过显式考虑机器学习预测动力学参数所固有的不确定性，获得约束更充分的代谢模型。kinGEMs成功为93个模型生成了ecGEMs，覆盖系统发育多样性广泛的生物，包括革兰氏阴性菌和革兰氏阳性菌、分枝杆菌、寄生原生生物、真菌及哺乳动物细胞系。这些创新降低了将ecGEMs应用于非模式生物的障碍，并为在工业相关性更高的宿主中开展代谢工程与合成生物学研究开辟了新途径。

papers.title: L-Threonine production from acetate by metabolically engineered Corynebacterium glutamicum using a pH-controlled fed-batch process.
papers.abstract: Acetate has a considerable potential as a non-food feedstock for microbial bioproduction, yet its use for amino acid production remains underexplored. Here, we developed a process for L-threonine production from acetate as the sole carbon source with Corynebacterium glutamicum by integrating rational, genome-based metabolic engineering with pH-coupled fed-batch cultivation. The engineered strain AT-3 carried five chromosomal mutations that alleviated feedback inhibition of key enzymes and redirected carbon flux toward the aspartate pathway. Substrate supply was controlled using a custom Visual Basic-based feeding script that automatically adjusted the acetic acid feed in response to online pH measurements. Robust process performance was maintained during a tenfold scale-up from 100-mL DASbox to 1-L DASGIP bioreactors. The optimized process achieved an L-threonine titer of 10.04 g/L and a yield of 0.086 g/g acetate. This study provides a basis for further studies on the development and improvement of acetate-based amino acid production process. KEY POINTS: • Plasmid-free C. glutamicum strains produce L-threonine in acetate minimal medium • pH-controlled acetic acid feed in bioreactors improved L-threonine production • Acetate-based production of feed amino acids avoids competition with human food.
papers.authors: Broschard P, Endt N, Wirtz A, Glitz C, Baumgart M, Bott M.

enrichment.titleZh: 采用pH控制的补料分批工艺，利用代谢工程改造的谷氨酸棒杆菌以乙酸盐生产L-苏氨酸
enrichment.abstractZh: 乙酸盐作为微生物生物生产的非粮原料具有很大潜力，但其在氨基酸生产中的应用仍缺乏充分探索。本研究将基于基因组的理性代谢工程与pH耦合的补料分批培养相结合，开发了利用谷氨酸棒杆菌、以乙酸盐为唯一碳源生产L-苏氨酸的工艺。工程菌株AT-3携带5处染色体突变，缓解了关键酶的反馈抑制，并将碳通量引向天冬氨酸途径。研究者利用以Visual Basic编写的定制补料脚本控制底物供应，根据在线pH测量结果自动调整乙酸补料。从100 mL DASbox生物反应器放大至1 L DASGIP生物反应器、规模扩大10倍后，工艺仍保持稳定表现。优化后的工艺实现了10.04 g/L的L-苏氨酸滴度，得率为0.086 g/g乙酸盐。本研究为进一步开发和改进以乙酸盐为原料的氨基酸生产工艺提供了基础。要点：①无质粒的谷氨酸棒杆菌菌株可在乙酸盐最小培养基中生产L-苏氨酸；②在生物反应器中通过pH控制乙酸补料，提高了L-苏氨酸产量；③以乙酸盐生产饲用氨基酸可避免与人类食物竞争原料。

papers.title: Physiological, behavioral, and genetic factors that shape interactions in the plant growth-promoting maize rhizosphere synthetic community.
papers.abstract: Profiling microbiomes is an important way to understand the function and composition of communities in the wild, but natural microbiomes are often highly complex and often unamenable to experimentation to reveal cause-and-effect relationships. By using a small group of cultivable strains to represent those found in the wild, synthetic communities are one solution to this problem. Here we describe the ma ize r hizosphere s ynthetic c ommunity (MARSc), a genome-enabled 31-member bacterial community representative of the diversity found on the roots of maize grown in Iowa soils. This community is built around Pseudomonas putida KT2440, a model maize rhizosphere colonist and synthetic biology chassis. We characterized microbe-microbe interactions and biofilm formation of MARSc members in a variety of environmental contexts, finding that both behaviors are broadly controlled by nutrient levels. Genomic analysis and microbiome profiling of these organisms revealed that annotated biofilm genes (such as surface attachment and exopolysaccharide production) were significantly correlated with rhizosphere abundance, but neither trait correlated to in vitro biofilm formation. In vitro interaction assay findings were surprisingly consistent with co-correlations of rhizosphere abundance among MARSc members on roots. Finally, we found that when applied to the roots, MARSc can increase maize biomass (dry weight) by up to 40%-50% under varying nitrogen fertilization levels. Altogether, MARSc is a useful tool for identifying some of the factors influencing rhizosphere microbiome assembly and will be a strong foundation for further work in this area.IMPORTANCEThe microbiome surrounding the roots of plants can play an integral role in plant health and growth, and it is composed of thousands of species of microbes that are specific to the plant and environment it is grown in. However, due to this complexity, little is known about the means by which microbiomes form. In this study, we developed the maize rhizosphere synthetic community (MARSc) to gain a better understanding of the formation and function of microbiomes on the roots of plants. This consortium consists of 30 bacterial isolates plus Pseudomonas putida KT2440, a model maize root colonist. In this study, we investigated the interactions between these organisms, their genomes, cultural characteristics, and growth on the roots of maize. We show that MARSc increases maize growth under low nitrogen fertilizer, suggesting it will be a useful tool for identifying the mechanisms behind microbiome formation and plant growth promotion.
papers.authors: Paulsen AA, Roghair Stroud MN, Halverson LJ.

enrichment.titleZh: 塑造促玉米生长根际合成群落中相互作用的生理、行为与遗传因素
enrichment.abstractZh:
对微生物组进行分析，是了解自然环境中群落功能与组成的重要方式。然而，天然微生物组通常高度复杂，往往难以通过实验揭示因果关系。用少量可培养菌株代表自然环境中存在的菌株，构建合成群落，是解决这一问题的一种方法。本文介绍玉米根际合成群落（MARSc）：这是一个由基因组信息支持、包含31个细菌成员的群落，可代表在美国爱荷华州土壤中生长的玉米根部所发现的微生物多样性。该群落围绕恶臭假单胞菌（Pseudomonas putida）KT2440构建；这一菌株是研究玉米根际定殖的模式菌，也是合成生物学底盘。我们在多种环境条件下表征了MARSc成员之间的微生物相互作用及其生物膜形成情况，发现这两类行为总体上均受营养水平调控。对这些微生物的基因组分析和微生物组分析显示，经注释的生物膜相关基因（例如与表面附着和胞外多糖生成有关的基因）与根际丰度显著相关，但这两类特征均与体外生物膜形成不相关。体外相互作用实验的结果与根部MARSc成员之间根际丰度的共同相关关系表现出出乎意料的一致性。最后，我们发现，在不同氮肥施用水平下，将MARSc施用于根部，可使玉米生物量（干重）最大提高40%-50%。总体而言，MARSc是识别影响根际微生物组组装的部分因素的一项实用工具，并将为该领域的后续研究提供坚实基础。

研究意义（IMPORTANCE）：植物根部周围的微生物组可在植物健康和生长中发挥重要作用，由数千种具有植物及其生长环境特异性的微生物组成。然而，由于这种复杂性，人们对微生物组形成方式的了解仍然有限。本研究构建了玉米根际合成群落（MARSc），以更好地理解植物根部微生物组的形成与功能。该菌群由30株细菌分离株，以及作为玉米根部定殖模式菌的恶臭假单胞菌KT2440组成。我们研究了这些微生物之间的相互作用、它们的基因组、培养特征，以及它们在玉米根部的生长情况。结果表明，MARSc可在低氮肥条件下促进玉米生长，提示其有望成为识别微生物组形成及植物促生机制的实用工具。
enrichment.sourceTitle: Physiological, behavioral, and genetic factors that shape interactions in the plant growth-promoting maize rhizosphere synthetic community.
enrichment.sourceAbstract: Profiling microbiomes is an important way to understand the function and composition of communities in the wild, but natural microbiomes are often highly complex and often unamenable to experimentation to reveal cause-and-effect relationships. By using a small group of cultivable strains to represent those found in the wild, synthetic communities are one solution to this problem. Here we describe the ma ize r hizosphere s ynthetic c ommunity (MARSc), a genome-enabled 31-member bacterial community representative of the diversity found on the roots of maize grown in Iowa soils. This community is built around Pseudomonas putida KT2440, a model maize rhizosphere colonist and synthetic biology chassis. We characterized microbe-microbe interactions and biofilm formation of MARSc members in a variety of environmental contexts, finding that both behaviors are broadly controlled by nutrient levels. Genomic analysis and microbiome profiling of these organisms revealed that annotated biofilm genes (such as surface attachment and exopolysaccharide production) were significantly correlated with rhizosphere abundance, but neither trait correlated to in vitro biofilm formation. In vitro interaction assay findings were surprisingly consistent with co-correlations of rhizosphere abundance among MARSc members on roots. Finally, we found that when applied to the roots, MARSc can increase maize biomass (dry weight) by up to 40%-50% under varying nitrogen fertilization levels. Altogether, MARSc is a useful tool for identifying some of the factors influencing rhizosphere microbiome assembly and will be a strong foundation for further work in this area.IMPORTANCEThe microbiome surrounding the roots of plants can play an integral role in plant health and growth, and it is composed of thousands of species of microbes that are specific to the plant and environment it is grown in. However, due to this complexity, little is known about the means by which microbiomes form. In this study, we developed the maize rhizosphere synthetic community (MARSc) to gain a better understanding of the formation and function of microbiomes on the roots of plants. This consortium consists of 30 bacterial isolates plus Pseudomonas putida KT2440, a model maize root colonist. In this study, we investigated the interactions between these organisms, their genomes, cultural characteristics, and growth on the roots of maize. We show that MARSc increases maize growth under low nitrogen fertilizer, suggesting it will be a useful tool for identifying the mechanisms behind microbiome formation and plant growth promotion.

papers.title: Spatial control of enzyme orientation at the lipid droplet interface enables regio- and chemoselective metabolic flux.
papers.abstract: Precise spatial control over multienzyme cascade reactions is increasingly recognized as a design lever in synthetic biology for enhancing catalytic performance and directing metabolic flux. By emulating principles of cellular compartmentalization, synthetic scaffolds and engineered interfaces have emerged as powerful platforms to modulate intermediate channeling and reaction efficiency in complex biocatalytic systems. However, robust and spatially defined immobilization of multienzyme assemblies within physicochemically optimal compartments remains challenging because of the dynamic intracellular environment. Here, we reprogram the amphiphilic interface of yeast lipid droplets (LDs) as a programmable scaffold system to support regio- and chemoselective localization of enzymes. Guided by molecular dynamics simulations, we designed LD-anchoring motifs to direct the enzyme orientation at the LD monolayer interface, yielding cytosol-facing or LD inner-facing configurations. Using this designed LD-anchoring motif, we spatially reorganize a trienzyme cascade for prodeoxyviolacein (PDV) biosynthesis across the cytosol-LD interface, facilitating directional conversion of hydrophilic substrates into hydrophobic products. This spatial reorganization substantially improved PDV production by 1300%, achieving 46.25 milligrams per liter. Our approach offers a modular and tunable platform for engineering spatially organized and readily deployable enzyme cascades, opening avenues for biosynthetic catalysis at organellar interfaces.
papers.authors: Son SH, Bae S, Moon SY, Kim M, Oh SS, Son CY, Lee JY.

enrichment.titleZh: 在脂滴界面空间调控酶取向，实现具有区域选择性和化学选择性的代谢通量
enrichment.abstractZh: 对多酶级联反应进行精确的空间调控，正日益被视为合成生物学中提高催化性能和引导代谢通量的一种设计手段。通过模拟细胞区室化原理，合成支架与工程化界面已成为在复杂生物催化体系中调节中间体通道化和反应效率的有力平台。然而，由于细胞内环境具有动态性，要在理化条件最优的区室内稳固且以明确的空间位置固定多酶组装体，仍然具有挑战性。本研究将酵母脂滴（LDs）的两亲性界面改造为可编程支架体系，以支持酶具有区域选择性和化学选择性的定位。在分子动力学模拟的指导下，研究者设计了脂滴锚定基序，以控制酶在脂滴单分子层界面的取向，形成朝向细胞质溶胶或脂滴内部的构型。利用这一设计的脂滴锚定基序，研究者在细胞质溶胶与脂滴的界面两侧，对用于prodeoxyviolacein（PDV）生物合成的三酶级联进行了空间重组，促进亲水底物向疏水产物的定向转化。这种空间重组使PDV产量显著提高了1300%，达到46.25 mg/L。该方法为构建具有空间组织且便于应用的酶级联提供了模块化、可调节的平台，为在细胞器界面开展生物合成催化开辟了方向。

papers.title: A biosynthetic paradox implicating dynamic zeaxanthin biosynthesis at the ER-LD interface.
papers.abstract: Traditional metabolic engineering often treats lipid droplets (LDs) as inert storage sinks and assumes shortening enzyme-substrate distance inherently enhances pathway efficiency. Harnessing Yarrowia lipolytica for zeaxanthin production, we uncovered a pivotal "spatial paradox" challenging this conventional dogma. A selective shielding strategy first identified the hydroxylase Pa CrtZ as the primary biosynthetic bottleneck. Subcellular localization trials revealed that directly targeting Pa CrtZ to the β-carotene-rich LD surface unexpectedly yielded the lowest zeaxanthin relative fraction (9.87%), significantly underperforming compared to cytosolic (27.15%) or peroxisomal targeting (43.16%). To investigate this counterintuitive phenomenon, multidimensional engineering strategies were implemented to boost zeaxanthin accumulation. Subsequently, in situ , label-free stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy unequivocally demonstrated the co-localization of β-carotene and zeaxanthin within LDs, confirming that substrate inaccessibility was not the limiting factor. Guided by principles of LD biogenesis, these findings led us to conceptualize a dynamic endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-LD interface functional microenvironment model. We propose that robust Pa CrtZ-catalyzed hydroxylation is sustained predominantly at transient ER-LD junctions, where hydrophobic β-carotene "skimming" is dynamically synchronized with efficient O 2 and NADPH cofactor exchange. This model redefines lipid organelles as active, organized metabolic hubs beyond mere storage, offering a novel transformative framework for future organelle-targeted metabolic interface design.
papers.authors: Sun L, Zhang J, Abdullah CN, Shen Y, Geng S, Xu S, Zhou J.

papers.title: AI-enhanced CRISPR-Cas9 therapeutics: Advances in precision, safety, and delivery.
papers.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing has transformed biomedical research and is advancing toward clinical translation. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) offers improved precision in guide RNA design, off-target prediction, and delivery optimization. This review synthesizes recent advances in CRISPR-Cas9 for medical applications, covering core mechanisms, engineered variants, base and prime editors, and therapeutic applications including CAR T-cell and CAR-NK engineering, genetic disorders, infectious diseases, and regenerative medicine. Delivery strategies are evaluated with emphasis on AI-driven optimization. AI applications are highlighted across deep learning architectures for guide RNA design, AI-designed nucleases such as OpenCRISPR-1, structure-guided and AI-assisted design of compact high-fidelity SaCas9 variants, reinforcement learning for pipeline optimization, and roles in CAR T-cell therapy and safety assessment. Safety challenges are examined, including off-target effects, chromosomal rearrangements, immunogenicity, and regulatory concerns. Future directions emphasize multi-scale modeling, explainable AI, clinical validation, and integration with synthetic biology, single-cell sequencing, organoids, and nanomaterials. The convergence of AI and CRISPR-Cas9 holds substantial potential for personalized medicine.
papers.authors: Boretti A.
papers.journal: Progress in biophysics and molecular biology

enrichment.titleZh: 人工智能增强的CRISPR-Cas9治疗技术：精准性、安全性与递送的研究进展
enrichment.abstractZh: CRISPR-Cas9基因组编辑已经改变了生物医学研究，并正向临床转化推进。人工智能（AI）的引入有助于提高向导RNA设计、脱靶预测与递送优化的精准性。本综述综合了CRISPR-Cas9医学应用的近期进展，涵盖其核心机制、工程化变体、碱基编辑器与先导编辑器（prime editors），以及嵌合抗原受体T细胞（CAR-T）和嵌合抗原受体自然杀伤细胞（CAR-NK）工程改造、遗传性疾病、感染性疾病及再生医学等治疗应用。文章评估了递送策略，重点关注由AI驱动的优化。所讨论的AI应用包括：用于向导RNA设计的深度学习架构；OpenCRISPR-1等由AI设计的核酸酶；结合结构指导与AI辅助，设计紧凑型、高保真SaCas9变体；利用强化学习优化流程；以及AI在CAR-T细胞治疗和安全性评估中的作用。综述还考察了脱靶效应、染色体重排、免疫原性及监管方面的安全挑战。未来方向重点包括多尺度建模、可解释AI、临床验证，以及与合成生物学、单细胞测序、类器官和纳米材料相结合。AI与CRISPR-Cas9的融合为个体化医疗带来了很大潜力。

papers.title: Bile acid dysmetabolism and microbial dysbiosis coincide with Clostridioides difficile infection in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease.
papers.abstract: Pediatric inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients are at increased risk for Clostridioides difficile infection. This review highlights bile acid dysmetabolism, driven by gut microbiota dysbiosis and reduced microbial production of secondary bile acids, as a key factor linking pediatric IBD to increased CDI susceptibility. We examine interactions among IBD, dysbiosis, bile acid metabolism, and C. difficile , and discuss emerging microbiome-based interventions aimed at restoring bile acid homeostasis.
papers.authors: Rowe JC, Winston JA.

papers.title: Cell culture tightrope: Balancing amino acids and dipeptides to optimize media formulation and biomanufacturing performance.
papers.abstract: High-quality cell culture media remain central to mammalian bioprocessing as industry produces increasingly complex molecules at higher cell densities under intensified processing conditions. Amino acids represent a critical class of media components, serving as building blocks for endogenous and recombinant proteins and also as key regulators of cellular metabolism. This requires delivery of amino acids at concentrations that challenge their stability and solubility limits. This review provides an overview of amino acid roles in cell culture and how to choose their optimal levels in media formulations, with a focus on Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells. Omics-assisted medium development strategies are described to characterize amino acid metabolism and minimize metabolic inefficiencies arising from amino acid degradation. Additionally, genetic engineering approaches aimed at introducing amino acid auxotrophies or removing metabolic bottlenecks are discussed as complementary strategies to improve cell culture performance. Understanding the physicochemical limitations associated with amino acid solubility becomes increasingly important in concentrated media formulations. Emerging in silico thermodynamic models that capture interactions between amino acids and other media components are highlighted as valuable tools for predicting solubility limits and guiding rational media formulation strategies. Dipeptides represent an increasingly attractive alternative to free amino acids due to improved solubility, stability, and process-enhancing properties. Consequently, this review summarizes key dipeptides, current knowledge of their uptake and metabolism, and the amino acid and dipeptide transporters and cleavage enzymes. Finally, the review emphasizes the importance of smart media design by integrating experiments with modeling approaches to enable efficient, robust, and sustainable biomanufacturing processes.
papers.authors: Ladiwala P, Kappel A, Reddy JV, Schoelzel M, Naik HM, Peters J, Dhara VG, Young EM, Antoniewicz MR, Betenbaugh MJ.

enrichment.titleZh: 细胞培养中的精细平衡：调配氨基酸与二肽，优化培养基配方及生物制造性能
enrichment.abstractZh: 随着工业界在强化工艺条件下，以更高细胞密度生产日益复杂的分子，高质量细胞培养基仍然是哺乳动物生物加工的核心。氨基酸是一类关键培养基组分，既是内源蛋白和重组蛋白的构建单元，也是细胞代谢的重要调节因子。因此，氨基酸的供给浓度会对其稳定性和溶解度极限构成挑战。本综述概述氨基酸在细胞培养中的作用，以及如何为培养基配方选择最佳氨基酸水平，重点关注中国仓鼠卵巢（CHO）细胞。文章介绍了组学辅助的培养基开发策略，用于表征氨基酸代谢，并尽量减少由氨基酸降解引起的代谢低效。此外，综述讨论了旨在引入氨基酸营养缺陷或解除代谢瓶颈的遗传工程方法，将其作为改善细胞培养性能的互补策略。在浓缩培养基配方中，理解氨基酸溶解度相关的理化限制变得日益重要。新兴的计算热力学模型能够描述氨基酸与其他培养基组分之间的相互作用，文章强调了其作为预测溶解度极限、指导理性培养基配方设计的有价值工具的作用。由于溶解度、稳定性以及促进工艺表现的性质有所改善，二肽正日益成为颇具吸引力的游离氨基酸替代选择。因此，本综述总结了关键二肽、目前关于其摄取和代谢的认识，以及氨基酸和二肽的转运蛋白与切割酶。最后，综述强调，将实验与建模方法相结合开展智能培养基设计，对于实现高效、稳健且可持续的生物制造过程具有重要意义。

papers.title: Chloroplast genome engineering: Recent advances, pathways towards commercialization and future directions.
papers.abstract: Chloroplasts are ideal biofactories because thousands of transgene copies integrated into each plant cell to produce high levels of recombinant proteins and enzymes. Because chloroplast genomes are predominantly maternally inherited, transgenes are generally not transmitted via pollen. Nuclear genome engineering ushered in the GMO revolution for crop protection that mostly required lower levels of transgene expression. Higher level expression and biosafety through gene containment facilitate new applications of GM crops, including production of high-value biopharmaceuticals and enzymes. This review focuses on recent advances in this field, including the first FDA approval of biopharmaceuticals made in plant cells for evaluation in human clinical trials, topical or oral drug delivery, marker free edible plants by removal of antibiotic resistance genes and novel post-translational modifications required to produce functional human proteins. In addition, new tools are discussed to improve DNA delivery, vector free assembly, episomal or integration methods, enhancement of transgene expression through optimization of regulatory sequences, codons, targeted genome editing and other innovations in biomanufacturing. Topical drug delivery using plant cells incorporated into chewing gums to control oral viruses, pathogenic bacteria, or yeast and oral drug delivery with therapeutic proteins made in plant cells to treat diabetes, obesity and cardiopulmonary diseases currently advanced to human clinical trials are discussed. In addition, high-value industrial enzymes for launching new products or to confer valuable agronomic traits or enhance photosynthesis are discussed. Future perspectives section provides examples of biotechnology products anticipated to be launched in the next 3-5 years, with opportunities and anticipated challenges.
papers.authors: Fatima I, Daniell H.

enrichment.titleZh: 叶绿体基因组工程：近期进展、商业化路径与未来方向
enrichment.abstractZh: 叶绿体是理想的生物工厂，因为每个植物细胞中可整合数千个转基因拷贝，从而高水平生产重组蛋白和酶。由于叶绿体基因组主要通过母系遗传，转基因通常不会经花粉传播。核基因组工程开启了以作物保护为目标的转基因生物（GMO）革命，而这类应用大多只需要较低的转基因表达水平。更高水平的表达，以及通过限制基因扩散而实现的生物安全性，有助于拓展转基因作物的新应用，包括生产高价值生物药和酶。本综述重点介绍该领域的近期进展，包括植物细胞制备的生物药首次获美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）批准开展人体临床试验评估、局部或口服给药、通过去除抗生素抗性基因获得不含筛选标记的可食用植物，以及产生有功能的人源蛋白所需的新型翻译后修饰。此外，文章讨论了改善DNA递送、无载体组装、游离型或整合型方法的新工具，通过优化调控序列和密码子增强转基因表达的方法、靶向基因组编辑，以及生物制造中的其他创新。文中还讨论了利用含植物细胞的口香糖进行局部给药、以控制口腔病毒、致病细菌或酵母，以及使用植物细胞制得的治疗性蛋白进行口服给药、以治疗糖尿病、肥胖和心肺疾病的策略；这些策略目前已推进至人体临床试验。文章还讨论了用于推出新产品、赋予有价值的农艺性状或增强光合作用的高价值工业酶。未来展望部分列举了有望在未来3—5年推出的生物技术产品，并讨论了相关机遇与预期挑战。
