papers.title: Engineering all human milk oligosaccharide fucosidic linkages in planta.
papers.abstract: Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are a component of breast milk which improve infant health outcomes by modulating immune responses, inhibiting pathogen adhesion, and promoting healthy gut microbiota. Although their effects are well-documented, few HMOs have been clinically or biochemically studied because only a handful of the simplest HMOs out of >200 species are currently possible to chemically synthesize or produce in microbes via metabolic engineering in microbial hosts. In contrast, plants are naturally adept at biosynthesizing a wide range of complex polysaccharides, and they have recently been established as a heterologous system for HMO production. However, much of the structural diversity of HMOs has not yet been reproduced in a plant, particularly fucosylations. Four fucosidic linkages can be found in fucosylated HMOs, but only Fucα1-2Gal has been biosynthesized in planta. Here, we screened bacterial fucosyltransferases using the model plant Nicotiana benthamiana to produce 3-fucosyllactose (Fucα1-3Glc), lacto-N-fucopentaose II (Fucα1-4GlcNAc), and lacto-N-fucopentaose III (Fucα1-3GlcNAc), demonstrating that all four fucosidic linkages can be made in planta. Just twelve glycosidic linkages make up all the HMOs found in breast milk, and our findings increase the number of linkages made in planta from seven to ten, greatly expanding the variety of HMOs accessible in a plant.
papers.authors: Tang SN, Drako K, Wyatt G, Cheng L, Zerbe P, Shih PM.

enrichment.titleZh: 在植物体内工程化构建母乳寡糖的全部岩藻糖苷键类型
enrichment.abstractZh: 母乳寡糖（HMOs）是母乳的一种组分，可通过调节免疫反应、抑制病原体黏附和促进健康的肠道微生物群，改善婴儿的健康结局。尽管这些作用已有充分报道，但接受过临床或生化研究的HMO种类仍很少，因为在超过200种HMO中，目前只有少数结构最简单的种类能够通过化学合成，或在微生物宿主中利用代谢工程生产。相比之下，植物天然具备生物合成多种复杂多糖的能力，近期也已被用作HMO生产的异源体系。不过，HMOs中的许多结构类型尚未在植物中构建出来，尤其是岩藻糖基化结构。岩藻糖基化HMO中存在4种岩藻糖苷键，但此前仅有Fucα1-2Gal在植物体内实现了生物合成。本研究以模式植物本氏烟草（Nicotiana benthamiana）筛选细菌来源的岩藻糖基转移酶，生产了3-岩藻糖基乳糖（3-fucosyllactose，Fucα1-3Glc）、lacto-N-fucopentaose II（Fucα1-4GlcNAc）和lacto-N-fucopentaose III（Fucα1-3GlcNAc），表明全部4种岩藻糖苷键均可在植物体内构建。母乳中的所有HMO仅由12种糖苷键构成，本研究将已能在植物体内构建的糖苷键种类从7种增加到10种，大幅扩展了可利用植物合成的HMO种类。
enrichment.sourceTitle: Engineering all human milk oligosaccharide fucosidic linkages in planta.
enrichment.sourceAbstract: Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are a component of breast milk which improve infant health outcomes by modulating immune responses, inhibiting pathogen adhesion, and promoting healthy gut microbiota. Although their effects are well-documented, few HMOs have been clinically or biochemically studied because only a handful of the simplest HMOs out of >200 species are currently possible to chemically synthesize or produce in microbes via metabolic engineering in microbial hosts. In contrast, plants are naturally adept at biosynthesizing a wide range of complex polysaccharides, and they have recently been established as a heterologous system for HMO production. However, much of the structural diversity of HMOs has not yet been reproduced in a plant, particularly fucosylations. Four fucosidic linkages can be found in fucosylated HMOs, but only Fucα1-2Gal has been biosynthesized in planta. Here, we screened bacterial fucosyltransferases using the model plant Nicotiana benthamiana to produce 3-fucosyllactose (Fucα1-3Glc), lacto-N-fucopentaose II (Fucα1-4GlcNAc), and lacto-N-fucopentaose III (Fucα1-3GlcNAc), demonstrating that all four fucosidic linkages can be made in planta. Just twelve glycosidic linkages make up all the HMOs found in breast milk, and our findings increase the number of linkages made in planta from seven to ten, greatly expanding the variety of HMOs accessible in a plant.

papers.title: Raman/SERS-based identification, sorting and validation in droplet microfluidics: potential and challenges for biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: High-throughput microbial metabolite detection and screening support strain development and the design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycle in biomanufacturing. Droplet microfluidics provides independent microreactors for detection, sorting and recovery, but reliable screening also requires accurate identification, controlled separation and independent validation. This review discusses cell-laden and non-cell-laden droplets, detection methods, integration of surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) with droplet microfluidics, fermentation-matrix effects, Raman-activated cell and droplet sorting, and performance assessment. SERS provides signals through molecular fingerprints or specific recognition systems to inform sorting decisions. However, hot spots, probe state, matrix composition, droplet position and acquisition conditions affect absolute intensity, making single measurements unreliable for quantification without adequate calibration. Internal standards, matrix-matched calibration and averaging signals from droplets containing the same sample can improve quantitative reliability, while HPLC, LC-MS or functional assays can provide independent post-sorting validation. Many well-developed microdroplet SERS demonstrations use standards or biomedical models; complete detection, sorting and validation workflows in genuine fermentation samples and cell-laden droplets remain limited. Organised around target identification, physical sorting and post-sorting validation, this review evaluates the signal-throughput trade-off, matrix compatibility, detection-sorting timing and inconsistent evaluation criteria. A staged validation route from model droplets to fermentation samples and cell-laden droplets is discussed. By linking fermentation-matrix effects, sorting reliability and independent validation, the review helps identify sources of screening errors and assess the potential and limitations of these approaches in biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: Zhao H, Zheng S, Duan Y, Ge C, Yuan H, Wang Q, Chen L.
papers.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

papers.title: Sustainable 2-keto-L-gulonic acid biosynthesis via single-strain one-step fermentation.
papers.abstract: L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is an essential antioxidant molecule that maintains normal physiological functions in humans. Currently, industrial production relies primarily on a three-strain, two-step fermentation process to produce 2-keto-L-gulonic acid (2-KLG), the direct precursor of vitamin C. 2-KLG is then converted to vitamin C through chemical lactonization. However, this process is limited by prolonged fermentation cycles, poor stability of the mixed-culture system, and complex process control. In recent years, engineered single-strain platforms capable of one-step 2-KLG biosynthesis have emerged as a promising strategy for more sustainable vitamin C production. Nevertheless, the efficiency of L-sorbose-to-2-KLG conversion in this system remains low, making it a major bottleneck to further improving 2-KLG production. This review summarizes recent advances on single-strain, one-step fermentation systems using Gluconobacter oxydans as the chassis strain. It focuses on strategies including genetic tool development, metabolic engineering, and key enzyme optimization. The review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical reference for optimizing and industrializing green biomanufacturing systems for vitamin C.
papers.authors: Wang F, Zhou Q, Wang Y, Wang Z, Li D.

papers.title: YEASTRACT+: the 2026 update with focus on global quantitative transcription regulation data and metabolic engineering applications.
papers.abstract: YEASTRACT+ (http://yeastract-plus.org/) is a tool for the analysis, prediction, and modelling of transcription regulatory data at gene and genomic levels in yeasts. It incorporates three integrated databases: YEASTRACT, PathoYeastract, and NCYeastract, focused on Saccharomyces cerevisiae, pathogenic yeasts, and non-conventional yeasts of biotechnological relevance, respectively. In this release, YEASTRACT+ offers upgraded information on transcription regulation for 13 yeast species, extending the database to two additional yeasts of the basidiomycota phylum, the pathogenic yeast Cryptococcus neoformans, and the biotechnologically relevant Rhodotorula toruloides. A dramatic upgrade in the quality of the data provided occurred, as regulatory associations between transcription factors (TFs) and target genes are now associated with quantitative assessment. Quantitative impact of TFs on gene expression levels enabled the construction and release of two additional analytical tools: quantitative rank by TF, for the prediction of the most relevant TFs underlying a given transcriptomics dataset; and metabolic engineering based on integrating the quantitative impact of TF expression into genome-scale metabolic models. Altogether, this release of YEASTRACT+ provides unparalleled access to massive, curated, quantitative data associated with gene expression control in 13 yeast species, and a set of tools to enable its full exploitation towards fundamental, biotechnological, and health-related applications.
papers.authors: Coutinho L, Paulo L, Couceiro D, Val T, Oliveira J, Costa IV, Zolotareva M, Matos M, Fernandes M, Mupueleque M, Sá-Correia I, Teixeira MC, Monteiro PT.

papers.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations.
papers.abstract: Developing artificial intelligence (AI)-native experimental laboratories for autonomous scientific exploration with minimal human intervention represents a long-standing goal. Although autonomous experimental systems are emerging 1-4 , especially in chemical and materials science, they remain largely confined to domains with singular objectives, well-defined workflows and simple instrumentation. This limitation may reflect an 'add-on' architecture that uses AI as a task-specific tool rather than providing it with a global understanding of experiments, especially under engineering-oriented circumstances. Here we present AutoDNA, an AI-native autonomous biomolecular engineering laboratory targeting multi-objective experiments across diverse instruments. Through the co-design of models, experiments and instruments, AutoDNA realizes the co-evolution of AI and the automation system within an end-to-end multi-user framework. The system autonomously orchestrates over 20 types of instruments across more than 11,000 steps to execute core nucleic acid operations including synthesis, transcription, amplification and sequencing, while human intervention is limited to hardware maintenance tasks, such as reagent and labware replenishment. Across four representative applications, AutoDNA matched expert-optimized enzymatic DNA synthesis yields, accelerated concurrent protocol execution by 3.2-fold, completed an end-to-end DNA data storage cycle with exact recovery of the original digital content, and identified and validated a clinically detected KRAS G13D mutation. AutoDNA establishes a blueprint towards science-as-a-service, accelerating biological discovery and advancing various applications in synthetic biology and information storage.
papers.authors: Wu M, Wang Z, Wang J, Dong Z, Yang J, Li Q, Huang T, Zhang C, Song P, Zhao L, Li M, Zuo X, Wang F, Fan C, Chen H.

papers.title: Bacillus-mediated selenium nanoparticle biosynthesis: reduction pathways, cellular processes, and applications.
papers.abstract: Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) have attracted considerable interest due to their unique physicochemical properties, low toxicity compared with inorganic selenium (Se) compounds, and diverse biological activities. Microorganisms, particularly species of the genus Bacillus, represent efficient biological platforms for SeNP synthesis because of their tolerance to selenium oxyanions and their ability to reduce selenite Se (IV) to elemental selenium (Se 0 ) under mild conditions. Selenate-reduction is relatively poorly understood in this genus, so the candidate selenate-reductase system proposed here is inferred from selenium-respiring organisms and has not been genetically confirmed in Bacillus. This review summarizes current knowledge on Bacillus-mediated SeNP biosynthesis with an emphasis on microbial selenium transformation, cellular responses, and biochemical processes involved in nanoparticle formation. The roles of redox-associated pathways, reducing equivalents, candidate enzymes, metabolites, and extracellular biomolecules in selenium reduction, nucleation, and stabilization are critically discussed, while highlighting the limitations of current mechanistic understanding and the need for further genetic validation. In addition, this review examines how bacterial strain characteristics and cultivation conditions influence SeNP properties, including particle size, surface chemistry, stability, and biological activity. The applications of Bacillus-derived SeNPs, including antimicrobial, antioxidant, anticancer, agricultural, and environmental applications, are discussed in relation to the nanoparticle characteristics and biological performance. Throughout the review, evidence is explicitly attributed to the relevant source system, distinguishing among Bacillus-derived, other microbial, chemically synthesized, plant-derived, and general SeNP literature. Current biomedical evidence for Bacillus-mediated SeNPs is based predominantly on in-vitro studies. Finally, emerging approaches for improving microbial SeNP production through strain selection, metabolic engineering, and process optimization are highlighted. This review provides an integrated perspective on Bacillus-mediated SeNP biosynthesis, identifies future research directions and offers insights for researchers in microbiology, bioprocess engineering, animal nutrition and agricultural biotechnology.
papers.authors: Nawaz S, Anayat M, Nawaz N, Tao Z, Iftikhar M, Wang F.

papers.title: Biological Warfare, Bioterrorism, and Biocrime: A Systematic Review with Evidence-Based Historical Tiering (1763-2019).
papers.abstract: Introduction Biological warfare involves the deliberate use of microorganisms or toxins to cause disease and death in humans, animals, or plants, and has occurred across state warfare, bioterrorism, biocrime, and accidental laboratory release. Despite a substantial historical literature, many commonly cited events lack rigorous primary-source documentation, and secondary reviews frequently perpetuate unverified claims. This review applies explicit evidentiary criteria to distinguish well-documented incidents from contested allegations and unsubstantiated claims, using Carus's typology to categorize events by actor and intent. Materials and methods Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO CRD42024592724), we searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus up to April 4, 2024, supplemented by grey literature and expert consultation. Two reviewers applied predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria to title/abstract and full-text screening. A 3-tier evidentiary framework (well-documented, contested, and unsubstantiated), adapted from elements of ROBIS and PRISMA, was applied to 48 candidate events identified between pre-historic times and 2019, with adjudication by subject-matter experts. Quantitative analysis was restricted to the 19 well-documented events to anchor findings to corroborated evidence from primary archival sources, forensic investigations, and specialist scholarship. Results The 19 well-documented events caused at minimum 21,595 injuries and 10,079 deaths, comprising 17 deliberate uses (89.5%) and 2 major accidental releases (10.5%). Deliberate events comprised 6 biocrimes (31.6%), 5 acts of warfare (26.3%), 4 bioterrorist attacks (21.1%), and 2 State-sponsored acts (10.5%). Fourteen biological agents were employed across 31 agent instances. CDC Category B agents predominated (58.1%, n = 18), followed by Category A (35.5%, n = 11); 2 agents did not fit into the CDC classification (6.5%), and no Category C agents were identified. Bacillus anthracis was the most frequently used agent (22.6%, n = 7), followed by ricin (12.9%, n = 4) and Vibrio cholerae (9.7%, n = 3). The principal dispersal methods were contaminated food and beverages (29.2%, n = 7) and direct inoculation and infected animals or insect vectors (12.5%, n = 3), respectively. Events occurred across 9 countries, with the United States most frequently affected (31.6%, n = 6). Perpetrators originated from 10 countries, with the United States, United Kingdom, and Japan together accounting for over half of the well-documented events. Fewer than half of the events identified across the historical literature (n = 19; 39.6%) met the criteria for well-documented status, underscoring the need for consistent evidentiary standards in biosecurity research. Conclusions Biological warfare remains a significant concern given its covert nature, the accessibility of low-technology dispersal methods, and emerging risks from synthetic biology, dual-use research, and artificial intelligence. Prevention, early detection, and rapid response, supported by ethical research oversight and open-source surveillance, are essential to mitigating these threats.
papers.authors: Honeyman DA, Akhtar Z, Heslop DJ, MacIntyre CR.

papers.title: Global health security and smallpox: A strategic review of post-eradication biosafety and preparedness.
papers.abstract: The global biosecurity framework faces a potential critical transition driven by synthetic biology advancements and declining population-level immunity. This review evaluates smallpox as a central case study for contemporary pathogen governance and biopolitical preparedness. We analyze the convergence of two primary risks: the technical feasibility of de novo orthopoxvirus synthesis and the expanding immunity gap following the cessation of routine vaccination. The 2022 mpox resurgence is assessed as a sentinel event revealing strategic vulnerabilities in cross-protective immunity. Ultimately, this perspective argues that smallpox reemergence risk is not merely a technological byproduct, but a fundamental global governance crisis. To mitigate these threats, we propose a multidimensional framework integrated with One Health principles and transnational coordination. Maintaining strategic vigilance and institutional memory is presented as a critical political capacity for post-eradication health security.
papers.authors: Bülbül A, Kara A.
papers.journal: Politics and the life sciences : the journal of the Association for Politics and the Life Sciences

papers.title: Metabolic engineering of Saccharomyces cerevisiae for improved polyphosphate production
papers.abstract: Finite high-grade phosphate rock reserves and rising legislative demand for phosphorus recycling create a need for processes converting phosphorus-containing residual streams into valuable products. Microbial synthesis of inorganic polyphosphate (polyP) could complement its energy-intensive chemical manufacturing while enabling phosphorus recovery in a value-added product with applications ranging from food processing to flame retardants and fertilizer. After orthophosphate (P i ) starvation and refeeding, Saccharomyces cerevisiae naturally accumulates polyP as a cellular P i reserve, but the current multistage process complicates industrial implementation. Here, we identified metabolic interventions that uncouple polyP accumulation from P i starvation by systematic evaluation of 57 engineered S. cerevisiae CEN.PK113-7D strains. Constitutive activation of the PHO regulon produced the strongest increase in polyP, whereas disruption of inositol pyrophosphate synthesis, P i import, or the vacuolar transporter chaperone complex impaired accumulation. This pattern indicates that efficient polyP accumulation depends on coordinated activation of P i acquisition and vacuolar polymerization. Notably, deletion of PHO80 converted a transient starvation response into a constitutive production phenotype, enabling high polyP accumulation during growth. Optimization of the growth medium increased the polyP content further, and efficient use of the supplied P i was demonstrated, while electron microscopy paired with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy supported increased vacuolar storage. During aerobic exponential fed-batch cultivation, pho80Δ simultaneously formed biomass and polyP, reaching a polyP content of 22.1% of cell dry weight and a titer of 8.2 g/L, both expressed as KPO 3 equivalents. These findings establish S. cerevisiae pho80Δ as a promising platform for biological polyP production and phosphorus recovery. Abstract Figure
papers.authors: Baier M, Karmainski T, Buhl EM, Deitert A, Eerlings R, Völker F, Brans L, Deis E, Demling P, Blank LM.

papers.title: Metabolic shuttles between mitochondria and plastids: Roles of key transporters in coordinating carbon-nitrogen metabolism.
papers.abstract: Carbon and nitrogen metabolism in plant cells is distributed across multiple organelles, requiring extensive metabolite exchange to coordinate growth, development and environmental responses. Mitochondria and plastids function as interconnected metabolic hubs linked through the transport of carbon skeletons, amino acids, organic acids, and redox equivalents across organellar membranes. These transport processes are essential for integrating energy conversion processes, nitrogen assimilation, and biosynthetic metabolism. In this review, we integrate current knowledge of mitochondrial and plastid envelope transporters that mediate carbon-nitrogen exchange between organelles, focusing on recent characterisation of transporters with confirmed substrates. We discuss how these transporters contribute to the coordination of cellular metabolism, highlight emerging concepts regarding their regulation and integration, and identify major knowledge gaps in our understanding of interorganellar metabolic communication. Understanding how these transport systems collectively shape carbon-nitrogen fluxes is essential for deciphering metabolic flexibility and guiding metabolic engineering strategies in plants.
papers.authors: Le XH, Millar AH, Kuhnert F.

papers.title: Next-generation CAR-NK therapies: molecular engineering strategies for solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are innate lymphocytes that exert cytotoxic activity against malignant and virus-infected cells without prior antigen sensitization. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-engineered NK (CAR-NK) cells combine CAR-dependent tumor-antigen recognition with endogenous NK-cell receptor-dependent cytotoxicity against stress-induced ligands and tumor cells with reduced HLA class I expression. Clinical studies of allogeneic CD19 CAR-NK cells have reported antitumor responses without notable cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity, or graft-versus-host disease. CAR-NK cells also support allogeneic manufacturing for off-the-shelf cellular therapy. NK-associated intracellular domains including DAP10, DAP12, 2B4, and CD3ζ, cytokine expression using IL-15 or IL-21, and gene editing of inhibitory molecules have been incorporated into CAR-NK designs. PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 and JAK-STAT signaling, glycolytic metabolism, mitochondrial activity, and transcriptional control contribute to CAR-NK cytotoxic function. Recent CAR-NK studies have also examined inhibitory-receptor editing, chemokine receptor expression, and metabolic engineering to improve cytotoxic activity, intratumoral infiltration, and resistance to hypoxia and immunosuppressive signaling in solid tumors. This review examines the molecular mechanisms involved in NK-cell activation and metabolism and evaluates molecular engineering strategies for next-generation CAR-NK therapy in solid tumors.
papers.authors: Kim ME, Lim Y, Lee JS.

papers.title: Protein nanocages: Programmable biomaterial platforms for therapeutics, bioimaging, and diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Protein nanocages are monodisperse, hollow structures formed through the symmetric self-assembly of protein subunits. Their genetically encoded architectures combine the geometric precision of nanoscale assemblies with the intrinsic biocompatibility and functional versatility of naturally evolved proteins. Well-defined internal cavities and engineerable interior and exterior surfaces enable the spatial organization of therapeutic cargoes, molecular recognition elements, and bioactive components within a single nanoscale platform. In this Review, we examine the structural organization, self-assembly mechanisms, physicochemical properties, and functional diversity of representative protein nanocages, including ferritin, the pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 core, DNA-binding proteins from starved cells (Dps), small heat shock proteins (sHSPs), encapsulins, and lumazine synthase. We discuss how their structural features and assembly behavior govern biological performance and support biomedical applications in targeted drug delivery, cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, and in vivo and in vitro diagnostics. Beyond describing individual platforms, we establish a unifying framework that positions protein nanocages as programmable molecular organizers and highlights five transferable design principles: multivalent ligand display, spatial compartmentalization, receptor-guided targeting, reporter organization and signal enhancement, and stimulus-responsive cargo release and functional activation. We also examine persistent challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, scalable manufacturing, and clinical translation, alongside emerging opportunities in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and computational protein design. Collectively, these principles establish protein nanocages as versatile biomaterial platforms for integrating sensing, targeting, imaging, and therapy within a single molecular architecture, providing a foundation for next-generation precision nanomedicine. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Reviews typically treat protein nanocages individually, obscuring shared structural features and the extent to which design strategies transfer across systems. This Review addresses this gap by establishing a comparative framework spanning structurally diverse nanocages and distilling their similarities into a concise set of generalizable design principles. It reframes protein nanocages not merely as passive delivery vehicles but as programmable molecular scaffolds that organize cargo with controlled spatial arrangement and stoichiometry. This framework provides biomaterials researchers with a transferable basis for engineering protein assemblies for precision nanomedicine while identifying key challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, and scalable manufacturing that must be addressed to facilitate clinical translation.
papers.authors: Shin J, Jung S, Lee AS, Kim CS.

papers.title: Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation.
papers.abstract: Translatable circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional mRNA therapy due to their improved stability that results in a prolonged expression window. The translation of circRNAs is mainly driven by internal ribosome entry site (IRES) or IRES-like elements, which is tightly regulated by various trans-acting RNA binding proteins (RBPs). Here we develop a cell-based system to systematically screen RBPs that enhance translation of circRNAs, identifying 68 proteins as putative activators of noncanonical translation. These translation activators are involved in a broad range of biological processes including RNA processing, ribosomal biogenesis, and translation initiation. We further design a machine learning algorithm to extract common sequence features of these activators and predict more potential RBPs with translation activator activities. The newly identified and predicted activators are subsequently validated to promote the IRES-mediated circRNA translation in a context-dependent fashion. Overall, this study provides new insights into IRES-related trans-acting factors and expands the toolbox for engineered RBPs in RNA synthetic biology.
papers.authors: Lu QY, Wang SQ, Ye YW, Wei T, Yang Y, Wei HY, Wang Z.

papers.title: A century of soybean breeding increased photosynthetic capacity but not NPQ relaxation.
papers.abstract: Accelerating photoprotective regulation to improve carbon assimilation is a promising strategy to increase crop productivity. Although rapid non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) relaxation has been validated as a target through metabolic engineering, it remains unclear whether conventional breeding has improved this trait. Here, we investigated whether more than a century of soybean breeding enhanced NPQ relaxation alongside light-saturated carbon assimilation and seed traits. We evaluated a historical panel of 24 soybean genotypes across vegetative and reproductive developmental stages by integrating NPQ relaxation, gas exchange parameters, xanthophyll-cycle pigment profiles, expression of key photoprotective genes (VDE, PsbS, and ZEP), seed number and seed weight. NPQ relaxation parameters were not consistently associated with genotype release year, seed number, or seed weight at either developmental stage. The only exception was the amplitude of the rapidly relaxing NPQ component (AqE), which was negatively correlated with all three variables during the reproductive stage. In contrast, genotype release year was positively associated with maximum net CO2 assimilation rate (Amax), maximum carboxylation rate of Rubisco (Vcmax), maximum electron transport rate (Jmax), seed number, and seed weight, while Amax and Vcmax were positively correlated with seed number and seed weight. These findings indicate that the greater photosynthetic capacity of modern genotypes was not accompanied by faster photoprotective response. Thus, photoprotective regulation has not kept pace with gains in photosynthetic capacity under field conditions. We conclude that rapid NPQ relaxation remains an important target for synchronizing photoprotection with the high photosynthetic capacity of modern soybean lines.
papers.authors: de Oliveira LP, Attri K, Doran L, Leonelli LB, Long SP, Ainsworth EA.

papers.title: Adipose-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells: Isolation, Origin, Phenotype Applications, and Challenges.
papers.abstract: Traditional adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (AD-MSCs) research has relied on unfractionated bulk populations, whose therapeutic efficacy is constrained by cellular heterogeneity, culture-induced phenotypic drift, and rapid postengraftment functional exhaustion, resulting in inconsistent outcomes and impeding clinical translation. This review systematically examines AD-MSC developmental origins, tissue niches, isolation and purification strategies, functional phenotypes, and biomanufacturing bottlenecks. It integrates preclinical and clinical evidence for AD-MSCs and their extracellular vesicles (EVs) in bone and cartilage regeneration, chronic cutaneous diseases, neurological disorders, cardiovascular diseases, and other conditions. These therapies remodel injured microenvironments through immunometabolic reprogramming, antifibrotic signaling, angiogenesis, mitochondrial transfer, and paracrine regulation rather than direct tissue replacement. Major translational barriers include cellular heterogeneity, safety concerns, the transdifferentiation controversy, nonstandardized preconditioning, culture-induced phenotypic drift, and low cell retention after transplantation. We propose that clinical translation should be based on prospective isolation of functional subpopulations, coupled with tailored preconditioning, precision gene editing, three-dimensional biomaterials, EV engineering, and automated closed-system biomanufacturing. This framework aims to preserve potency, phenotypic stability, and paracrine function, transforming AD-MSCs and their bioactive derivatives from variable, unfractionated preparations into well-characterized, standardized, highly potent precision biologics. More broadly, it offers a mechanism-driven, function-defined, engineering-enabled, and clinically accessible roadmap for next-generation regenerative medicine.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Tu G, Wang C, Zhao H, Wu Z, Li W, Chen L, Niu B.

papers.title: Advancing terpenoid biosynthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Synthetic biology approaches for efficient longifolene production.
papers.abstract: The sustainable microbial production of high-value terpenoids like longifolene represents a critical frontier in green manufacturing, yet it is often hindered by systemic metabolic inefficiencies in microbial hosts. To address this, we present a comprehensive systems metabolic engineering framework in Saccharomyces cerevisiae that integrates three complementary modules to overcome the key bottlenecks of enzyme catalysis, cofactor supply, and precursor availability. First, we enhanced the catalytic module by employing the RII dimerization/docking domain-RI anchoring disruptor (RIDD-RIAD) peptide-mediated enzyme assembly and structure-guided Pinus sylvestris longifolene synthase (psTPS) variant screening, 'which improved whole-cell longifolene production under the tested conditions. Second, to resolve nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) cofactor imbalance, we engineered a dual-regeneration system by introducing an exogenous formate dehydrogenase (FDH) and simultaneously amplifying endogenous pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) flux. Third, we reprogrammed central carbon metabolism by integrating the non-oxidative glycolysis (NOG) pathway and deleting the transcriptional repressors DOS2 and YNR063W, and was associated with a larger steady-state cytosolic acetyl-CoA pool, the essential terpenoid precursor. This multi-pronged strategy culminated in a highly optimized strain that achieved a titer of 92.84 mg/L in shake-flask cultures. Critically, the process was successfully scaled to a 5 L bioreactor under fed-batch conditions, yielding 4181.51 mg/L total longifolene at 204 h (3484.79 mg/L extracellular and 696.72 mg/L cell-associated), the highest total titer among the microbial reports identified in Supplementary Table S4. Differences in product recovery and cultivation protocols limit direct process comparisons. Our work demonstrates that coordinated optimization of enzyme assembly, cofactor regeneration, and carbon-flow reprogramming can substantially improve longifolene biosynthesis in S. cerevisiae. This study provides a longifolene-focused case study for modular pathway optimization, while broader application of this strategy to other terpenoids or natural products will require further pathway-specific validation.
papers.authors: Zhang W, Xin Y, Li S, Shen X, Zhang J, He H, Xiang S, Ba L, Liu Y.

papers.title: Biosensor-guided genome-wide CRISPR screens enable cis , cis -muconic acid overproduction in yeast
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Classical pathway metabolic engineering relies on enhancing strain productivity through the introduction of rationally identified genetic perturbations, which while useful, are time-consuming and miss unintuitive targets. Genome-wide CRISPR screens offer an alternative by efficiently sampling genomes, enabling the engineering of novel phenotypes, and are further enhanced when combined with high-throughput strain interrogation methods. Here, using Saccharomyces cerevisiae , we engineered small molecule biosensors into population enrichment tools using zeocin resistance and fluorescence as signal outputs. We then introduced the multi-functional genome-wide CRISPR (MAGIC) library that targets every gene for activation, interference, or deletion, thus creating biosensor-aided MAGIC, or senMAGIC. As a case study, we utilized senMAGIC to identify single genetic determinants that improve productivity of the nylon precursors protocatechuic and cis , cis -muconic acids (PCA and ccM). These were then randomly assembled as triple gRNA-tRNA arrays for multiplexed gene perturbations to identify combinatorial effects. Top gRNA hits were then confirmed using direct genomic integrations in senMAGIC-free production strains, resulting in identifying known as well as novel targets that increase PCA and ccM titres. Our results demonstrate senMAGIC as a robust automation-friendly whole-genome evolution tool and highlight limitations of the method, providing a roadmap for future multifunctional CRISPR screens to optimize host metabolism for efficient bioprocesses.
papers.authors: Nasr MA, Knoops A, Thornbury M, Davies M, Kwan DH, Martin VJ.
papers.status: 预印本 · 未经同行评审

papers.title: Ca 2+ signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots.
papers.abstract: Plants must continually balance growth with arrest, especially under stress. Auxin signaling acts as a central regulatory hub in this process, yet the mechanisms that dynamically tune auxin signaling in real time remain unknown. Here, we use the light-gated, Ca 2+ -permeable Channelrhodopsin 2 variant XXM2.0 to optogenetically impose defined Ca 2+ signatures on Arabidopsis root cells. Repetitive light activation triggers cytosolic Ca 2+ signals that in turn suppress membrane depolarization and Ca 2+ transients triggered by exogenous auxin. Moreover, prolonged optogenetic Ca 2+ stimulation affects auxin-responsive transcriptional reprogramming. As phenotypic output, reversible inhibition of root growth by suppressing cell division and elongation is observed. We further identify a candidate CaM7-CNGC14 module that likely mediates Ca 2+ -dependent gating of responsiveness to exogenous auxin as well as Ca 2+ -dependent root growth inhibition. Our study thus introduces a synthetic biology approach to decompose calcium-auxin crosstalk in plant cells, and demonstrates that optogenetically imposed cytosolic Ca 2+ signals act as dynamic regulators of auxin susceptibility in roots.
papers.authors: Song H, Baudon A, Freund M, Randuch M, Pěnčík A, Novák O, He Z, Kaufmann K, Li N, Gilliham M, Friml J, Hedrich R, Huang S.

papers.title: Circadian rhythms in arthritis: from pathophysiology to chronotherapy.
papers.abstract: Arthritis is characterized by pain and inflammation of the joints, with the most common forms being osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). These conditions affect a sizeable portion of the adult population, creating substantial health and socioeconomic burdens. Dysregulated inflammatory pathways contribute to arthritis and represent important targets for current and emerging therapies. Symptoms and cytokine levels change dynamically over time in arthritis, varying not only with disease state (such as flare-ups) but also with daily circadian rhythms. Daily fluctuations in rheumatoid arthritis symptoms are well established and parallel changes in inflammatory mediators, whereas osteoarthritis seems to exhibit more variable and patient-specific temporal patterns. Current treatments generally do not account for these biological rhythms. However, growing evidence suggests that aligning therapy with circadian fluctuations (termed 'chronotherapy') could improve outcomes and reduce adverse effects, although practical implementation remains challenging. Emerging synthetic biology approaches aim to enable timed drug delivery by harnessing the endogenous genetic mechanisms that regulate cellular rhythms. Together, these advances highlight opportunities for translating circadian-based therapies into clinical practice.
papers.authors: Cimino A, Lipa KE, Kim A, Meng QJ, Herzog ED, Pham CTN, Guilak F.

papers.title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates.
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA-peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. Integrating systematic experiments with all-atom simulations, we decode a multiscale mechanism: coacervate infiltration at the micrometer scale mediates molecular buffering at the nanometer scale, which fluidizes the crosslinked network to drive macroscopic liquefaction. This capability is governed by a design rule, where coacervates formed by small-molecular anions exhibit optimal efficacy. We deploy this principle to functionally rescue silenced RNA within a model of pathologically solidified ribonucleoprotein assemblies. Our work provides a general framework for the active, compositional control of biomolecular phase behavior, with direct implications for managing pathological aggregation and engineering functional condensates in synthetic and living systems.
papers.authors: Guo W, Luo R, Shen Y, Zeng X, Liu Z, Shum HC.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Combinatorial Tuning of Multigene Biosynthetic Pathways based on RNA Interference.
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning the expression level of multigene pathways remains a major challenge in engineering eukaryotic microbial cell factories. Modifications to individual pathway genes and CRISPR-based approaches often require repeated genome reconstruction, large regulatory components, or complex guide-array assembly. Here, we developed a lightweight, post-transcriptional RNAi-based strategy that enables fine-tuning gene expression without iterative genome editing. Size-selected small-RNA sequencing and functional testing were used to identify endogenous Pol III promoters spanning graded transcriptional strengths in Schizochytrium sp. Combining promoter strength with multiple short hairpin RNA (shRNA) target positions expanded the accessible repression range and enabled high-resolution gene-dosage tuning. The RNAi-based combined regulation strategy was applied to the three-gene carotenoid pathway of Schizochytrium sp. and the nine-gene docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) pathway of Yarrowia lipolytica, significantly enhancing the product production in both hosts. Integration of RNAi screening and dosage optimization further identified and tuned bypass pathways, increasing the ratio of DHA to docosapentaenoic acid (DPA) by 4.50-fold versus wild type. These gains were maintained during 5-L fermentation and serial passaging. This work establishes a compact and scalable regulatory framework for engineering complex biosynthetic pathways in eukaryotic microbial hosts.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Xu Y, Li Z, Du F, Ma W, Yang G, Sun X.

papers.title: Decoding the landscape in biomanufacturing of xylose: metabolic bottlenecks and computation-assisted strategies.
papers.abstract: As the second most abundant sugar in lignocellulose, xylose suffers from low utilization efficiency due to carbon catabolite repression and the scarcity of natural metabolic pathways. This bottleneck leads to the wastage of nearly 40% of available carbohydrate sources, undermining the economic competitiveness of biorefineries. Overcoming these metabolic barriers is essential for the transition toward large-scale, sustainable biomanufacturing. This review comprehensively summarizes the main pathways of xylose metabolism, with a particular focus on its major metabolic products, rate-limiting enzymes, cofactor preferences, feedback regulation, and compartmentalization. Special attention is given to the significance of modifying rate-limiting enzymes for enhancing carbon flux in the xylose metabolic pathway. The study aims to integrate current knowledge, and to provide support for further research. While enzyme limitations and redox imbalances persist, this review highlights how integrating AI-driven protein engineering with genome-scale metabolic models offers precise solutions. By optimizing key enzymes and correcting cofactor dependencies, these computational strategies provide a robust framework for overcoming metabolic bottlenecks. Ultimately, synergistic AI-metabolic modeling accelerates the efficient conversion of xylose, unlocking its transformative potential for the green bioeconomy.
papers.authors: Zou L, Rashwan AK, Fozi V, Yahia ZO, Xie L, Chen W.

papers.title: Enzyme-Immobilized Nanomaterials for Endocrine Disorders: Therapeutic Innovation and Translational Challenges.
papers.abstract: Endocrine disorders result from chronic disturbances in the hormonal regulation and feedback control, which cause metabolic, reproductive, and systemic complications. Despite the advances in disease management with current therapies such as hormone replacement or multi-pathway pharmacological therapies, problems with variable patient response, side effects and the need for continuous monitoring and dose adjustment remain. To overcome some of these limitations, enzyme-immobilized nanomaterials have become attractive platforms for providing controlled biochemical interactions, catalytic activity and enzyme stability for therapeutic and diagnostic purposes. Enzymes can be immobilized using adsorption, covalent binding, cross-linking and entrapment to minimize denaturation, enhance reusability and improve operational performance. At the nanoscale level, other advantages of having high surface area and tunable interfacial chemistry are the better orientation of the enzyme, mass transfer and control over enzyme activity. There are other benefits for magnetic and field responsive nanomaterials in recovery, re-use, scalable processing and regenerable biosensing systems. In this review, the therapeutic potential of enzyme-immobilized nanomaterials for endocrine diseases has been discussed, focusing on the concepts of nanobiocatalyst design, biosensing for endocrine diseases, and the promise of biomanufacturing in the same field. It also points to some of the main hurdles facing the clinical translation of these technologies, such as problems with enzyme leaching, diffusion limitations, loss of interfacial activity, reproducibility issues, long-term stability, and safety evaluation requirements.
papers.authors: Zhang B, Zhang J, He Y.

papers.title: Green production of short-chain diols through microbial fermentation and bioconversion: Current advances, challenges, and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Short-chain diols (C2-C5) are important platform chemicals used in polymers, textiles, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and specialty chemicals. Their conventional petrochemical production is associated with fossil-resource dependence and substantial energy requirements, motivating the development of bio-based alternatives. However, existing knowledge remains fragmented across individual diols, microbial hosts, metabolic pathways, and production technologies, limiting systematic assessment of their relative performance and industrial feasibility. This review addresses these gaps through a product-oriented comparative analysis of microbial production of ethylene glycol, propanediols, butanediols, and pentanediols. It examines metabolic pathway design, host engineering, renewable feedstock utilization, and fermentation strategies, highlighting how precursor availability, intermediate toxicity, redox balance, and cofactor requirements influence product yield, titer, and productivity. The review further evaluates downstream recovery options and their implications for purification costs, alongside reported techno-economic and life-cycle assessment findings. Particular attention is given to the challenges of comparing studies with different process conditions, economic assumptions, and environmental system boundaries. Finally, the review distinguishes comparatively mature bio-based production platforms from emerging pathways and identifies priorities for improving process integration, economic competitiveness, and environmental performance. This integrated perspective provides a basis for evaluating research progress and guiding the development of commercially viable and environmentally sustainable short-chain diol production systems.
papers.authors: Bhatia SK, Gurav R, Joo JC, Yang YH.

papers.title: Harnessing yeast biodiversity to identify superior chassis strains for metabolic engineering and precision fermentation.
papers.abstract: Microbial cell factories are increasingly used for the sustainable production of fuels, chemicals and pharmaceuticals. Yeasts are particularly suitable as production hosts because of their metabolic flexibility, robustness, and expanding synthetic biology toolkits. Metabolic engineering of yeast historically relied on a narrow set of reference species and strains, especially Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Recent studies, however, show that applying identical pathway designs to different strain backgrounds or species can yield significant differences in titer, rate and yield (TRY). In this review, we examine how diversity within and between species in genomic features, metabolic regulation, substrate utilization and stress tolerance shapes chassis performance. We focus on eight species, including S. cerevisiae, Yarrowia lipolytica, Kluyveromyces marxianus, Komagataella phaffii, Ogataea polymorpha, Rhodotorula toruloides, Lipomyces starkeyi and Pichia kudriavzevii. We highlight that different species and strain backgrounds provide distinct advantages depending on the target product, pathway requirements, substrate, and process conditions. Finally, we discuss the transition from empirical strain screening toward diversity-informed and predictive chassis selection through multi-omics, phenotyping, metabolic modeling, and machine learning. We propose that chassis identity should be treated as a design variable, and that chassis selection should become an integral part of the Design-Build-Test-Learn cycle to develop optimal cell factories.
papers.authors: Zhu Y, Voordeckers K, Steensels J, Verstrepen KJ.

papers.title: Integrated metabolic and process engineering of Rhodotorula toruloides for light-driven hydrocarbon production.
papers.abstract: Long-chain hydrocarbons are bulky chemicals traditionally produced via petroleum refining. Microbial production of these hydrocarbons from renewable resources has attracted much attention, but is limited by precursor accessibility and catalysis efficiency. Here, we combined genetic engineering and photobioprocess optimization for blue-light-driven hydrocarbon production by the oleaginous yeast Rhodotorula toruloides . Cytosolic expression of the Chlorella variabilis fatty acid photodecarboxylase ( Cv FAP) in R . toruloides conferred cells producing 15.0 mg/L hydrocarbons, while targeting Cv FAP to lipid droplets (LDs) via fusion with the LD-associated protein Ldp1 enhanced titer by more than 3-fold. Systematic optimization of blue-light fermentation further doubled hydrocarbon titers. Metabolic rewiring of the pathways related to fatty acid activation, lipid turnover, and carotenoid biosynthesis showed that CRT1 deletion had the most pronounced effect, increasing hydrocarbon titer by 2.5-fold. Additional improvements were achieved by reinforcing free fatty acid supply and increasing CvFAP copy number. The final strain R. toruloides NF72D produced 557.7 mg/L hydrocarbons in flask culture, over 37-fold higher than that by the initial cytosolic expression strain. Collectively, this study demonstrates the importance of proper localization of key enzymes for improved biosynthesis of fatty acid-derived metabolites and a great potential for light-driven production of renewable hydrocarbons by oleaginous yeasts.
papers.authors: Zhao H, Zhang Y, Lyu L, Lu H, Zhao ZK.

papers.title: N-GLYcanyzer monitoring of a microperfusion process reveals critical parameters’ impact on Trastuzumab biosimilar N-glycoform time evolution
papers.abstract: Controlling monoclonal antibody (mAb) N-glycosylation as a critical quality attribute (CQA) remains challenging in continuous and intensified biomanufacturing, where conventional end-point analyses obscure dynamic pathway responses. Here, we deployed the N-GLYcanyzer process analytical technology (PAT) for automated monitoring of a microperfusion process that reveals critical parameters’ impact on Trastuzumab biosimilar N- glycoform time evolution across a 20-day culture duration of Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells in a ∼2 mL scale-down microbioreactor perfusion platform. Using offline PAT assays combined with our integrated at-line PAT workflow, we systematically screened six perfusion process parameters: carbon source, viable cell density (VCD), perfusion rate, temperature, and pH. While nutrient limitation and thermal/acidic stress significantly disrupted N-glycans maturation, notably triggering high-mannose (Man5) accumulation and severe productivity penalties under pH 6.7 and 39 °C operation, targeted feed supplementation with galactose and MnCl consistently shifted glycoform profiles away from G0F toward galactosylated species (G1F, G1F′, G2F). Crucially, coupling this combined feed strategy with an intensified perfusion rate (1.2 VVD) achieved a sustained, desired galactosylation shift without a productivity cost. These findings demonstrate that nutrient feed composition and perfusion rate are primary levers for steering continuous intensified microperfusion processes for biologics production with desired N-glycoform states and highlight the utility of automated at-line PAT like N-GLYcanyzer for enabling real-time attribute-based control in continuous biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: Narvekar A, Harrison M, Thakur R, Khot P, Semira P, Lee K, Chundawat SP.
papers.status: 预印本 · 未经同行评审

papers.title: Artificial photosynthetic cells: bridging chemical energization with biological functionalization.
papers.abstract: Artificial photosynthetic cells are nature-inspired systems that reproduce photosynthetic functions within cell/cell-mimetic compartments. Unlike discrete photocatalytic platforms, they integrate light harvesting, charge separation, multistep catalysis, selective transport, and compartmentalization to convert isolated photochemical reactions into coordinated cell-like functions. Driven by needs in carbon-neutral manufacturing, sustainable solar conversion, and precision medicine, the field is advancing from simple photocatalytic vesicles toward integrated and increasingly synthetic-cell platforms. In this review, we systematically elaborate on the rational design principles and emergent functional landscapes of artificial photosynthetic cells from a bioinspired perspective. We first decode the fundamental operational logic of natural photosynthesis, serving as a design blueprint. We then summarize the core construction modules of artificial photosynthetic cells, including cell-mimetic chassis, high-performance light-harvesting engines, multi-level catalytic networks, and precise interfacial engineering strategies. Furthermore, we categorize assembly paradigms into three mainstream branches: semi-artificial biohybrid systems, bottom-up reconstituted synthetic systems, and fully abiotic photosynthetic mimics. We further highlight a series of current and prospective functionalities, ranging from solar-driven CO 2 fixation and high-value chemical synthesis to in situ biomedical drug generation, as well as primitive life-like characteristics including intercellular communication, motility, and compartment division. Finally, we pinpoint the key technical bottlenecks, common pitfalls and outline opportunities enabled by the deep integration of synthetic biology, functional materials chemistry, and systematic bioengineering.
papers.authors: Gao F, Li D, Chen Y, Chen A, Liu G, Wang Y, Gao C, Xiong Y.

papers.title: Beyond the Stool: Circulating Short-Chain Fatty Acids Better Predict Human Gut-Related Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) mediate host-microbiota interactions and are typically measured in feces as markers of gut microbial activity. However, whether fecal SCFAs adequately reflect disease-associated host-microbiota dysfunction remains unclear. We hypothesized that circulating SCFAs, which integrate microbial production, intestinal absorption, barrier function, and host metabolism, provide a more informative representation of gut-related diseases. Methods Seven fecal and serum SCFAs were quantified by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry in 193 individuals, including patients with colorectal cancer (CRC, n = 30), celiac disease (CD, n = 35), obesity (OB, n = 33), and healthy controls (HCs, n = 95). We developed an interpretable machine-learning framework combining stacking ensembles, bootstrap validation, permutation testing, SHAP and LIME analyses. Cross-compartment predictive modeling was used to assess the reciprocal informativeness of fecal and circulating SCFAs. Results Circulating SCFAs exhibited markedly stronger disease-associated signatures than fecal SCFAs across all groups. Serum-based models achieved excellent classification performance (95% accuracy; multiclass ROC-AUC 1.00), whereas fecal SCFAs provided substantially lower predictive power (59% accuracy). Combining serum and fecal datasets yielded only marginal improvement (97.4% accuracy), indicating most diagnostic relevant information was already captured in circulation. Valeric, propionic, 2-methylbutyric, and isovaleric acids were consistently identified as the main contributors to disease discrimination. Cross-compartment modeling revealed weak predictive relationships between fecal and serum SCFAs, indicating these pools are largely non-redundant and reflect distinct biological processes. Conclusions Circulating SCFAs outperform fecal SCFAs as biomarkers of gut-related diseases, capturing the integrated effects of microbial activity and host physiology. These findings support blood-based SCFA profiling as a promising approach for precision diagnostics in microbiota-associated disorders.
papers.authors: Baldi S, Rotelli A, Cei F, Bertorello S, Bongianni A, Menicatti M, Calabrò AS, Cianchi F, Colombini B, Sofi F, Niccolai E, Bartolucci G, Iadanza E, Amedei A.
papers.journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians

papers.title: Cyclotides from Clitoria ternatea: Genomic Organization, Biosynthesis, and Roles in Plant Defense.
papers.abstract: Clitoria ternatea, commonly known as butterfly pea, is a perennial legume widely recognized for its ornamental and medicinal value. Beyond its characteristic anthocyanin-rich blue flowers, the plant produces cyclotides, a type of ultra-stable, cyclic cystine-knot peptide, with exceptional biological functions. Unlike other cyclotide-bearing families that carry independent cyclotide genes, C. ternatea integrates cyclotide domains into albumin-1 genes, replacing β-chain domains through divergent or convergent evolution. Genomic and transcriptomic studies reveal a large repertoire of albumin-1 loci and associated biosynthetic enzymes, including asparaginyl endopeptidases (butelase-1), protein disulphide isomerases, and peptidyl-prolyl isomerases, which orchestrate the cyclization, folding, and stabilization of cyclotides. Transcriptome analyses further demonstrate tissue-specific expression patterns, with distinct cyclotides such as cliotides T2 and T3 enriched in flowers and pods, and cliotides T8-T10 specialized in seeds, reflecting adaptive responses to localized biotic stress. Functionally, C. ternatea cyclotides exhibit broad-spectrum defense properties, including insecticidal, bactericidal, nematicidal, and antifungal activities, primarily through membrane permeabilization and disruption of lipid bilayers. Their preferential affinity for phosphatidylethanolamine-rich membranes highlights their selective toxicity toward insect and microbial targets. Recent advances in synthetic biology exploit cyclotides' structural stability as molecular scaffolds for therapeutic peptide design, with applications in immunomodulatory, antimicrobial, and anticancer drug development. This review consolidates genomic, transcriptomic, and functional insights into cyclotide biosynthesis and activity in C. ternatea, highlighting its evolutionary distinctiveness and biotechnological potential. Future research integrating multi-omics and spatial single-cell analyses can further unravel regulatory networks, defense dynamics, and translational applications of these unique plant peptides.
papers.authors: Kumar R, Yeo LM, Singaram N, Mah SH, Bunawan H, Lee KW, Yap WHH.

papers.title: Fluidized Bed Cathodes Enable High-Rate CO 2 to Formate Production and In Situ Microbial Growth
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical CO 2 Reduction Reaction (eCO 2 RR) to formate offers a sustainable and promising route for storing renewable electricity in a microbial energy substrate. Conventional CO 2 electrolyzers rely on flat electrodes with limited catalytic surface area, mass-transfer constraints, and electrolytes that are incompatible with microbial growth, preventing direct coupling of electrochemical formate production with biological conversion. Here, we developed a biocompatible CO 2 electrolysis configuration that uses fluidized particles of Sn, Bi, and In as electrocatalysts to enhance CO□-to-formate conversion while supporting microbial utilization in the same chamber. The fluidized configuration enabled high formate production rates up to 0.24 mmol h□¹ cm□² with Faradaic efficiencies of 86–92%, representing a two-fold improvement over static electrodes. The system also achieved a carbon conversion efficiency of 42%, approaching the theoretical limit for co-generation of formate and bicarbonate. Importantly, electrolysis was performed in a biocompatible medium that supported direct in situ cultivation of Cupriavidus necator within the cathode chamber using only electricity and CO 2 /O 2 as fed substrates. C. necator continuously consumed electro-generated formate for 5-6 days under aerobic conditions, demonstrating integrated CO 2 -to-biomass conversion. This work establishes a fluidized electrocatalytic platform for simultaneous electrosynthesis and microbial upgrading in a single reactor, providing a scalable strategy for renewable carbon fixation and sustainable biomanufacturing. TOC GRAPHIC
papers.authors: Zakaria B, Lanzilotti A, Sundstrom E, Tejedor-Sanz S.

papers.title: Machine learning guided design of strong transcriptional activation domains
papers.abstract: Summary Artificial intelligence has accelerated the design of structured proteins, but it remains difficult to design functional intrinsically disordered proteins because of weak structural constraints and poorly defined sequence-to-function relationships 1 . Activation domains (ADs), transcription factor regions that recruit coactivators, are an excellent test case for the de novo design of intrinsically disordered sequences. ADs are one of the oldest groups of functional intrinsically disordered sequences 2 and designed ADs have applications in synthetic biology, biotechnology, and agriculture. We computationally generated 500,000 candidate sequences that resembled known ADs and predicted AD function with extant machine learning models, including three neural networks. From high-scoring sequences, we selected 18,750 for experimental validation in yeast. Surprisingly, >90% of the 16,770 well-measured sequences function as ADs. Sequences predicted to be active by multiple models were stronger, motivating development of a fast and accurate consensus AD predictor, MADRIGAL. A number of our designed ADs retain functionality across fungi, plants, and human cells. This work illustrates a generalizable paradigm for incorporating sequence-to-function models into the design loop to efficiently generate functional intrinsically disordered sequences.
papers.authors: Zintel MA, LeBlanc CJ, Kotha SR, Soriano M, Bansal RJ, Aguilera D, Majidi T, Ornelas I, Kirkpatrick LD, Udupa A, Hu G, Agarwal P, Lam AWY, Nuñez JK, Shih PM, Sozzani R, Strader LC, Staller MV.

papers.title: Research progress in the production, purification, and applications of long single-stranded DNA.
papers.abstract: Long single-stranded DNA (long ssDNA) plays important roles in cutting-edge fields such as DNA origami, gene therapy, and synthetic biology. However, the production, preparation, and purification of long ssDNA remain technically challenging. This review systematically summarizes current strategies for long ssDNA production and preparation, including phage-E. coli-based biological production, template-dependent enzymatic amplification, and viral-vector-based generation of ssDNA genomes. CRISPR-Cas-assisted approaches are discussed separately as complementary tools for post-synthetic processing, sequence-selective cleavage, enrichment, and quality control, whereas other enzymatic approaches are considered for post-synthetic strand conversion. We compare the characteristics and limitations of these production and preparation strategies, discuss purification techniques for long ssDNA, and summarize its applications in DNA origami nanotechnology and gene therapy. This review comprehensively synthesizes the bottlenecks in long ssDNA production, preparation, and purification, and outlines further development trends. We highlight template-independent de novo enzymatic DNA synthesis, automated DNA manufacturing, synthetic biology-based production systems, and AI-assisted sequence optimization. These developments are expected to accelerate the transition of long ssDNA technologies from laboratory research toward scalable manufacturing and practical applications.
papers.authors: Wang X, Wu Y, Zhang X, Du Y, Liu N, Wang Z, Zhang H, Gao X, Zheng A.

papers.title: Systematic metabolic engineering for trans-aconitic acid production in Aspergillus niger .
papers.abstract: Trans-aconitate (TAA) is a valuable bio-based chemical for nematicides and polymer synthesis. We repurposed the industrial citrate producer Aspergillus niger for efficient TAA biosynthesis. Heterologous AexA enabled extracellular aconitate export. However, overexpressing aconitases from various sources, targeted to the cytoplasm or mitochondria, failed to increase titers. Although mitochondria proved the optimal site for cis-aconitate accumulation, the bottleneck likely persisted due to thermodynamic constraints. To overcome this, we designed a push-pull strategy: a pull module using mitochondrial MttA to export cis-aconitate to the cytosol, where TbrA isomerizes it to TAA, coupled with a push module enhancing cytosolic acetyl-CoA via the phosphoketolase pathway. Multicopy tbrA expression was critical. The final strain produced 34.30 g/L total aconitate (>90% TAA) in a 5-L bioreactor within 6 days. This work highlights a compartmentalized push-pull strategy exploiting mitochondrial-cytosolic organization to convert a citrate chassis into a high-yield TAA cell factory.
papers.authors: Wang S, He J, Li W, Cui C, Liu J, Liu H.

papers.title: Additive Manufacturing of Metabolically Active Living Materials with Enhanced Biocontainment.
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing of engineered living materials (ELMs) enables the spatial patterning of living cells or organisms within three-dimensional (3D) polymer matrices. However, effective biocontainment, defined as the ability to retain cells within 3D-printed matrices during the application period, remains a key limitation for ELMs requiring physical confinement. While synthetic biology provides cell-specific biocontainment strategies, materials-based approaches can enable generic cell retention capabilities. Therefore, we applied a materials-based strategy that combines pre-printing formulation development and post-printing processing to increase the retention of yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae in Pluronic F127-bisurethane methacrylate (F127-BUM) hydrogels. F127-BUM precursor solutions were formulated with the comonomers methacrylic acid (MAA) and/or 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate (DMAEMA), extrusion-printed, UV-cross-linked, and immersed in 70 vol % ethanol for 60 or 300 s before cultivation. Comonomer addition preserved dimensional fidelity, thermoresponsiveness, and shear-thinning behavior for 3D printing. After immobilization and cross-linking, DMAEMA and higher concentrations of MAA considerably reduced yeast viability, whereas a 70-80% viability was observed for 0.03 and 0.06 mol L-1 MAA. With 0.06 mol L-1 MAA and 300 s ethanol immersion, the yeast retention time reached 98 ± 12 h, which was approximately 48% longer than that of the correspondingly treated F127-BUM-only control and represented about a 465% increase relative to the untreated F127-BUM-only control. After ethanol immersion, a peripheral growth-free zone developed around a metabolically active core, enhancing cell retention and contributing to delayed cell escape. The selected MAA-containing ELMs remained metabolically active and showed nearly 38% higher apparent glucose-to-ethanol conversion than treated F127-BUM-only controls. The suspension cultures fermented faster and achieved higher yield. Our method achieved enhanced biocontainment, with an operational window of about 4-5 days. In conclusion, we demonstrate that combining pre-printing and post-printing processes can enhance biocontainment for different ELM applications. We suggest the integration of this method with synthetic-biology strategies to further extend biocontainment duration for metabolically active living materials.
papers.authors: Hamacek HSDR, Daily S, Le L, Khalid S, Spuul P, Lahtvee PJ, Nelson A, Kumar R.

papers.title: Anthocyanin Biosynthesis, Multilayered Regulation, and Biotechnological Applications in Fruits.
papers.abstract: Anthocyanins are water-soluble flavonoid pigments that confer vivid coloration to fruits and provide multiple health benefits. Here, we critically review recent advances in the structural diversity, biosynthetic pathways, and multilayered regulation of fruit anthocyanins. We summarize the enzymatic and postsynthetic modifications that determine pigment stability, and examine the MYB-bHLH-WD40 (MBW) complex, its interplay with NAC, WRKY, ERF, and bZIP factors, and the roles of epigenetic and post-translational controls. Hormonal, environmental, and nutrient signals are integrated into a unified model, emphasizing the contrasting regulatory logics of climacteric versus nonclimacteric fruits and the tissue specificity of peel- vs flesh-localized pigmentation. We evaluate biotechnological strategies, including CRISPR-based precision breeding, microbial cell factories, and plant metabolic engineering, highlighting both transformative potential and translational bottlenecks. Finally, we propose future directions for translating fundamental knowledge into anthocyanin-enriched fruits and sustainable production systems for the food and health industries.
papers.authors: Zhu J, Wu Y, Chen X, Li X, Zhang G, Xu S, Lin Y, Wu X, Li Y, Zheng B, Ni J, Shi K, Cui F, Wang J.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

papers.title: Automated Quenching and Extraction for High-Precision Metabolomics Uncovers Distinct Metabolome Trajectories across Escherichia coli Lineages.
papers.abstract: Quantitative microbial metabolomics requires rapid quenching and highly standardized extraction, yet these pre-analytical steps remain labor-intensive and difficult to reproduce, limiting time-resolved intracellular measurements under controlled bioreactor cultivation. Here, we present an integrated robotic platform that couples parallel fermenter operation with circulation-based sampling, immediate cold-alcohol quenching, automated refrigerated centrifugation, interface-aware supernatant removal, and solvent extraction with controlled heating and mixing, followed by plate-based storage for liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). To benchmark the precision of the automated preparation module, we compared repeated LC-MS/MS measurements of a single extract with measurements of independently processed samples subjected to post-quench automated harvesting, extraction, and transfer. The analysis was restricted to 76 analytes consistently detected in all replicates of both datasets. The mean coefficients of variation increased from 6.92% for repeated LC-MS/MS measurements to 8.82% for automated preparation, corresponding to a modest increase of 1.90 percentage points. These results indicate that post-quench automated preparation introduces a small but measurable additional source of variability while maintaining mean analytical variation below 10%. We then performed time-course endo- and exometabolomics across four widely used Escherichia coli lineages (BW25113, BL21(DE3), W, and C). Principal component analysis resolved strain-specific trajectories throughout batch growth and revealed strain-specific metabolic phenotypes, including coordinated accumulation of sugar phosphates and 2-C-methyl-d-erythritol 4-phosphate (MEP) pathway intermediates in strain C, and comparatively high intracellular pools of branched-chain amino acids in strain W. This platform enables standardized and traceable automated preparation for dense, time-resolved metabolomics and provides directly measurable phenotypes for host selection and metabolic engineering.
papers.authors: Tanaka K, Bamba T, Takenaka M, Hori Y, Yoshida T, Matsuda M, Kondo A, Hayakawa Y, Hasunuma T.

papers.title: Clustered Regularly Interspaced Palindromic Repeats-Cas Genome-Editing Systems in Filamentous Fungi: Current Tools, Optimization Strategies, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Filamentous fungi are important microbial cell factories for producing antibiotics, organic acids, enzymes, and other valuable products, with broad applications in food, agriculture, and medicine. However, inefficient and imprecise genome editing remains a major bottleneck limiting rational strain engineering. This review summarizes major genome-editing tools in filamentous fungi, including Cre-loxP, TALENs, and CRISPR-Cas systems, with emphasis on their mechanisms, advantages, and limitations. We highlight CRISPR-Cas9 as the predominant platform and discuss optimization strategies involving sgRNA design, engineered Cas9 variants, promoter engineering, AMA1-based replicative plasmids, and ribonucleoprotein delivery. Emerging technologies, including base editing, prime editing, Cas12a, and Mad7, are also discussed for their potential to broaden editing capabilities. Finally, we outline future perspectives focusing on extending the application of existing genome-editing systems in filamentous fungi and discovering novel genome-editing tools from large-scale omics data sets. This review will accelerate the development of filamentous fungi as versatile platforms for biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: Du R, Wang W, Xie J, Li Y, Wu N, Xu Q.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

papers.title: Coiled Coils as a Programmable Platform for Computational Biosensor Design.
papers.abstract: Coiled coils are a versatile class of α-helical protein motifs characterized by recurring sequence patterns that direct their assembly into defined oligomeric bundles and underpin a wide range of biological functions. The well-established sequence-structure relationships governing coiled-coil formation enable predictive control over stability, specificity, and oligomerization state, making them attractive and chemically tractable building blocks for biosensor design in applications ranging from single-molecule detection to synthetic biochemical circuits and functional nanomaterials. After revisiting the theoretical foundations of coiled-coil architecture, this review outlines strategies to engineer programmable binding interfaces that can be rationally tuned to generate orthogonal, high-affinity interaction pairs, enabling flexible and modular biosensor platforms. Particular emphasis is placed on recent advances in computational and data-driven design approaches, including machine-learning and AI-based strategies, alongside established rational and empirical methods for coiled-coil construction. These complementary design principles underpin the development of coiled-coil-based biosensors and are discussed together with selected application examples to illustrate how engineered coiled-coil interactions support sensitive and specific molecular recognition as well as switchable control in synthetic biology and chemical biology. Overall, this review highlights coiled coils as programmable, stable, and highly designable scaffolds at the interface of molecular engineering, computation, and chemical biology.
papers.authors: Kluge P, Shabani F, Gemming S, Künze G.
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology

papers.title: Comprehensive O-Phosphoproteomic Landscape of Corynebacterium glutamicum.
papers.abstract: Corynebacterium glutamicum serves as a pivotal industrial platform organism, accounting for an annual global amino acid output of several million tons. Elucidating its adaptive mechanisms under diverse environmental perturbations during high-density fermentation is fundamental to advanced metabolic engineering and strain optimization. Despite the critical role of protein phosphorylation in cellular adaptation, the phosphoproteome of C. glutamicum remains largely unexplored. With fewer than 50 phosphoproteins currently identified, this knowledge gap hinders the elucidation of regulatory networks underlying industrial stress tolerance. In this study, we implemented a highly robust workflow for O-phosphopeptides enrichment utilizing titanium-based immobilized metal affinity chromatography (Ti-IMAC). By integrating an offline reversed-phase prefractionation strategy and a combination of Electron-Transfer/Higher-Energy Collision Dissociation (EThcD) and Higher-Energy Collision Dissociation (HCD) mass spectrometry fragmentation techniques, we established the most comprehensive phosphoproteomic data set for this species to our knowledge. We identified 874 phosphoproteins and 2,137 phosphorylation sites, representing a more than 20-fold increase over existing literature. Furthermore, we delineated the dynamic phosphoproteome under nitrogen starvation, uncovering novel site-specific phosphorylation events on key proteins such as OdhI (Ser2/Thr7), FtsZ (Thr387), and EF-G (Thr48). This study provides a high-quality, global phosphoprotein resource, that elucidates the molecular insights into the orchestration of environmental adaptation and metabolic regulation of C. glutamicum.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Han M, Qin P, Zhang W, Liu Q, Cao Q, Sun J.

papers.title: Cytoskeletal and Extracellular Factors Regulating Stem Cell Differentiation: Mechanisms, Tools, and Emerging Applications.
papers.abstract: Stem cell lineage determination is governed not only by biochemical cues but also by the organization and force-generating state of the cytoskeleton, which integrates extracellular mechanical cues into transcriptional and epigenetic responses. Cytoskeletal organization and remodeling play essential roles in stem cell fate determination, as well as other relevant biological processes including development, tissue regeneration, and disease progression. In this review, we first outline the different types of cytoskeletal structures-actin filaments, microtubules, and intermediate filaments-and their coordinated roles in cell shape, polarity, and contractility. We then discuss how extracellular cues, including matrix stiffness, geometry, topography, shear, stretch, and compression remodel cytoskeletal distribution and adhesion dynamics to affect stem cell lineage commitment.
