We highlight matrix viscoelasticity and stress relaxation as time-dependent mechanical regulators that modulate traction transmission, focal adhesion, and cytoskeletal tension, thereby directing stem cell differentiation outcomes beyond stiffness alone. We next discuss mechanotransduction pathways, such as RhoA/ROCK-mediated contractility, Wnt/β-catenin, Piezo1/Piezo2, and YAP/TAZ nuclear shuttling, which couple cytoskeletal forces to gene regulation. We further summarize quantitative approaches to measure cell molecular forces, including traction force microscopy, molecular tension sensors, and advanced live-cell imaging platforms. Finally, we discuss the translational potential of cytoskeleton-informed design principles in regenerative medicine, where they can be leveraged to improve stem cell biomanufacturing, optimize tunable biomaterials, and develop more predictive mechanopathology models. Together, these developments will establish cytoskeletal organization as a controllable, engineerable lever for directing stem cell fate and enabling functional tissue formation.
papers.authors: Wang S, Caron J, Zhai S, Wang B, Mak M.

papers.title: Dual Constraints of Microbial Carbon Use Efficiency and Mineral Protection Govern Necromass Accrual.
papers.abstract: Increasing soil organic carbon (SOC), central to food security and climate mitigation, is increasingly recognized as being mediated by microbial necromass C (MNC) accrual. However, how microbial production and mineral preservation jointly govern MNC accrual under contrasting resource conditions remains unclear. Here, we analyzed soils from 14 long-term fertilization experiments (up to 47 years) to assess how edaphic and climatic conditions regulate the response of MNC accrual to manure (M) and non-manure (NM) fertilization treatments. We found that the primary constraints on MNC accrual varied with resource availability, with microbial production under resource-limited conditions and mineral preservation under resource-abundant conditions. Under resource-limited conditions, M treatments increased MNC by up to 122%, with changes tightly coupled to SOC gains. This accrual was associated with increases in dissolved organic C and microbial C use efficiency, indicating a production-constrained pathway in which manure inputs alleviate substrate limitation and promote microbial C allocation toward biomass production and necromass formation. Conversely, under resource-abundant conditions, MNC responses to fertilization were weaker (+56%) and uncoupled from SOC gains. Instead, MNC accrual was primarily associated with mineral protection capacity (e.g., Fe and Al oxides), consistent with a preservation-constrained pathway. Overall, microbial processing and mineral preservation represent context-dependent constraints on MNC accrual under contrasting resource conditions. These findings underscore the importance of resource context for site-specific C management and for understanding soil C dynamics under global change.
papers.authors: Xiao Q, Yao B, Qiu T, Li G, Li X, Huang Y, Wang J, Wu L, Xu M, Fang L, Liang C, Kuzyakov Y, Zhang W.

papers.title: Electron Transfer at Microbe-Mineral Interfaces: From Molecular Mechanisms to Ecosystem-Scale Biogeochemical Cycling and Remediation.
papers.abstract: Microbe-mineral electron transfer (MMET) drives key microbial processes and biogeochemical cycling, but linking these microscopic interactions to ecosystem-scale dynamics remains a major challenge. MMET couples intracellular metabolism to extracellular mineral transformations. The resulting changes in mineral redox state and reactivity can, in turn, influence microbial energy conservation and metabolism. MMET flux could therefore provide a quantitative link between nanometer-scale electron exchange and larger-scale biogeochemical processes. In energy-limited and contaminated environments, electroactive microorganisms may transfer electrons to or acquire electrons from redox-active minerals, depending on their metabolic capabilities and local redox conditions. These interactions can support energy conservation, mitigate toxic stress, and generate localized zones of high biogeochemical activity. As their effects accumulate across space and time, microscale electron transfer may influence ecosystem-scale elemental cycling, microbial community succession, organic carbon stabilization, and contaminant fate. Building on established modeling approaches, we suggest that integrating individual-based models (IBMs) with genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) could translate spatially heterogeneous, genome-informed microbial responses into collective MMET fluxes across scales while accounting for key thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. More broadly, progress requires characterizing electroactive microbial diversity and mechanisms, engineering microbe-mineral interfaces through computational design and synthetic biology, and translating MMET principles into scalable environmental applications.
papers.authors: Liu J, Wu Z, Feng X, Shi L, Rosso KM.

papers.title: End-to-End Biomanufacturing of Extracellular Vesicles.
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as next-generation, multispecific, and multifunctional agents across medicine, biotechnology, veterinary science, cosmetics, and nutrition. Their delivery efficiency of therapeutic cargo surpasses that of conventional carriers, and their capacity to simultaneously transport internal cargo and activate multiple recipient cells gives them a therapeutic versatility that no other platform can match. Translating this potential into real-world products depends on integrating process design with product characterization, a link that has not yet been systematically established for EV manufacturing. The functionality of an EV is inseparable from how it is made. EV composition is shaped at every stage of production, from the biology of the producer cell, to upstream microenvironmental stressors, to the operational parameters of downstream isolation and purification. Each of these variables influences the final product quality and functionality, which means that process design is, in effect, product design. While many guidelines, including minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV) and quality by design (QbD), have been reported, they operate at different levels: MISEV ensures the validity of EV characterization, whereas QbD defines how a manufacturer designs, controls, and releases a product. Currently, however, there is no link between them to provide an integrative framework. This manuscript, therefore reviews and proposes a framework for context-of-use-dependent EV biomanufacturing, in which biomanufacturing and bioprocessing parameters are deliberately matched to the intended application. By linking specific process conditions to resultant EV characteristics, and by fine-tuning upstream and downstream operations accordingly, bespoke EVs can be produced for defined therapeutic, diagnostic, or industrial purposes rather than made as a single generic product. Together, this work offers essential guidance for producing EVs at scale and for designing end-to-end bioprocesses that can be tailored to the diverse needs of future EV-based products.
papers.authors: Lei Q, Zhang P, Cameau E, Guterstam P, Chrzanowski W, Donati D.

papers.title: EPOTF-Enabled Scalable Production of Structurally Intact Lemon-Derived Extracellular Vesicles with Enhanced Bioactivity.
papers.abstract: Lemon-derived extracellular vesicles (LDEVs) have attracted increasing attention as promising bioactive nanovesicles for cosmetic and skin engineering applications owing to their biocompatibility, bioactive cargo, and skin-friendly lipid bilayer structure. However, the lack of standardized purification methods and limited scalability remain critical bottlenecks for the practical application and industrial translation of LDEVs. In this study, we developed an electrophoretic oscillation-assisted tangential flow filtration (EPOTF) platform using a SiNx membrane nanofilter for the scalable and high-purity purification of structurally intact LDEVs. The EPOTF process effectively suppressed membrane cake formation and membrane fouling, enabling stable size-selective purification under large-volume conditions. EPOTF-purified LDEVs exhibited stable physicochemical characteristics, high recovery yield, and excellent batch-to-batch reproducibility. Cryo-TEM analysis confirmed preservation of a distinct lipid bilayer structure and near-ideal spherical morphology with low spherical deviation, indicating minimal structural damage during purification. Furthermore, EPOTF-purified LDEVs significantly enhanced hydration, antioxidant activity, skin barrier recovery, and anti-inflammatory responses in an ex vivo human skin explant model. Taken together, these findings establish EPOTF as a robust and scalable purification platform for the biomanufacturing of high-quality LDEVs, with strong potential for cosmetic and skin-engineering applications.
papers.authors: Ko M, Jung H, Shin K, Kim S, Lee KN, Lee YK, Jeong S, Do YR.

papers.title: Expression of Human CYP2D6 in Artificial Cells Based on Polymer-Lipid Hybrid Vesicles.
papers.abstract: Artificial cells with the ability to express functional, biomedically relevant enzymes have long been a goal in the field of bottom-up synthetic biology. Here, we demonstrate the expression of human cytochrome P450 2D6 (CYP2D6) within the lumen of giant hybrid vesicle-based artificial cells using a cell-free protein expression system based on the protozoan Leishmania tarentolae. The vesicle membranes comprise 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine and amphiphilic block copolymers containing poly(cholesteryl methacrylate-co-butyl methacrylate) with either poly(galactose methacrylate) (pGalacMA) or poly(carboxyethyl acrylate) as the hydrophilic block. The amount and composition of the block copolymer incorporated into the giant hybrid vesicle membrane altered the artificial cells' ability to support functional protein expression, likely through changes in membrane properties. In particular, giant hybrid vesicles containing pGalacMA supported production of enzymatically active CYP2D6. Overall, the reported approach advances the development of artificial cells capable of producing functional, biomedically relevant enzymes. Further, the effort highlights complex interplay between polymer properties and performance of biological components in the functional complexity achievable in polymer-lipid hybrid vesicles.
papers.authors: Dahl S, De Dios Andres P, Beaune G, Timonen JVI, Behrendorff J, Alexandrov K, Johnston W, Städler B.
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology

papers.title: Fecal Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Early Islet Autoimmunity: Limited Prognostic Value or an Incomplete Measure of Microbial Production?
papers.authors: Igudesman D.

papers.title: Functional Characterization and Application of Yarrowia lipolytica YlYxc1 for Enhanced Production of Sphingoid Bases.
papers.abstract: Long-chain bases (LCBs; sphingoid bases), derived from ceramide metabolism, are valuable sphingolipid intermediates for industrial applications. Here, we functionally characterized a putative ceramidase from Yarrowia lipolytica (YlYxc1) and evaluated its potential to enhance LCB production. YlYxc1 contains a conserved alkaline ceramidase motif with seven transmembrane helices and shares ~42% amino acid identity with Saccharomyces cerevisiae alkaline ceramidases ScYpc1 and ScYdc1. Despite lacking a canonical ER retention motif, YlYxc1 localized to the ER membrane. Deletion of YlYXC1 caused no major growth or lipid profile changes. Heterologous overexpression of YlYXC1 in S. cerevisiae wild-type and Scypc1Δydc1Δ strains increased phytosphingosine (PHS) production over dihydrosphingosine (DHS), mimicking ScYPC1 overexpression. In vitro activity assays using microsomal fractions from Scypc1Δydc1Δ cells expressing YlYXC1 revealed preferential hydrolysis of phytoceramide with an alkaline pH optimum. Furthermore, YlYXC1 expression in an engineered Y. lipolytica strain expressing heterologous acetyltransferases WcSLI1 and WcATF2 remarkably enhanced acetylated LCB production. Multi-copy integration of YlYXC1 into the Ylsur2Δsld1Δ strain also increased the secretory production of non-acetylated DHS. These findings establish YlYxc1 as a promising metabolic engineering target for producing value-added LCBs for pharmaceutical and cosmeceutical applications.
papers.authors: Shin SH, Jeon EJ, Moon HY, Go GY, Yoo YS, Lee JK, Jeon CO, Kang HA.

papers.title: Genetic Engineering Efforts to Generate Chlamydomonas Strains for Large-Scale Biomolecule Production.
papers.abstract: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is an established model microalga. Its easy manipulation, metabolic flexibility and tractable genomes allowed researchers to investigate fundamental processes such as photosynthesis using genetic studies for decades. Chlamydomonas is not naturally rich in lipids or pigments compared to industrially relevant microalgae. However, we highlight how its biotechnological potential relies on advanced genetic and metabolic engineering strategies, now possible due to the availability of extensive toolbox and synthetic biology platforms, which can improve industrial traits and allow to produce a variety of biomolecules of biotechnological interest. We provide examples of biomolecule production (terpenoids and recombinant proteins), and show that productivities (mg/L) are in the same range or could even be higher than those reached in other photosynthetic chassis (e.g., cyanobacteria or mosses). We point out that despite these achievements, the industrial implementation of C. reinhardtii is still lacking. Further technological advancements as well as clear international regulations and social acceptance are fundamental to reach the full potential of this microalga.
papers.authors: Inturri S, Rouhier N, Remacle C.

papers.title: Harnessing Biotechnology for the Development of Brazzein as a Next-Generation Sweetener.
papers.abstract: Sugar reduction has emerged as a major direction in the food industry, increasing the need to reduce sucrose while maintaining desirable sweetness quality. Brazzein, a high-intensity sweet protein, has attracted considerable interest. Depending on the sucrose reference concentration, its sweetness potency ranges from 500 to 2000 times that of sucrose, while the minor form is approximately twice as sweet as the major form. This review summarizes the structure-activity relationships of brazzein, its performance across food matrices, and synergistic blending effects with other sweeteners. Because brazzein occurs only in trace amounts in fruit, conventional plant extraction cannot support stable, scalable supply. Recent advances in microbial production are reviewed, including host selection, expression and folding control, secretion engineering, fermentation optimization, and downstream processing. Current production strategies are critically compared, with emphasis on product consistency, production cost, and scale-up challenges.
papers.authors: Wan JY, Wang YF, Yang DD, Wu XY, Liu H, Xu Q.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

papers.title: Living Spatially Organized Hybrid Condensates for Efficient Light-Driven CO2-to-Chemical Conversion.
papers.abstract: Light-driven CO2-to-chemical conversion presents a sustainable route for biomanufacturing, yet the performance of photosynthetic biohybrid systems remains fundamentally constrained by disorganized biotic-abiotic interfaces, which result in inefficient photoelectron transfer, low carbon production, and substantial cellular toxicity. Here, we report a spatially organized intracellular biohybrid system that enables the light-powered conversion of CO2 to 2,3-butanediol inEscherichia coli. Inspired by the algal pyrenoid, we constructed a TiO2/RuBisCO hybrid condensate (TRHC) by integrating protein liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) with in situ biomimetic mineralization. This spatially defined condensate physically clusters light-harvesting and carbon-fixing modules, thereby facilitating direct photoelectron transfer and contributing to improved long-term cellular robustness under continuous illumination. The TRHC achieved an apparent quantum yield of 12.4% and reduced the light-induced cellular mortality by 64%. By providing a robust photoelectron supply for CO2 assimilation, the integrated system attains a 2,3-butanediol yield of 1.38 mol/mol from the consumed glucose. Moreover, under illuminated fed-batch fermentation, the platform maintains sustained biosynthetic activity over 5 days, producing 62.11 g/L of 2,3-butanediol. This LLPS-guided strategy offers a generalizable framework for engineering efficient biotic-abiotic interfaces in solar-driven biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: Li J, Zhang J, Yu Z, Zhang Z, Chen H, Shen J, Liu Y, Zhang Z, Wang L, Chen X, Zhong C.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

papers.title: NanoBlocks: Creating Genetically Encoded Protein Switches Using Competitive Binding.
papers.abstract: Many regulatory mechanisms function by changing a molecule's conformation such that it is switched between active and inactive states. Engineering macromolecules such as proteins to show robust conformational changes in response to arbitrary, well-defined molecular stimuli is of great interest in fields such as synthetic biology and nanoscale engineering, because it allows the development of "smart" molecular tools. We present a strategy that can convert "simple" affinity binders such as nanobodies into protein switches that undergo clear structural rearrangements in response to their innate targets, by introducing a peptide that competes for the binding site. We demonstrate proof-of-concept implementations of this "NanoBlock" design by developing genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors based on two entirely different binder frameworks, the ALFA nanobody and the PDZ domain of Erbin. We show that our design allows the construction of well-performing protein switches that can reliably detect their targets in vitro, in mammalian cells, as part of fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) experiments, and that also generalizes to the creation of stimulus-responsive enzymes via the integration of a bioluminescent readout. We furthermore develop a theoretical model that rationalizes the observations and provides insight into the underlying molecular mechanisms. Overall, our strategy expands the possibilities to create "smart" protein-based molecules and effectors.
papers.authors: Denis S, Van Deuren V, Frecot DI, Rothbauer U, Ismail S, Tebo AG, Dedecker P.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Microbial Community Composition of Fermented Soy Whey and Its Mechanism for Biotransformation of Soybean Isoflavones.
papers.abstract: Fermented soy whey (FSW), a traditional natural tofu coagulant, harbors complex microbial communities that drive soy-protein coagulation via organic-acid secretion and enhance the bioavailability of soybean isoflavones, conferring desirable flavor characteristics and health-beneficial bioactivities. However, several critical knowledge gaps restrict its scaled-up industrial deployment. The dynamic regulatory connections between microbial community temporal succession and metabolite biosynthesis during spontaneous FSW fermentation have not been fully deciphered. Interspecies interactions inside highly heterogeneous microbial consortia remain ambiguous, and the whole-fermentation system is exceptionally sensitive to fluctuating environmental conditions. This review synthesizes prior literature together with cutting-edge multi-omics datasets to systematically dissect the temporal dynamics of FSW microbial ecosystems. Enzymatic mechanistic analysis delineates key catalytic and metabolic pathways responsible for transforming soy isoflavone glucosides into aglycones and subsequent bioactive derivatives. We critically evaluate promising technical strategies, covering targeted synthetic-biology modification, integrated intelligent control systems, artificial intelligence, and digital-twin modeling, to advance the transition from experience-driven spontaneous fermentation to precision manufacturing. Selective manipulation of functional microbes or rate-limiting catalytic enzymes enables directional enrichment of high-activity isoflavone metabolites. This framework mitigates bioavailability drawbacks of native isoflavones and builds solid scientific foundations for zero-waste valorization of soy-processing by-products, circular food manufacturing, and innovative high-value-added functional-food development.
papers.authors: Li Z, Yan J, Zhang Z, Deng Y.
papers.journal: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety

papers.title: Redirecting Metabolic Flux to Minimize By-Product Formation Enables Efficient De Novo Biosynthesis of Chlorogenic Acid in Escherichia coli.
papers.abstract: Chlorogenic acid (CGA) is an important natural hydroxycinnamic acid ester with diverse biological activities, including antioxidant, antibacterial, and potential antitumor properties. However, efficient microbial titer of CGA remains challenging because of insufficient hydroxylation efficiency, by-product accumulation, and limited host tolerance. Herein, an efficient and sustainable microbial platform for de novo CGA biosynthesis was constructed in Escherichia coli. Enhancement of the NAD(H) biosynthetic pathway increased intracellular reducing power and increased hydroxylation efficiency. A synergistic hydroxylation module consisting of the p-coumarate 3-hydroxylase from Saccharothrix espanaensis (SeC3H) and the flavin reductase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PaHpaC)was further introduced to promote the conversion of p-coumaric acid (pCA) to caffeic acid (CA) and redirect metabolic flux toward CGA biosynthesis. Rational engineering of 4-coumarate-CoA ligase from Arabidopsis thaliana (At4CL) increased substrate selectivity and decreased the formation of the major by-product p-coumaroylquinic acid (pCQA). In addition, transcriptomic analysis identified lsrG, a gene associated with the AI-2 quorum-sensing system, as a beneficial target whose overexpression further enhanced CGA titer. The final engineered strain produced 7220.3 mg/L CGA in a 50 L fed-batch fermentation. The strategies developed herein may provide an effective metabolic engineering framework for the sustainable biosynthesis of CGA and other aromatic natural products.
papers.authors: Su Y, Chen Q, Chen J, Zhang S, Yu Y, Qin Z, Zeng W, Zhou J.

papers.title: SecAntiGami: A Secondary-Antibody-Inspired RNA Origami for Qualitative Aptamer Validation.
papers.abstract: RNA aptamers are short, single-stranded RNA molecules that fold into specific three-dimensional structures and selectively bind molecular targets. Despite applications in therapeutics, diagnostics, and biosensing, tools for aptamer validation remain scarce compared to well-established pipelines for other biomolecular binders such as antibodies. Here, we introduce SecAntiGami─a secondary-antibody-inspired RNA origami─as a modular tool for signal enhancement and aptamer characterization. SecAntiGami binds aptamers of interest through programmable kissing-loop interactions and carries a fluorescent aptamer for visualization. It amplifies aptamer-dependent size increases in dynamic light scattering assays and enables fluorescence-based aptamer localization. We rationally design three different variants of a biotin-binding aptamer and use SecAntiGami to demonstrate that all of them retain their functionality, enabling efficient integration of aptamers into RNA origami structures. SecAntiGami serves as a versatile tool for qualitative aptamer validation for synthetic biology, structural RNA nanotechnology, RNA therapeutics, and diagnostics.
papers.authors: Frey LS, Verstraeten W, Tran MP, Venkert D, Monari L, Geary C, Göpfrich K.

papers.title: SeqSol-FECS: An Integrated Deep Learning and Structural Modeling Framework for Protein Solubility Engineering.
papers.abstract: Escherichia coli is widely used as a workhorse for heterologous protein expression. However, insoluble protein expression is frequently encountered. The mechanisms underlying protein solubility remain incompletely understood, limiting the effectiveness of current protein solubility engineering strategies. Here, SeqSol, a sequence-level solubility prediction model capable of prioritizing single-amino-acid substitutions through WT-mutant rescoring, was developed using 71,425 proteins. SeqSol achieved an accuracy of 75.8% and an AUC of 0.840 on an independent test set and correctly identified experimentally validated solubility-enhancing mutations from diverse proteins. To minimize the risk of activity loss, candidate mutation sites were prioritized according to conformational flexibility, relative solvent accessibility, and evolutionary conservation before solubility engineering. Using only 30 experimentally tested mutations, the resulting SeqSol-FECS framework increased the solubility of two industrial enzymes from 56.18% and 10.53% to over 95%, respectively, while maintaining their specific activities. SeqSol-FECS provides an efficient strategy for enzyme solubility engineering and biomanufacturing applications.
papers.authors: Guo Q, Zhou XT, Zhou R, Fang ZR, Shen Q, Xue YP, Zheng YG.

papers.title: STRATUM-structured framework for reporting, assessment, and translational utility of metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Background Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) enables broad, untargeted detection of pathogens and microbial signals across complex sample types. However, the diversity of operational contexts, from regulatory enforcement to exploratory discovery, challenges the defining of analytical or interpretive standards appropriate across all applications. Variability in laboratory practices, bioinformatic methods, and reporting conventions continues to limit consistency and decision-maker confidence in mNGS results. Objectives We introduce Structured Framework for Reporting, Assessment, and Translational Utility of Metagenomics (STRATUM), a use-case-stratified framework that aligns QA, metadata reporting, and interpretive standards with the consequence and intended use of metagenomic sequencing outputs. Methods STRATUM is organized around five representative biosurveillance use cases spanning public health, food safety, environmental monitoring, synthetic biology detection, and national security. A three-tier interpretive model calibrates analytical rigor, validation expectations, and reporting requirements to decision consequence; from high-consequence regulatory and clinical determinations (Tier 1), through operational surveillance (Tier 2), to exploratory and hypothesis-generating contexts (Tier 3). Results The framework provides graduated guidance across key domains including sample preparation, sequencing design, controls and contamination governance, reference database curation, bioinformatics reproducibility, and multi-factor signal validation. Cross-cutting principles include explicit documentation of evidentiary bases, transparency in database and pipeline provenance, and defined escalation pathways when results transition between interpretive tiers. Conclusion Realizing the operational potential of mNGS requires evidentiary standards responsive to decision context rather than fixed across applications. STRATUM offers a consequence-tiered model for quality and reporting in applied metagenomics, supporting reproducible, transparent, and defensible sequencing-based surveillance across public health and biodefense domains. Highlights Introduction of STRATUM, a consequence-tiered evidentiary framework for applied metagenomics. Structured calibration of analytical rigor and reporting standards to decision context. Cross-use-case guidance spanning surveillance, regulatory, and national security applications.
papers.authors: Russell JA, Keenum I, Jarvis K, Sanderson H, Sussman MD, Khanipov K, Lacirignola J, Xiao A, Phillips JM, Johns M, Ganesan B, Parsons C, Davis B, Sozhamannan S.

papers.title: Arbitrium crosstalk enables shared signaling among phages.
papers.abstract: The arbitrium system has transformed our understanding of phage biology by demonstrating that temperate phages communicate through extracellular peptides to coordinate lysis-lysogeny decisions. Initially considered a highly specific signaling pathway restricted to individual phage lineages, arbitrium communication has now been shown to extend beyond lineage boundaries in some phage systems. Recent studies have shown that non-cognate arbitrium peptides can interact with heterologous receptors, providing evidence of inter-phage crosstalk. Here, we synthesize current knowledge of the molecular basis of arbitrium signaling, the structural determinants of peptide-receptor specificity, and the potential ecological and evolutionary consequences of inter-phage communication. We suggest that arbitrium crosstalk may shape phage ecology by mediating competitive and potentially cooperative interactions within shared signaling environments. We also discuss its potential uses in engineered phage systems, synthetic biology, and microbiome engineering. Collectively, the available evidence broadens the concept of viral communication beyond lineage-specific signaling, while the ecological significance and practical applications of arbitrium crosstalk remain to be established.
papers.authors: Lomeli-Ortega CO, Balcázar JL.

papers.title: CultureBoost: an intelligent framework for retrospective analysis of commercial cell culture processes.
papers.abstract: Commercial-scale monoclonal antibody manufacturing requires stringent productivity control to maximize profitability. However, final productivity is frequently compromised by subtle process deviations beyond standard operating procedures, such as minor pH shifts, gas sparging variations, and nutrient consumption fluctuations. Although modern Industrial Internet of Things systems generate abundant inline and offline data, actionable process insights remain underexploited. To tackle the critical challenge of productivity fluctuations, identification of root causes is urgent. Therefore, this study proposes an intelligent retrospective data analysis framework for commercial-scale cell culture processes, integrating three core modules: inline data processing, offline data processing, and discriminative information extraction. It enables end-to-end automated historical data mining, quantifies factor contributions to batch quality variations, facilitates rapid potential root-cause identification with minimal data science expertise, and guides timely process optimization. Practical efficacy was demonstrated through two commercial-scale case studies manufacturing biosimilars to adalimumab (HS016) and trastuzumab (HS022), with data from over 30 batches collected per product. Critical factors possibly driving productivity declines were identified from early-batch data and successfully validated through targeted operational optimizations in subsequent runs. By converting latent process data into actionable insights, this scalable and operator-friendly framework provides a practical AI/ML-driven solution for continuous batch quality enhancement in GMP-regulated commercial biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: Chen H, Zhang S, Wan Y, Qu H.

papers.title: Engineering an Enzymatically Active Granular Matrix for On-Chip Modeling of Bone-Like Mineralization.
papers.abstract: Controlled biomineralization is central to engineering physiologically relevant hard-tissue models, yet achieving spatially organized, three-dimensional (3D) mineral deposition in microfluidic on-chip systems remains challenging. While cell-based bone-on-chip platforms offer biological complexity, they couple mineral initiation to matrix remodeling and paracrine signaling, complicating isolation of the earliest biochemical drivers of mineralization. Inspired by bottom-up synthetic biology, we engineered an enzymatically active granular matrix that recapitulates a key osteogenic function within a perfusable 3D microenvironment. Alkaline phosphatase (ALP), the key driver of native bone formation, was covalently conjugated to poly(ethylene glycol)-based (PEG) microgels via thiol-ene photochemistry, retaining over 90% of its initial activity after 24 h. These monodisperse microgels were assembled into a jammed, perfusable matrix on-chip, enabling independent control over enzyme loading and substrate delivery. The system supported in situ mineralization (24-48 h), yielding a calcium-deficient, poorly crystalline apatite-like phase characteristic of early-stage bone mineral. We demonstrate 3D localization of enzymatic activity to the granular matrix, which, coupled with interstitial perfusion, enabled mineral formation whose spatial distribution depended on the perfusion regime. This mechanistically defined, acellular platform provides a tunable foundation for investigating ALP-driven 3D mineralization and establishes a modular route toward hybrid biosynthetic models of (patho)physiological tissue mineralization.
papers.authors: Sanaei F, Zandieh D, Hofman D, Joziasse L, van den Beucken JJJP, Leeuwenburgh SCG, Diba M.

papers.title: Improving aerobic fermentation performance of glucose to gluconic acid production by cooperating with Gluconobacter oxydans and diatoms.
papers.abstract: Gluconic acid (GA) and its derivatives are widely demanded in construction, food and pharmaceutical industries. To mitigate food resource competition, the enzymatic hydrolysate of lignocellulosic agricultural waste (corncob) is regarded as a sustainable alternative feedstock for the GA bioproduction by Gluconobacter oxydans (G. oxydans). However, high‑solid hydrolysate causes dissolved‑oxygen deficiency due to increased broth viscosity, inhibiting the aerobic metabolism of this obligate aerobe. Herein, an economical diatom co‑cultivation system was constructed to supply oxygen in‑situ through photosynthesis. The neutralizer CaCO 3 neutralizes GA and generates CO 2 to partially sustain diatom photosynthesis, forming a chemically coupled interaction cycle (rather than strict mutualistic symbiosis). Experimental results demonstrated that diatom addition can effectively improve GA productivity. For corncob hydrolysate containing 100 g/L initial glucose, up to 32% higher GA yield was obtained. Such performance improvement is condition‑dependent, and limited enhancement was observed in high‑viscosity hydrolysate under high‑substrate loadings. This strategy partially mitigates oxygen‑transfer bottlenecks for lignocellulose‑derived GA production and provides a complementary low‑cost route for aerobic biomanufacturing of sugar acids from non‑food biomass.
papers.authors: Lu Z, Li F, Ouyang S, Zhang R, Zhou X.

papers.title: Prokaryotes bridging the lipid divide.
papers.abstract: The fundamental biochemical and stereochemical difference in how cell membrane lipids are built between Archaea on one side, and Bacteria and Eukarya on the other is known as the lipid divide. It is often assumed to translate in the impossibility of combining membranes of both types. It was established early when little sampling of the biodiversity was available. Since then, exceptions have been revealed and accumulated. Here, we review those exceptions and complement them with a broad survey, revealing diverse bacteria with mixed membrane-lipid features. Together with liposome assays and synthetic-biology experiments, studies on these organisms suggest that the lipid divide can be bridged. We conclude by discussing the evolutionary implications for LUCA, the origin of the prokaryotic domains and eukaryogenesis.
papers.authors: García-Domínguez R, Devos DP.

papers.title: Structure-guided engineering of medium- and long-chain triglycerides:​Fermentation-assisted biosynthesis, structural control and future perspective.
papers.abstract: Medium- and long-chain triglycerides (MLCTs) are triacylglycerols (TAGs) that have medium-chain fatty acids (MCFAs) and long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs) linked together on a single glycerol backbone. The positioning of the components, such as the MCFA-LCFA-MCFA (MLM-type) positioning, can affect lipase-mediated hydrolysis, release of fatty acids (FAs), absorption and metabolic behavior, however, structure-function relationships requires experimental validation. This review presents a comparison between chemical interesterification, lipase-catalyzed interesterification and fermentation-assisted biosynthesis of MLCT. Chemical interesterification will redistribute fatty acyl groups, but offers​ limited positional control, while lipase-catalyzed synthesis provides more positional selectivity but is susceptible to acyl migration. Fermentation-​assisted biosynthesis is a prospective approach that connects FA chain-length control, acyl-CoA supply and TAG assembly more strongly. However, there is currently more evidence that strongly supports the production of tailored FAs by microbes than demonstrated positional control of MLCT molecular species. Structural validation requires intact TAG molecular species analysis, positional analysis, and stereospecific analysis. An integrated framework combining applications of structural analysis, selective biocatalysis, fermentation optimization, metabolic engineering and functional evaluation is proposed.
papers.authors: Naseem A, Zhang L, Sun S.

papers.title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
papers.abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti-lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody-functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 10 3 -fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 10 3 -fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.
papers.authors: Chen Z, Hu W, Nie H, Zhang Y, Tang W, Yu Z, Cao J, Zhu X, Liu X, Chen M, Qimron U, Pich A, Peng H, Liu J.

papers.title: Beyond Cell Factory: In Vitro Biotransformation (ivBT): A Paradigm-Shifting Biomanufacturing Platform.
papers.abstract: The paradigm of industrial biomanufacturing is shifting rapidly. Microbial fermentation mediated by cell factories is the dominant platform of biomanufacturing and has a history of thousands of years. However, their inherent properties, such as self-proliferation, cellular complexity, maintenance, and bioenergetic limits, could prevent them from being the best winner of biomanufacturing, especially for biocommodities and bioenergy. In this book chapter, we introduce a new concept of in vitro biotransformation (ivBT) as an emerging biomanufacturing platform that can surpass microbial cell factory. The development of ivBT is driven by the urgent great needs of food security and a new carbon-neutral energy society in the future. In theory, ivBT can have the theoretical yield and very high volumetric productivity and could have low-cost biomanufacturing costs. Furthermore, we highlight several representative applications, such as artificial photosynthesis for CO 2 -to-starch synthesis, in vitro respiration that can produce hydrogen under anaerobic conditions and electricity under aerobic conditions, directed glycosidic bond rearrangement (i.e., ATP-free or low-ATP biotransformation of cellulose to starch), and healthy sugars. Industrial biomanufacturing of myo-inositol, D-tagatose, and cellulosic starch would wipe off any prejudice (e.g., costly enzymes and short lifetime) and demonstrate transformative potential of ivBT. ivBT would be a paradigm-shifting biomanufacturing platform because it is like a dimensional reduction attack that can simplify extremely complicated cell factories by decreasing their dimensions.
papers.authors: Song Z, Job Zhang YP.

papers.title: Deep mutational scanning of the GPCR rhodopsin reveals pleiotropic mutational effects and their roles in modulating receptor signaling.
papers.abstract: Biophysical pleiotropy, the phenomenon in which a mutation affects multiple protein properties, underlies many genetic diseases and shapes protein evolution, yet remains poorly understood, limiting synthetic biology and therapeutic development. Although extensively studied in soluble proteins, little is known about how pleiotropic effects shaped the evolution of receptor protein functions. Here, we developed a cell-based assay designed to assess pleiotropic effects in G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), the largest receptor class in eukaryotes. Because our assay allows for multiple GPCR molecular phenotypes (basal activity, ligand-dependent signaling, and cellular receptor abundance) to be simultaneously assessed, we applied it to study rhodopsin, a visual GPCR that evolved for high phototransduction capabilities by maximizing light-driven responses while minimizing noise. To investigate this, we integrated our assay with deep mutational scanning to test the impacts of ~2,000 single-residue substitutions in rhodopsin across all three molecular phenotypes (~6,000 measurements). By analyzing these data in the context of rhodopsin's protein structures, we found complex pleiotropic effects that act asymmetrically to impose joint constraints, restricting mutational tolerance in rhodopsin's retinal binding pocket and G protein interaction interface. A dose-response analysis of rhodopsin signaling revealed that these pleiotropic constraints arise from the dual functions of its chromophore, which acts as an agonist upon light-driven isomerization but also an inverse agonist in darkness. Because these constraints reflect mechanistically driven limitations in the evolution of receptor signaling, these findings reveal a role for biophysical pleiotropy in shaping the signaling capabilities of receptor proteins.
papers.authors: Chen SK, Liu J, Chang BSW.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: EverGreen: A Calcium Sensing Fluorescent Protein with Ultra-Slow Response Properties
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Fluorescent calcium indicators are typically optimized for fast kinetics, but for some bio-engineering projects in synthetic biology slower indicators with long decay time constants may be more practical and easier to apply. We here present a green fluorescent protein calcium biosensor with unusually slow response kinetics. By molecular engineering we were able to extend a slow component of the decay t 1/2 to 6.1 min. The fluorescence in “EverGreen” could thus be detected for minutes after the underlying calcium fluctuation had already dissipated. This may be useful when constraints in instrumentation and methodology do not allow close coupling of physiological activation of cells and read-out of signals, facilitating directed evolution projects run via plate readers or cell sorters.
papers.authors: Valiente-Gabioud A, Griesbeck O.
papers.status: 预印本 · 未经同行评审

papers.title: From discovery to engineering: revealing and optimizing the indigoids biosynthesis by FMO from Indigofera tinctoria.
papers.abstract: Introduction Indigo-producing plants have been used for millennia as natural dyes and traditional medicines. Despite evolutionary divergence, these species converge on a conserved indigo biosynthesis pathway, yet the molecular basis for differences in catalytic efficiency remains largely unknown. Objectives This study aimed to identify and characterize the key genes involved in indigoid biosynthesisfrom Indigofera tinctoria, and to elucidate the structural determinants underlying their catalytic properties. Methods We performed transcriptome mining and functional screening of candidate genes fromI. tinctoria, followed by enzyme kinetic characterization, substrate specificity profiling, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using the catalytically competent state, alanine scanning mutagenesis, and metabolic engineering through co-expression and co-cultivation strategies in Escherichia coli. Results Three genes, Flavin-containing monooxygenase (ItFMO),Tryptophan synthase α-subunit (ItTSA), and Indole synthase(ItINS), were identified and functionally validated. ItFMO exhibited higher catalytic efficiency (k cat /K m = 0.22 ± 0.05 s⁻ 1 *mM⁻ 1 ) toward indole than other plant FMOs tested, and converted 16 substituted indoles into variously colored indigoids. When 2-oxindole was supplied, ItFMO co-produced indirubin (∼70% of total pigments) via condensation of enzymatically generated indoxyl with 2-oxindole. Co-expression of ItFMO with E. coli TnaA (Tryptophanase) yielded the highest indigo titer (41.27 ± 0.84 mg/L), followed by ItINS (30.54 ± 0.33 mg/L) and ItFMO alone (27.58 ± 0.19 mg/L), whereas ItTSA severely reduced production (5.68 ± 0.20 mg/L). Co-cultivation of the two strains achieved a 2.7-fold increase over the monoculture, with a titer of 60.03 ± 0.82 mg/L. MD simulations and alanine scanning identified Q51, Y160, K212, S213, F373, and N427 as critical residues governing ItFMO catalysis, and which were authenticated by site-directed mutagenesis. Conclusion Our findings establish a mechanistic basis for understanding FMO-mediated indigo formation in plants and provide a structural insight for engineering plant-derived enzymes in microbial systems.
papers.authors: Liu C, Zhang D, Zhang M, Chang S, Cheng M, Lou Y, Tan H.

papers.title: Isoquercetin Attenuates Graves' Disease-Related Thyroid Epithelial Inflammatory Responses: Exploratory Evidence from Network Pharmacology, Mendelian Randomization, and Cellular Validation.
papers.abstract: Background Graves' disease (GD) is initiated by thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor autoantibody signaling, whereas cytokine-mediated inflammation within the thyroid may amplify thyrocyte activation. The microbiota-related metabolites contributing to this inflammatory component remain incompletely defined. Methods We integrated reported gut microbiota-metabolite associations with GD-associated genes, constructed protein-protein interaction and enrichment networks, prioritized candidate metabolites, and evaluated predicted docking of isoquercetin (ISO) with inflammatory targets. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) used MiBioGen microbiota and FinnGen autoimmune hyperthyroidism data. A separate four-group experiment compared control, M22 alone, interferon-γ (IFN-γ) alone, and combined M22/IFN-γ stimulation in Nthy-ori 3-1 thyroid follicular epithelial cells. ISO treatment was then evaluated under combined stimulation; inflammatory transcripts, NF-κB p65 phosphorylation, and cell viability were assessed. Results Fifty-three shared targets were identified, and the highest-degree PPI nodes included IL6, TNF, AKT1, IL1B, JUN, NFKB1, TP53, and CASP3. The shared targets were enriched in TNF, NF-κB, MAPK, PI3K-Akt, and Th17-related pathways. After chemical-name standardization, ISO had a network degree of 8 and was connected with TNF and IL6; docking indicated predicted molecular compatibility rather than direct binding. Twelve taxa showed nominal IVW associations with GD, but none survived false discovery rate correction. In the four-group experiment, IFN-γ was the dominant stimulus for IL1B, IL6, and TNF expression; the combined M22/IFN-γ group had the highest mean expression, but no interaction term was significant. Under combined stimulation, ISO reduced inflammatory transcripts and the phospho-p65/total p65 ratio without markedly changing total p65. Conclusion These exploratory, convergent findings identify ISO as a microbiota-related candidate modulator of thyroid epithelial inflammatory responses. They do not establish microbial production, direct target binding, or clinical efficacy, and require further mechanistic and in vivo validation.
papers.authors: Zhang S, Ma Q, Ding X, Zhang X, Wang G, Liu J.

papers.title: Microbial production of the low-caloric sweetener d-allulose from d-glucose by evolutionary engineering.
papers.abstract: d-Allulose is a low-caloric natural sweetener and a promising alternative to d-sucrose and high-fructose corn syrup. Its current production relies on immobilized enzymes operating at approximately 60°C. In this research article, we developed a whole-cell process that converts d-glucose to d-allulose at 30°C, eliminating the need for enzyme purification and immobilization. To overcome inefficient d-glucose conversion to d-fructose at this temperature, we subjected a bacterial selection strain, whose growth was coupled to d-glucose isomerase activity, to adaptive laboratory evolution. This yielded improved d-glucose isomerase variants and mutations that strongly enhanced sugar uptake. Their integration into a highly engineered chassis strain expressing d-allulose 3-epimerase, together with another adaptive evolution experiment, enabled d-allulose yields of up to 19%, exceeding those obtained with immobilized enzymes at high temperatures. Together, our findings establish a strategy to overcome the limitations of a cell-free enzymatic process using a microbial whole-cell catalyst, offering alternative solutions for the food industry.
papers.authors: Lehnert A, Gentile R, Tahiraj C, Wirtz A, Baumgart M, Polen T, Gohlke H, Bott M.

papers.title: Next-generation precision fermentation: integrating engineered cell factories, bioprocess intensification, and smart bioprocessing.
papers.abstract: Precision fermentation (PF) uses engineered microbial cell factories to manufacture defined products under controlled bioprocess conditions. In this review, PF is treated operationally as the integration of engineered hosts with metabolic engineering and process control, while traditional food fermentations without engineered production strains are excluded. The field now spans pharmaceuticals, food ingredients, industrial enzymes, specialty chemicals, and biopolymers, but commercial translation remains constrained by biological non-linearity, substrate and feedstock variability, mass-transfer limitations at scale, downstream recovery, and the cost gap with incumbent processes. This mini-review examines five connected layers: engineered microbial chassis; design build test learn (DBTL) and multi-omics-guided metabolic engineering; bioreactor intensification; Process Analytical Technology (PAT), soft sensors and AI-enabled control; and techno-economic and life cycle assessment. Quantitative case studies illustrate both the progress and the remaining scale-up gaps, including semi-synthetic artemisinin, recombinant insulin, lactic acid, succinic acid, QS-21, and polyhydroxyalkanoates. The central argument is that the next phase of PF will depend less on isolated improvements in strain performance than on coordinated integration of strain design, intensified operation, real-time process understanding, and rigorous economic and environmental assessment. This integration is essential for translating laboratory performance into reproducible, scalable, and commercially credible biomanufacturing. KEY POINTS: PF requires integration of cell-factory engineering with scalable bioprocessing rather than optimisation of any single layer. DBTL and multi-omics improve strain performance, but laboratory titres do not guarantee industrial scalability. Bioprocess intensification and real-time monitoring are required to convert strain performance into robust production. PAT, soft sensors, and AI strengthen process control when supported by reliable online data and qualified models. TEA and LCA should be integrated early to filter commercial and environmental feasibility before scale-up.
papers.authors: Mahmoud YA, El-Badry AM.

papers.title: Strain engineering of Aspergillus species for industrial enzymes bioproduction: a comprehensive review.
papers.abstract: Filamentous fungi of the genus Aspergillus, because of their exceptional secretory capacity and metabolic versatility have been extensively applied in traditional food fermentation and industrial biotechnology for production of diverse bioproducts. Their history of domestication and industrial application has enabled major progress in enzyme production; however, challenges associated with the filamentous growth and strain engineering for future biomanufacturing development still remain. This review summarizes the advances across the spectrum of strain-improvement methodologies, from classical mutagenesis, protoplast fusion, genome shuffling, and adaptive laboratory evolution to the modern era of CRISPR enabled genome editing, synthetic biology, and systems-level metabolic engineering. Previous reviews have primarily focused on individual Aspergillus species, specific industrial products or particular strain improvement approaches. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of classical and modern strain engineering technologies and industrial scale up across a wide range of Aspergillus species for industrial enzyme production. In particular, emerging non-GMO evolution tools such as atmospheric and room temperature plasma (ARTP) mutagenesis, and modern molecular biotechnology coupled with microdroplet-based ultrahigh-throughput screening, now allow the researchers to generate and screen a large number of Aspergillus species mutants with single-cell precision. The discovery of high-performance strains with enhanced secretion, stress tolerance, substrate utilization, and favorable enzymatic profiles for food and bioprocessing applications has been accelerated by the strain innovations. Collectively, these advances establish A. oryzae and the related species as increasingly reliable, scalable, and programmable hosts that can meet the biomanufacturing requirements of future circular and sustainable bioeconomies.
papers.authors: Ullah I, Zhang Z, Geng D, Zhou Q, Zou Y, Xu B, Zhang C, Xing XH.

papers.title: Valorizing watermelon rind waste into plant-based scaffolds for proof-of-concept cultivated meat production in a dynamic fixed-bed bioreactor.
papers.abstract: Cultivated meat (CM) biomanufacturing faces major challenges in cost and in scaling adherent-cell processes from the laboratory toward pilot and industrial production. This study presents a proof-of-concept (POC) in which watermelon rind, an agricultural waste by-product, was valorized into decellularized plant scaffolds (vDPS) and evaluated in a dynamic fixed-bed reactor (FBR). By replacing Triton® X-100 (1% v/v) with Tween-20 (10% v/v), we achieved effective decellularization, reducing residual DNA to below 25 ng/mg while eliminating the use of the toxic Triton X-100, making the scaffolds more suitable for CM applications. The resulting scaffolds exhibited high porosity (85.6%) and a Young's modulus of 36.8 ± 5.9 kPa, confirming their suitability for use as CM scaffolds. For dynamic bioreactor evaluation, the scaffolds were coated with Corning® Synthemax® II SC substrate and cultured with murine myoblast C2C12 cells under the process control capabilities of the Corning Ascent® fixed bed reactor (FBR) system. Over seven days, cells attached, proliferated, and differentiated; relative to static culture, the dynamic condition showed higher metabolic activity and denser cell coverage. Myogenic differentiation was confirmed by Myosin heavy chain and Desmin expression, and cross-sectional imaging showed cell penetration into the scaffold. The prototypes remained structurally stable after cooking. Overall, this work demonstrates the feasibility of integrating waste-valorized scaffolds into a dynamic FBR system, providing a POC foundation for future scale-up studies.
papers.authors: Suntornnond R, Xu S, Murugan P, Yap WS, Ng SK, Sharma AK, Choudhury D.

papers.title: Yeast-Based Platforms for Next-Generation Human Health Applications.
papers.abstract: Yeast platforms are rapidly transitioning from traditional eukaryotic model organisms to versatile, programmable chassis for next-generation human health applications. This review systematically examines the translational evolution of conventional and non-conventional yeasts including Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Komagataella phaffii, Saccharomyces boulardii, and Yarrowia lipolytica and redefines them as scalable biomanufacturing factories and advanced living therapeutics. We highlight milestone advancements in synthetic biology toolkits that lower technical barriers, such as CRISPR-mediated multiplex editing, modular cloning frameworks, and high-throughput secretion screening. We focus on sophisticated glycoengineering strategies for humanized N-glycosylation, alongside data-driven paradigms that leverage artificial intelligence to predict gene expression and streamline strain design. In clinical domains, we detail the established success of yeast in producing subunit or virus-like particle vaccines (e.g. HBV and HPV) and therapeutic enzymes (e.g. ecallantide), alongside its emerging role as gut-adapted live biotherapeutic products (LBPs) engineered for in situ delivery and biosensing. Finally, we explore specialized non-conventional platforms, focusing on lipid- and acetyl-CoA-rich hosts for lipophilic drug discovery, and stress-tolerant systems optimized for economical, feedstock-flexible bioprocesses. In summary, this review underscores the integrated value of yeast systems across disease modeling, industrial manufacturing, and clinical intervention, charting future directions to address global health challenges.
papers.authors: Yook S, Lee JW, Park M, Koh HG, Shin J.

papers.title: Advanced cannabidiol delivery platforms: smart biomaterials, controlled release systems, and 3D-bioprinted therapeutic technologies.
papers.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid derived from Cannabis sativa L. has gained significant attention in biomedical research due to its broad spectrum of therapeutic properties, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antioxidant, neuroprotective, and anticancer activities. However, its clinical translation remains limited by poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, rapid metabolism, and instability under physiological conditions. To overcome these challenges, advanced drug delivery platforms based on 3D bioprinting technologies have emerged as promising strategies for controlled and site-specific delivery of CBD. This review provides a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art CBD delivery systems, including polymeric biomaterials such as PLGA, PEG derivatives, chitosan, alginate, and cellulose-based hybrids, which enhance drug stability and enable sustained release profiles. Nano- and microstructured systems, including liposomes, nanoparticles, nanoemulsions, microspheres, and electrospun nanofibers, are discussed for their ability to improve bioavailability and facilitate targeted delivery at the cellular level. Hydrogel-based platforms, particularly injectable and stimuli-responsive systems, are highlighted for their role in localised therapy and tissue engineering applications. Furthermore, the integration of 3D bioprinting technologies enables the fabrication of patient-specific scaffolds and implantable constructs for precision medicine and regenerative therapies. Stimuli-responsive systems, including pH-, temperature-, enzyme-, and externally triggered release platforms, further enhance on-demand drug release in diseased microenvironments. The biomedical applications of CBD-based systems are critically evaluated in antimicrobial therapy, wound healing, tumour-targeted cancer therapy, immunomodulation, microbiome regulation, and regenerative medicine. Finally, this review addresses current translational challenges such as drug loading efficiency, stability issues, scalability, and regulatory barriers, while highlighting future perspectives involving artificial intelligence-guided design, personalised nanomedicine, and advanced biomanufacturing technologies. Overall, CBD-based smart biomaterial platforms represent a highly promising approach for next-generation therapeutic systems with improved efficacy, safety, and clinical potential.
papers.authors: Shabbir A, Parvinzadeh Gashti M.

papers.title: Automated anaerobic cultivation and phenotyping of diverse chain-elongating bacteria
papers.abstract: Anaerobic bacteria perform diverse metabolic functions with considerable biotechnological potential, yet their physiology remains poorly characterized because conventional anaerobic cultivation is low throughput. Here, we developed a Platform for Automated Cultivation of Microbial Anaerobes (PACMAN) and applied it to systematically characterize the physiology of diverse chain-elongating bacteria (CEB) that produce medium-chain carboxylic acids (MCCAs). High-throughput screening across nine CEB and 20 potential electron donors revealed extensive metabolic diversity, including previously unreported conversion of glycerol to octanoate by Pseudoramibacter alactolyticus and xylose to hexanoate by Caproiciproducens sp. 7D4C2. Comparison with genome-derived metabolic pathways further revealed widespread discrepancies between predicted and observed substrate utilization. Across diverse CEB and electron donors, decreasing the acetate-to-electron-donor ratio consistently shifted product distributions toward longer-chain carboxylates, revealing a general principle governing chain-length specificity, although maximum attainable chain length remained strain dependent. Finally, screening CEB across increasing carboxylate concentrations revealed substantial variation in MCCA tolerance, with Gram-positive MCCA producers exhibiting greater resilience than Gram-negative and butyrate-producing bacteria. Together, these findings reveal organizing principles underlying the metabolic versatility and product specificity of CEB and establish automated anaerobic phenotyping as a scalable approach for discovering microbial functions relevant to biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: Howard JP, Lawson CE.
papers.status: 预印本 · 未经同行评审

papers.title: Biodegradable polylactic acid microplastics pose greater field nitrous oxide emission risks than conventional polyethylene by reshaping microbial production-reduction pathways in a wheat-maize rotation system.
papers.abstract: Microplastic contamination in agroecosystems is increasing, yet the field-scale effects of biodegradable microplastics on soil nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions remain unclear. We conducted a wheat-maize rotation field experiment to compare conventional polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs) and biodegradable polylactic acid microplastics (PLA-MPs) at three application levels. Measurements included N 2 O fluxes, soil physicochemical properties, N-transformation enzyme activities, potential nitrification and denitrification rates, functional gene abundances, N 2 O/(N 2 O+N 2 ) product ratios, 15N-18O-based N 2 O production pathways. Two-way ANOVA showed that microplastic type was the most consistent determinant of key responses, whereas concentration and interaction effects varied among indicators and seasons. PE-MPs caused weak and variable changes in soil N cycling and cumulative N 2 O emissions. In contrast, PLA-MPs increased cumulative N 2 O emissions by 38.9-61.1%, increased dissolved organic carbon, lowered pH, suppressed ammonia monooxygenase activity and nitrification, and stimulated nitrite reductase activity, potential denitrification, and nirK/nirS abundances. Increased N 2 O/(N 2 O+N 2 ) and (nirK+nirS)/nosZ ratios indicated a stronger imbalance between N 2 O production and nosZ-mediated reduction. Dual-isotope tracing further showed that microplastics reduced nitrifier nitrification and shifted N 2 O production toward nitrifier denitrification, coupled nitrification-denitrification, and heterotrophic denitrification, with the strongest shift under PLA-MPs. These results demonstrate PLA-MPs pose greater N 2 O emission risks than PE-MPs, biodegradability does not necessarily imply environmental safety.
papers.authors: Wang C, He R, Wang L, Li Y, Li R, Dai Y, He X, Wang B, Yang M, Wang X.

papers.title: Characterization of a salt-responsive promoter from the moss Physcomitrium patens.
papers.abstract: Engineering stress-responsive gene regulation is critical for developing abiotic stress-tolerant plants. Two native Physcomitrium patens promoters was characterized under osmotic and salt stress, identifying Pp3c20_8210 as a salt-inducible promoter in P. patens that could hold a potential in future synthetic biology applications. We also investigated salt-responsive elements in the native promoters of Physcomitrium patens with long-term monitoring of protein expression under high osmotic and saline stress conditions. To evaluate the role of cis-regulatory elements in salt-inducible gene expression, we analyzed shorter engineered versions of Pp3c20_8210, which displayed continuous salt-responsive expression, even after the targeted deletion of key transcription factor binding sites for Homeodomain, MYB, GATA, and Dof transcription factors. Deletion of Homeodomain and GATA transcription factor binding sites reduced Venus reporter expression, suggesting that they are possibly the primary drivers of the Pp3c20_8210 promoter activity in P. patens. No statistically significant effect on promoter responsiveness was detected following the deletion of MYB and Dof transcription factor binding sites under our experimental conditions, possibly due to compensatory mechanisms from other regulatory elements. These findings lay the foundation for future dissection of salt-responsive promoter architecture and can provide valuable tools for synthetic gene regulation in plants.
papers.authors: Ríos FJA, Horn A, Workman C, Simonsen HT.

papers.title: Draft genome sequence and phenotypic analysis of Pseudozyma sp. SY16 with evidence of binucleate cells.
papers.abstract: Mannosylerythritol lipids (MELs) are glycolipid biosurfactants that have attracted considerable attention in cosmetic and industrial applications due to their favorable biocompatibility and stability. Pseudozyma sp. SY16 is a promising MEL-producing strain with high production capacity; however, the lack of genomic resources has limited our understanding of its genetic and cellular characteristics and hindered its application in metabolic engineering. In this study, we generated a high-quality draft genome of Pseudozyma sp. SY16 using a hybrid sequencing approach combining long- and short-read sequencing and comprehensively characterized its genomic and cellular features. The 20.2 Mb genome was assembled into 23 nuclear scaffolds and one mitochondrial scaffold, achieving a high BUSCO completeness of 98.9%. Comparative analysis of the MEL biosynthetic genes among closely related species within the family Ustilaginaceae revealed distinct patterns of gene conservation. The mac1 , mac2 , mat1 , mmf1 , and emt1 genes were highly conserved in both gene content and genomic organization among SY16, P. hubeiensis , and Mycosarcoma maydis , whereas only mmf1 was retained in the corresponding regions of P. pruni and P. flocculosa . This pattern suggests lineage-specific retention and loss of MEL biosynthetic genes during the evolution of family Ustilaginaceae. GenomeScope analysis revealed a predominantly single-peaked k-mer distribution, without a clear pattern indicative of either a haploid or diploid genome. Independently, confocal microscopy revealed frequent cells with two spatially separated DAPI-positive signals, consistent with an apparent binucleate morphology. Together, these findings establish a high-quality genomic resource for SY16 and provide new insights into MEL biosynthesis, genome evolution, and cellular organization, providing a foundation for future genetic and metabolic engineering of this non-model yeast toward enhanced MEL production.
papers.authors: Rho A, Choi DY, Yun JH, Park Y, Choi HI, Cho DH, Kim HS, Lee YJ.

papers.title: Engineered probiotics target granulomas to treat mycobacterial infection
papers.abstract: Granulomas are a pathological niche for mycobacteria that remain difficult to access with conventional therapies. Here we show that probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) infiltrates and colonizes granulomas and can be engineered as a delivery system that senses the local microenvironment and releases antimycobacterial payloads. Specifically, we leveraged the hypoxic microenvironment of necrotic granulomas to restrict bacterial growth, and developed a dual-mode lysis circuit combining intracellular and extracellular killing for sustained payload release with limited evolutionary escape. We further engineered EcN to express a mycobacteriophage-derived enzyme, generating a strain that suppressed drug-sensitive and drug-resistant mycobacteria in vitro and potentiated conventional antibiotic activity. Engineered probiotics also reduced mycobacterial burden in vivo, and in a murine model of rifampicin-resistant infection, combination treatment with pretomanid achieved greater bacterial reduction than either monotherapy. Together, these results establish a synthetic biology framework for targeting granulomatous infections with programmable living microbes.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Harimoto T, Makafe GG, Coker C, Kim H, Im J, Jing Y, Jin H, Hu X, Zutshi S, Raneri MR, Weinrick B, Danino T.

enrichment.titleZh: 工程化益生菌靶向肉芽肿，用于治疗分枝杆菌感染
enrichment.abstractZh: 肉芽肿是分枝杆菌的一种病理性生存微环境，常规疗法仍难以到达。本研究表明，益生菌大肠杆菌Nissle 1917（Escherichia coli Nissle 1917，EcN）能够浸润并定植于肉芽肿，还可被改造成感知局部微环境并释放抗分枝杆菌载荷的递送系统。具体而言，研究者利用坏死性肉芽肿的低氧微环境限制细菌生长，并开发了结合细胞内与细胞外杀伤的双模式裂解回路，以实现载荷持续释放，同时限制进化逃逸。研究者进一步改造EcN，使其表达一种来源于分枝杆菌噬菌体的酶，获得的菌株在体外抑制了药物敏感型和耐药型分枝杆菌，并增强了常规抗生素的活性。工程化益生菌还降低了体内分枝杆菌负荷；在利福平耐药感染的小鼠模型中，与pretomanid联合治疗实现的菌量下降幅度大于任一单药治疗。这些结果共同建立了一个利用可编程活微生物靶向肉芽肿性感染的合成生物学框架。
enrichment.sourceTitle: Engineered probiotics target granulomas to treat mycobacterial infection
enrichment.sourceAbstract: Granulomas are a pathological niche for mycobacteria that remain difficult to access with conventional therapies. Here we show that probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) infiltrates and colonizes granulomas and can be engineered as a delivery system that senses the local microenvironment and releases antimycobacterial payloads. Specifically, we leveraged the hypoxic microenvironment of necrotic granulomas to restrict bacterial growth, and developed a dual-mode lysis circuit combining intracellular and extracellular killing for sustained payload release with limited evolutionary escape. We further engineered EcN to express a mycobacteriophage-derived enzyme, generating a strain that suppressed drug-sensitive and drug-resistant mycobacteria in vitro and potentiated conventional antibiotic activity. Engineered probiotics also reduced mycobacterial burden in vivo, and in a murine model of rifampicin-resistant infection, combination treatment with pretomanid achieved greater bacterial reduction than either monotherapy. Together, these results establish a synthetic biology framework for targeting granulomatous infections with programmable living microbes.

papers.title: Engineering Methylobacterium as a C1 biomanufacturing platform: Metabolic architecture, regulatory networks, and synthetic biology strategies.
papers.abstract: Methanol is emerging as a sustainable and energy-dense one carbon (C1) feedstock for next-generation biomanufacturing, owing to its superior energy density, abundance, water miscibility, and decoupling from food supply chains. Methylobacterium species are facultative methylotrophs that have evolved sophisticated metabolic and regulatory networks for efficient methanol utilization. This review highlights the transition of Methylobacterium from a model organism for dissecting methylotrophy to a programmable C1 chassis for synthetic biology. We provide a unique overview of its core metabolic architecture, focusing on the lanthanide-switchable pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ)-dependent methanol oxidation, the tetrahydromethanopterin (H₄MPT)-mediated formaldehyde buffering system, and the tight coupling of the serine cycle with the ethylmalonyl-CoA (EMC) pathway, which together govern carbon flux, redox balance, and energy efficiency. Building on this intrinsic framework, we survey how these traits are leveraged to produce high-value chemicals, such as folate derivatives, redox cofactors, organic acids, terpenoids, bioplastics, and single-cell protein. Furthermore, we discuss advanced engineering strategies for systematic chassis optimization including global transcriptional regulation, metabolic valve control, and photo-methylotrophic configurations, along with a comprehensive evaluation of Methylobacterium chassis advantages and disadvantages, concrete product-chassis matching rules, common engineering bottlenecks, and diversified low-cost feedstock options. Finally, we propose a product-chassis matching framework and outline future directions centered on regulatory control, flux coordination, and robustness enhancement to overcome current limitations in titer, yield, and scale-up, while also leveraging agricultural applications and low-cost feedstocks, thereby positioning Methylobacterium as a cornerstone of sustainable low-carbon biotechnology.
papers.authors: Yao L, Ma Z, Liu Z, Tan L, Yang S.

papers.title: Metabolic Remodelingof the NOG Pathway and Glyoxylate Cycle for High-Yield L-Homoserine Biosynthesis.
papers.abstract: L‑homoserine is a valuable C4 amino acid with broad applications in agriculture, pharmaceuticals, and daily chemicals. However, existing high‑yielding strains have mainly been evaluated at laboratory scale, and their scale‑up feasibility has not yet been sufficiently verified, leaving industrial production without a direct engineering basis. In this study, a non-auxotrophic, scalable L‑homoserine high‑producer was constructed by targeting carbon loss, rewiring the metabolic network, and maintaining cofactor balance. Specifically, the threonine branch was dynamically attenuated to reduce product degradation, while the non‑oxidative glycolysis (NOG) pathway was introduced and coupled with the glyoxylate shunt to conserve carbon and redirect flux toward the aspartate pathway, thereby increasing precursor availability. The main biosynthetic pathway and cofactor regeneration were further strengthened to accelerate L‑homoserine synthesis. Ultimately, strain HS25 achieved a titer of 126.5 g/L L‑homoserine,a yield of 0.58 g/g glucose, and a productivity of 1.77 g/L/hin 50 L fermentation. These metabolic engineering strategies are scalable and may serve as a generalizable framework for the industrial production of other aspartate‑derived amino acids and their derivatives.
papers.authors: Shan Q, Zhang J, Gong R, Zhou Y, Xu J, Liu Z, Zheng Y.

papers.title: Metabolism-Informed Bioreactor Model for Transferring Knowledge from Fed-batch to Continuous Biomanufacturing
papers.abstract: Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells remain the dominant platform for monoclonal antibody (mAb) manufacturing, and rising demand is pushing the industry from fed-batch toward continuous operation. Continuous cultures promise sustained high cell densities and volumetric productivities, but their operation depends on reliable real-time monitoring, prediction and control. Limited intracellular observability and sparse extracellular measurements hinder this, leaving a persistent gap between mechanistic understanding and predictive deployment. Here we describe a metabolism-informed model for mAb production that embeds reactor- and intracellular-level mass balances directly within a learning architecture, while deliberately avoiding predefined kinetic rate laws and explicit steady-state assumptions. Because conservation relationships remain invariant across operating modes, this formulation provides a principled structural prior for cross-regime generalisation, positioning the model as a soft sensor for continuous bioprocesses: inferring unmeasured intracellular fluxes and one-step ahead forecasting extracellular concentrations to support process monitoring and control. Benchmarking two metabolic network sizes and three metabolic optimisation strategies, concentration predictions are indistinguishable across network sizes. Exchange flux fidelity is agnostic to solver choice, with network size mattering only for intracellular interpretability. Transferring the developed model from fed-batch to continuous operation with fine-tuning outperforming other transfer learning variants. This is consistent with the metabolic structure being invariant to mode of operation. Predicted fluxes reveal growth rate in fed-batch, rather than operating mode, as the dominant axis of metabolic variation, and identify potential regime-shift signals to guide experimental design for continuous culture characterisation. These results chart a route towards digital models sufficiently grounded in first-principles knowledge, yet adaptive for deployment under regime shifts.
papers.authors: Monteiro M, Bediako S, Tecson R, Nierode G, Kotidis P, Kontoravdi C.

enrichment.titleZh: 代谢知识引导的生物反应器模型：将补料分批工艺的知识迁移至连续生物制造
enrichment.abstractZh: 中国仓鼠卵巢（CHO）细胞仍是单克隆抗体（mAb）制造的主要平台，不断增长的需求正推动该行业从补料分批运行转向连续运行。连续培养有望维持高细胞密度和高体积生产率，但其运行依赖可靠的实时监测、预测与控制。细胞内状态的可观测性有限，细胞外测量又较为稀疏，阻碍了这一目标的实现，使机制认识与预测模型的实际部署之间持续存在差距。本研究提出一种由代谢知识引导的mAb生产模型，将反应器层面和细胞内层面的质量衡算直接嵌入学习架构，同时避免预设动力学速率定律和显式稳态假设。由于守恒关系在不同运行模式下保持不变，这一表述为跨工况泛化提供了基于原理的结构先验，并将模型定位为连续生物过程的软传感器：推断未测量的细胞内通量，并提前一步预测细胞外浓度，以支持过程监测和控制。研究者对两种代谢网络规模与三种代谢优化策略进行了基准比较，发现不同网络规模下的浓度预测结果无可区分的差异。交换通量的保真度与求解器选择无关，网络规模仅影响细胞内过程的可解释性。将所开发的模型从补料分批运行迁移至连续运行时，微调的表现优于其他迁移学习方案。这与代谢结构不随运行模式改变的认识一致。预测通量显示，补料分批培养中的生长速率，而非运行模式，是代谢变化的主导维度；模型还识别出可能提示工况转换的信号，可为连续培养表征的实验设计提供指导。这些结果为构建既充分建立在第一性原理知识之上、又能适应工况转换下部署的数字模型提供了一条路径。
