papers.title: Microbial Ethylene Glycol Metabolism: Pathways, Metabolic Engineering, and PET Upcycling.
papers.abstract: Ethylene glycol (EG) is an attractive non-sugar carbon source because it can be obtained from petrochemical routes, renewable production platforms, and the depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate (PET), thereby linking plastic upcycling with sustainable biomanufacturing. In recent years, substantial progress has been made in elucidating EG catabolism, including the initial oxidation of EG, native glyoxylate assimilation pathways, synthetic route design, and chassis engineering. Nevertheless, efficient and robust EG bioconversion is still limited by unfavorable thermodynamics, low catalytic efficiency, intermediate toxicity, and pathway-host incompatibility. In this Review, we summarize recent advances in three interconnected areas: the oxidation of EG to glycolaldehyde and its downstream processing; glyoxylate-centered native assimilation networks and their integration with central carbon metabolism; and synthetic pathways designed to improve carbon conservation and redirect carbon flux toward acetyl-CoA, central metabolites, and target products. We compare the tartronate semialdehyde pathway with the β-hydroxyaspartate cycle, discuss key design principles for synthetic modules, and highlight recent progress in chassis engineering, regulatory rewiring, and the direct conversion of PET hydrolysates. We further emphasize the ongoing transition from single-substrate EG utilization to integrated PET upcycling, in which mixed-monomer co-utilization, impurity tolerance, and aldehyde detoxification have emerged as major engineering targets. Overall, EG is becoming a promising platform substrate for connecting plastic waste recycling with green biomanufacturing, although further advances in enzyme discovery, pathway optimization, and pathway-host matching are still required.
papers.authors: Qian J, Wang P, Wang W, Li J, Zhang X, Zhu X, Chen M, Bi C, Zhang X.

enrichment.titleZh: 微生物乙二醇代谢：途径、代谢工程与 PET 升级再造
enrichment.abstractZh: 乙二醇（EG）可来源于石化路线、可再生生产平台及聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯（PET）的解聚，因此是一种连接塑料升级再造与可持续生物制造的有吸引力的非糖碳源。近年来，对乙二醇分解代谢的认识已取得较大进展，包括初始氧化、天然乙醛酸同化、合成途径设计和底盘工程。然而，不利的热力学、低催化效率、中间体毒性及途径与宿主不兼容，仍限制其高效稳健转化。本综述总结三个相互联系的方面：乙二醇氧化为乙醇醛及其后续转化；以乙醛酸为中心的天然同化网络及其与中心碳代谢的整合；旨在提高碳保留并将通量导向乙酰辅酶A、中心代谢物和目标产物的合成途径。文章比较羟基丙二酸半醛途径与 β-羟基天冬氨酸循环，讨论合成模块的设计原则，并介绍底盘工程、调控重构及 PET 水解产物直接转化的进展。文章强调该领域正从单一乙二醇利用转向集成 PET 升级再造，混合单体共利用、杂质耐受和醛解毒已成为主要工程目标。总体而言，乙二醇正成为连接塑料回收与绿色生物制造的有前景的平台底物，但仍需推进酶发现、途径优化及途径—宿主匹配。

papers.title: Neutral Morphological Masking: Constructive Neutral Evolution of Chiral Scaffolds for Information-Maintaining Artificial Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract A minimal synthetic cell that completes a full replication–growth–division cycle still demonstrates nothing about self-maintenance unless it also carries a state variable that can degrade under a genuine environmental stress and be actively defended. Our earlier proposal (Sandler, 2026b) specified such a module — chiral order Uχ as a programmable memory, D-glucose glycation as a stress channel, and circular dichroism (CD) as a sensor — but treated the robustness that protects Uχ as a static, hand-designed surface property, u_s. That is an adaptationist assumption dressed as an engineering parameter, and it is also why the initial submission read as disconnected from current artificial-life research: a designed robustness knob does not need to cite the literature on how robustness actually arises in living systems. This revision addresses both problems by fusing the chiral-order module with Constructive Neutral Evolution (CNE), the framework in which biological complexity accumulates through selectively neutral steps rather than adaptive design (Stoltzfus, 1999), and specifically with the interlocking-masking mechanism recently formalized for multi-subunit complexes in the Quandary Den artificial-life model (Walsh, 2026). In the synthesized framework, random neutral mutations introduce structural protrusions in one subunit of a multi-subunit chiral scaffold; complementary recesses that neutrally arise in partner subunits mask these protrusions to preserve packing order, and the accumulated interlocking geometry incidentally occludes the scaffold's glycation-vulnerable amine sites. Geometric surface uniformity, u_s, is therefore reframed as an emergent, unselected byproduct of a masking ratchet rather than a design input. We give the resulting multi-subunit dynamical system, retain the original module's mechanistic lattice Monte Carlo and site-diluted XY-model machinery as validation of the underlying stress–state–repair physics, and add a new toy evolutionary simulation demonstrating the internal consequences of the proposed masking rules: a one-directional ratchet in interlocking complexity, an incidental decline in the emergent glycation-rate constant, and accidental cross-protection against a novel stress shock in lineages that accumulated complexity under no direct selection for glycation resistance. We situate the proposal explicitly against current artificial-life and synthetic-biology literature on self-maintaining and homeostatic artificial cells, give an expanded, falsifiable prediction set, and lay out a staged validation roadmap.
papers.authors: Sandler L.
papers.status: 预印本 · 未经同行评审

enrichment.titleZh: 中性形态遮蔽：用于维持信息的人工细胞手性支架的建构性中性演化
enrichment.abstractZh: 即使最小合成细胞能够完成复制—生长—分裂全周期，也不足以证明其具有自我维持能力，除非它还携带一种会在真实环境胁迫下退化、并能受到主动保护的状态变量。作者此前的方案将手性有序度 Uχ 作为可编程记忆、D-葡萄糖糖基化作为胁迫通道、圆二色性（CD）作为传感器，但把保护 Uχ 的稳健性视为静态、人工设计的表面属性 u_s。本文通过将手性有序模块与建构性中性演化（CNE）整合来修订这一假设；CNE认为生物复杂性可通过选择中性的步骤积累，而非只能依赖适应性设计。具体采用近期在 Quandary Den 人工生命模型中形式化的互锁遮蔽机制：随机中性突变使多亚基手性支架中的某亚基产生结构突起，其他亚基中中性出现的互补凹槽遮蔽突起、维持堆积有序；积累的互锁几何形态附带遮挡易受糖基化影响的胺基位点。因此，表面几何均一性 u_s 被重新解释为遮蔽棘轮产生的、未经直接选择的涌现副产物，而不是设计输入。作者给出多亚基动力学系统，保留原模块的机制性晶格蒙特卡洛及位点稀释 XY 模型，用于验证胁迫—状态—修复的基础物理过程，并新增简化演化模拟，展示所提遮蔽规则的内部后果：互锁复杂性的单向增加、涌现糖基化速率常数的附带下降，以及未直接经历抗糖基化选择的谱系对新胁迫的偶然交叉保护。文章将方案置于自我维持和稳态人工细胞研究的背景中，扩展可证伪预测，并提出分阶段验证路线。

papers.title: Progress and perspectives in nitrogenase engineering in plants and yeast.
papers.abstract: Crop productivity relies on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers, which entail significant economic and environmental costs. Engineering crop plants to produce nitrogenase allowing them to acquire nitrogen from the atmosphere offers a transformative approach to sustainable agriculture. However, engineering the nitrogenase pathway into eukaryotic cells poses significant challenges due to the enzyme metal clusters, high energy demands, and extreme sensitivity to oxygen. This review summarizes recent advances in nitrogenase engineering in yeast and plants. Progress has been made using a stepwise modular approach and a functional validation pipeline for core and ancillary nitrogenase proteins. Key milestones include recovery of NifH with in vitro activity from mitochondria and chloroplasts, production of NifB that is active upon isolation or after in vitro cluster reconstitution, production of NifB-co in yeast mitochondria, in vitro FeMo-co biosynthesis using proteins purified from yeast mitochondria, and recovery of nitrogenase components from transgenic rice with activity demonstrated in vitro. Complete nitrogenase activity in engineered yeast or plants has not yet been demonstrated. We discuss the importance of organelle targeting, the exploitation of natural diversity and engineered proteins, and synthetic biology tools for the assembly of multigene pathways. Finally, we present the main remaining obstacles, such as the assembly of functional NifDK in plants, integration with host metabolism and coordinated regulation, and we outline the prospects for the development of nitrogen-fixing crops.
papers.authors: Paganelli Á, Curatti L, González-Guerrero M, Burén S, Rubio LM.

enrichment.titleZh: 植物与酵母固氮酶工程的进展与展望
enrichment.abstractZh: 作物生产依赖合成氮肥，带来较大的经济与环境成本。通过工程化使作物产生固氮酶、直接利用大气氮，为可持续农业提供了潜在的变革性途径。但固氮酶包含金属簇、能量需求高且对氧极度敏感，因此将其途径导入真核细胞面临重大挑战。本综述总结酵母和植物固氮酶工程的进展，重点介绍针对核心及辅助固氮酶蛋白的逐步模块化构建与功能验证流程。关键里程碑包括：从线粒体和叶绿体获得具有体外活性的 NifH；获得分离后或经体外金属簇重建后具有活性的 NifB；在酵母线粒体中产生 NifB-co；利用酵母线粒体纯化蛋白实现体外 FeMo-co 合成；以及从转基因水稻回收固氮酶组分并在体外证明其活性。不过，工程酵母或植物中的完整固氮酶活性尚未得到证明。文章讨论细胞器靶向、自然多样性及工程蛋白的利用，以及组装多基因途径所需的合成生物学工具，并指出植物中功能性 NifDK 组装、宿主代谢整合和协调调控等障碍，展望固氮作物开发前景。

papers.title: T Cell Receptor-Engineered T Cell Therapy in Solid Tumors: Where We Stand and What's to Come.
papers.abstract: T cell receptor-engineered T (TCR-T) cell therapy has emerged as a promising adoptive cellular therapy for solid tumors by enabling recognition of intracellular antigens presented via human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules. Unlike chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy, TCR-T cell therapy targets a broader antigen repertoire, including cancer-testis antigens, neoantigens, and viral antigens. Recent clinical advances, highlighted by the approval of afamitresgene autoleucel in synovial sarcoma, demonstrate meaningful antitumor activity. However, several limitations remain, including HLA restriction, antigen heterogeneity, toxicity related to on-target/off-tumor effects, and mechanisms of resistance such as antigen loss and T cell exhaustion. Advances in antigen selection, gene editing, and synthetic biology are improving both safety and efficacy. Combination strategies and next-generation engineered constructs are expected to overcome current barriers. This review summarizes the biological rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and resistance mechanisms of TCR-T cell therapy in solid tumors and discusses future directions to optimize their therapeutic potential.
papers.authors: Ferriol-Martínez C, D'Angelo SP.

enrichment.titleZh: 实体瘤中的 T 细胞受体工程 T 细胞治疗：现状与未来方向
enrichment.abstractZh: T细胞受体工程T细胞（TCR-T）疗法能够识别人类白细胞抗原（HLA）分子呈递的细胞内抗原，已成为实体瘤中有前景的过继细胞疗法。与嵌合抗原受体T细胞疗法相比，TCR-T可靶向更广泛的抗原，包括癌睾抗原、新抗原和病毒抗原。近期临床进展，尤其是 afamitresgene autoleucel 获批用于滑膜肉瘤，显示了有意义的抗肿瘤活性。但该疗法仍面临 HLA 限制、抗原异质性、靶向正常组织导致的毒性，以及抗原丢失和T细胞耗竭等耐药机制。抗原选择、基因编辑及合成生物学的进展正在改善安全性与有效性。联合策略和新一代工程构建体有望克服当前障碍。本综述总结实体瘤 TCR-T 疗法的生物学依据、临床证据、安全问题及耐药机制，并讨论优化其治疗潜力的未来方向。

papers.title: The Unfinished Story of Megakaryopoiesis.
papers.abstract: Since their nineteenth-century discovery, megakaryocytes (MKs) and the platelets they produce have remained among the least understood lineages in hematology. Understanding megakaryopoiesis and thrombopoiesis is essential for deciphering hematological disorders and developing platelet biomanufacturing and cell-based therapies. We revisit MK and platelet biogenesis, from MK emergence from hematopoietic stem cells to platelet release through proplatelet formation and cytoplasmic fragmentation. The growing complexity of differentiation pathways challenges the classical hierarchical view of hematopoiesis. Many concepts established in mice remain insufficiently validated in humans, motivating 3D bioengineered models for disease study that may rewrite key chapters in human platelet biology.
papers.authors: Gabinaud E, Goggi G, Alizadehghannad M, Balduini A.

enrichment.titleZh: 巨核细胞生成：尚未完成的故事
enrichment.abstractZh: 自19世纪被发现以来，巨核细胞（MK）及其产生的血小板一直是血液学中认识较不充分的细胞谱系之一。理解巨核细胞生成和血小板生成，对解析血液疾病、开发血小板生物制造及细胞疗法至关重要。本文回顾巨核细胞与血小板的发生过程，从造血干细胞产生巨核细胞，到通过前血小板形成和细胞质碎裂释放血小板。分化途径日益显现的复杂性，对经典的造血层级模型提出挑战。许多在小鼠中建立的概念尚缺少充分的人体证据，因此推动了用于疾病研究的三维生物工程模型的发展，这些模型可能改写人类血小板生物学中的关键认识。

papers.title: Binding pocket optimization of Pueraria mirifica type II chalcone isomerase synergizing with a necrosis-attenuating host transcription factor for persistent daidzein biosynthesis.
papers.abstract: Pathway reconstitution of leguminous isoflavonoids in non-legume plant chassis offers a tractably controlled environment to probe specialized metabolism, yet it remains critically bottlenecked by suboptimal heterologous enzyme efficiency and severe host tissue necrosis. Here, we overcome these long-standing architectural limitations by establishing a highly synergistic, necrosis-attenuated Nicotiana benthamiana synthetic biology platform. We characterized chalcone isomerases from Pueraria mirifica (PmCHIs), revealing that PmCHI Type II operates as a biochemical junction exhibiting a specialized substrate-dependent alkaline optimum (pH 7.5-8.0) exclusively toward isoliquiritigenin. Combining 500-ns molecular dynamics simulations with structure-guided mutagenesis, active-site engineering identified an I195V variant with enhanced isoliquiritigenin preference. The conservative I195V substitution was predicted to reduce local steric crowding and produced an isoliquiritigenin selectivity ratio of 1.63 in vitro. For in planta pathway integration, we delivered a polycistronic cascade using P2A ribosome-skipping peptides to streamline multiplex multi-gene stacking. Crucially, substituting the conventional Arabidopsis thaliana MYB12 regulator with a host-derived N. benthamiana MYB60 transcription factor successfully attenuated tissue necrosis, accompanied by reduced electrolyte leakage. Quantitative proteomics showed no statistically significant difference in PmCHI abundance between the I195V and WT-II treatments in planta, while independent plant batches consistently showed higher daidzein accumulation with I195V, although the magnitude of enhancement varied among experiments. The NbMYB60-based platform extended the operational viability window up to 9 days, delivering a robust daidzein titer of 1.5 mg/g DW at 6 days post-infiltration, with individual high-performing replicates reaching up to 2.5 mg/g DW. Together, these results establish an integrated enzyme-engineering and necrosis-attenuating regulatory framework for persistent daidzein biosynthesis and specialized pathway reconstitution in planta.
papers.authors: Suntichaikamolkul N, Sanachai K, Nutho B, Rungrotmongkol T, Tubtimrattana A, Thirati P, Sucharitakul J, Sirikantaramas S.

papers.title: High efficient production of adenine in Bacillus subtilis with novel metabolic engineering strategies.
papers.abstract: Adenine, serves as a crucial precursor for nucleic acid drugs and food additives, currently suffered from limited availability since its high production costs associated with expensive precursors and enzyme preparations. Here, we developed an effective strategy for high-yield adenine production using Bacillus subtilis as the host. Beginning with an adenosine-producing strain, we first knocked-out the apt and adeC genes, which were involved in product degradation pathways, and deleted the purR gene to alleviate the feedback inhibition on purine operon through CRISPR-Cas9 technology. Then, we overexpressed the nucleoside hydrolase RihC, PRPP amidotransferase PurF, and ribokinase RbsK to enhance the de novo adenine biosynthesis and enable the recycling of D-ribose. The production of adenine reached 18 g/L after the fed-batch fermentation, and the titer continued to reach 78 g/L when adenosine was added as the substrate subsequently, revealing the significant catalytic role of RihC produced during the fermentation. This work innovatively integrated de novo biosynthesis and enzymatic conversion strategies to achieve high yield adenine production in Bacillus subtilis, demonstrating a promising scalable process for industrial adenine manufacturing.
papers.authors: Han S, Shen P, Ren H, Xu J, Chen F, Huang J, Zhou M, Xu Z.

enrichment.titleZh: 利用新型代谢工程策略在枯草芽孢杆菌中高效生产腺嘌呤
enrichment.abstractZh: 腺嘌呤是核酸药物及食品添加剂的重要前体，但昂贵的前体和酶制剂使其生产成本较高，限制了供应。本研究以枯草芽孢杆菌为宿主，开发了高产腺嘌呤策略。从腺苷生产菌株出发，研究者首先敲除与产物降解途径相关的 apt 和 adeC，并利用 CRISPR-Cas9 删除 purR，以解除对嘌呤操纵子的反馈抑制。随后过表达核苷水解酶 RihC、PRPP酰胺转移酶 PurF 和核糖激酶 RbsK，增强腺嘌呤从头合成并实现 D-核糖循环利用。补料分批发酵后，腺嘌呤产量达到18 g/L；随后添加腺苷作为底物，滴度进一步达到78 g/L，显示发酵过程中产生的 RihC 具有显著催化作用。该工作将从头生物合成与酶促转化相结合，实现枯草芽孢杆菌高产腺嘌呤，展示了有望放大用于工业制造的工艺。

papers.title: Innovative Microbial Chassis for Systems and Synthetic Biology.
papers.abstract: The development of microbial chassis has revolutionized systems and synthetic biology, enabling the rational engineering of microorganisms for the biosynthesis of high-value metabolites ranging from pharmaceuticals to biofuels. This chapter systematically explores widely used and emerging microbial chassis systems, with a focus on their core biological characteristics, inherent advantages and limitations, cutting-edge advances in genetic and metabolic engineering, and real-world industrial application progress. Well-established chassis represented by Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae remain the gold standard mainstream platforms in both academic research and industrial production. Meanwhile, the growing global demand for sustainable, high-titer bioproduction has driven the development and application of functionally specialized industrial chassis including Bacillus subtilis and Corynebacterium glutamicum, which offer unique metabolic traits, exceptional environmental stress resistance, and broad substrate versatility. This chapter also discusses the core criteria for chassis selection, including genetic stability, industrial scalability, biosafety, and metabolic flexibility, alongside their validated applications in manufacturing a diverse array of products from bulk organic acids to complex biopharmaceuticals. By systematically comparing these chassis systems across key performance metrics, this chapter provides actionable insights into rational chassis design empowered by integrated systems and synthetic biology, to enable efficient, robust, and scalable biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: Ma Y, Maglangit F, Wang S.

enrichment.titleZh: 面向系统与合成生物学的创新微生物底盘
enrichment.abstractZh: 微生物底盘的发展推动了系统与合成生物学，使人们能够理性改造微生物，合成从药物到生物燃料的高价值代谢物。本章系统讨论常用和新兴微生物底盘的核心生物学特征、固有优劣势、遗传及代谢工程前沿进展，以及实际工业应用。以大肠杆菌和酿酒酵母为代表的成熟底盘，仍是学术研究与工业生产中的主流平台。与此同时，可持续高滴度生物生产需求正推动功能特化的工业底盘开发，包括具有独特代谢特征、较强环境胁迫耐受及广泛底物适应性的枯草芽孢杆菌和谷氨酸棒杆菌。本章还讨论底盘选择的核心标准，如遗传稳定性、工业可放大性、生物安全和代谢灵活性，以及这些底盘在大宗有机酸至复杂生物药物制造中的已验证应用。通过比较不同底盘的关键性能，文章为融合系统与合成生物学的理性底盘设计提供指导，以实现高效、稳健、可放大的生物制造。

papers.title: MnWRKY22 Mediates Tissue-Specific Resveratrol Biosynthesis through Coordinated Regulation of the Stilbene Synthase Gene Cluster in Mulberry.
papers.abstract: Resveratrol, a pharmaceutically significant stilbenoid accumulates in mulberry roots. To elucidate the molecular mechanism underlying this tissue-specific biosynthesis, we systematically analyzed the stilbene synthase (STS) gene family in mulberry. Our investigation revealed that nine out of ten MnSTS genes form tandem repeats in a single genomic cluster. Co-expression clustering and phylogenetic analysis implied that these genes undergo purifying selection, resulting in highly consistent co-expression patterns across tissues, with particularly specific high expression in roots and calli. Subsequent weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified the transcription factor (TF) MnWRKY22 as a key regulatory candidate. Functional validation confirmed that MnWRKY22 is specifically expressed in roots and calli and directly binds to W-box elements in all MnSTS promoters, thereby activating their transcription. Suppression of MnWRKY22 expression significantly reduced both MnSTS transcript levels and resveratrol accumulation, while its overexpression enhanced MnSTS expression and resveratrol production. Notably, overexpression of MnWRKY22 in leaves ectopically activated otherwise silent MnSTSs, enabling de novo resveratrol synthesis. This study reveals the coordinated evolutionary characteristics of the MnSTS gene family and establishes MnWRKY22 as a unified regulator of tissue-specific resveratrol accumulation in mulberry. These findings provide a foundation for enhancing resveratrol production through metabolic engineering approaches.
papers.authors: Xia X, Yang Z, Wang Z, Yuan M, Xie Y, Zhao S, Li Y, Luo Y, Yuan J, He N.

enrichment.titleZh: MnWRKY22 通过协调调控桑树芪合酶基因簇，介导组织特异性白藜芦醇合成
enrichment.abstractZh: 具有药用意义的芪类化合物白藜芦醇在桑树根部积累。为解析其组织特异性合成机制，研究者系统分析了桑树芪合酶（STS）基因家族，发现10个 MnSTS 基因中的9个以串联重复形式构成单一基因组簇。共表达聚类和系统发育分析提示，这些基因受到纯化选择，在不同组织间表现出高度一致的共表达模式，尤其在根和愈伤组织中高表达。随后通过加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）筛选出转录因子 MnWRKY22。功能验证证实，该因子在根和愈伤组织中特异表达，能够直接结合所有 MnSTS 启动子中的 W-box 元件并激活转录。抑制 MnWRKY22 表达显著降低 MnSTS 转录水平和白藜芦醇积累；过表达则增强二者。值得注意的是，在叶片中过表达 MnWRKY22 可异位激活原本沉默的 MnSTS 基因，使叶片从头合成白藜芦醇。本研究揭示 MnSTS 基因家族协调演化的特征，并确定 MnWRKY22 是桑树组织特异性白藜芦醇积累的统一调控因子，为通过代谢工程提高产量提供基础。

papers.title: Serotype-Tailored Midstream and Downstream Operations to Advance the Manufacturing of Adeno-Associated Viral Vectors.
papers.abstract: Adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) are the leading vectors for in vivo gene therapy, fueling a growing demand for scalable and robust biomanufacturing processes. Yet, the impact of cell lysis conditions on the performance of midstream and downstream unit operations across serotypes remains poorly characterized. This study presents a serotype-resolved investigation of cell lysis and its cascading effects on AAV2, AAV5, AAV8, and AAV9 processing. A panel of lysis methods including inorganic agents, non-ionic and ionic detergents, and mechanical disruption was evaluated using an analytical framework of at- and off-line assays to quantify AAV yield, purity, and activity at each stage. Our results reveal pronounced serotype-specific differences: cetrimonium bromide (CTAB) delivered the highest transduction output of any condition evaluated for AAV8 (2.25 × 10 9 TU/mL) at 55.0% capture step yield, while sodium deoxycholate achieved ~ 98% host cell protein (HCP) reduction for AAV9 (HCP log reduction value 1.60) and the highest functional enrichment for AAV5 (6.73-fold) and AAV8 (5.80-fold). AAV2 proved uniquely challenging, with CTAB enabling the highest tangential flow filtration (TFF) yield. Acid precipitation paired with high salt addition reduced aggregation and improved permeate flux for AAV5 and AAV9. TFF performance was governed by the detergents' physicochemical properties: micelle-forming agents generated multicomponent complexes that fouled membranes in condition- and serotype-specific patterns. Rheological characterization revealed that all clarified lysates converged to the viscosity of the media after filtration, supporting transferable TFF parameters. Mixed-mode chromatography using a peptide-functionalized resin amplified lysis-imprinted differences, decoupling step yield from functional enrichment. Bayesian optimization of the chromatographic step improved purification outcomes: for AAV8 residual HCPs in the eluate decreased > 300-fold, from 0.91 mg/mL to 3 μg/mL, while for AAV9 the yield rose to ~95% at residual HCP as low as 14 μg/mL, demonstrating that purity and recovery are co-optimizable when lysis, midstream, and downstream conditions are rationally paired.
papers.authors: Minzoni A, Shastry S, Barbieri E, Hurst MR, Idanwekhai K, Wu Y, Ernst K, Chung WK, Bombeck C, Khan SA, Koley S, Kiss G, Rammo O, Tropsha A, Boi C, Daniele MA, Cramer S, Byrne B, Kaminsky S, Bennett AS, Menegatti S.

papers.title: Synthetic activation of gibberellin signalling reveals spatial coordination of root growth.
papers.abstract: Gibberellins (GAs) influence cell division and elongation, profoundly shaping plant architecture and yield. GA perception occurs when bioactive GAs bind the receptor GID1, promoting DELLA degradation and activating transcriptional programs. While GA signalling in the root endodermis is essential for promoting root elongation, the contributions of other layers have remained unclear. Here we developed a synthetic GA (sGA) that exhibits little or no binding to endogenous GID1, together with a modified GID1 (mGID1) engineered to selectively recognize sGA, enabling cell-specific activation of GA signalling in vivo. Using this system in Arabidopsis, we demonstrate that coordinated action of GA signalling in the endodermis and epidermis is required for full root elongation. Moreover, the distal spatial distribution of GA signalling and GA biosynthetic enzymes supports a model in which bioactive GAs are transported from GA3ox-expressing tissues to the endodermis and epidermis to coordinate root elongation. The sGA-mGID1 system provides a versatile platform for spatially precise reprogramming of hormone signalling, enabling synthetic control of developmental processes such as root-shoot growth balance, thereby advancing applications in plant synthetic biology and sustainable crop improvement.
papers.authors: Yagami Y, Yamada R, Ishikawa Y, Meguro E, Kusano S, Itami K, Frommer WB, Hagihara S, Nakamura M.

papers.title: Tremella fuciformis-derived extracellular vesicles promote cutaneous regeneration through modulation of inflammatory microenvironment and regenerative responses.
papers.abstract: The clinical translation of extracellular vesicle (EV)-based therapies is currently hindered by the high manufacturing costs and limited scalability of conventional mammalian cell sources. Edible fungus-derived EVs have emerged as a promising alternative with potential advantages in scalability and cost-effectiveness. Here, we investigated the therapeutic potential of EVs derived from Tremella fuciformis fermentation broth (TFB-EVs) for cutaneous wound healing. In a murine full-thickness wound model, TFB-EV treatment significantly accelerated wound closure, reducing the residual wound area to 6.87 ± 2.95% by day 14, compared with 21.63 ± 4.82% in the control group (p < 0.001). Histological analysis confirmed improved tissue quality, characterized by enhanced re-epithelialization and more organized collagen deposition. Functionally, TFB-EV treatment was associated with a coordinated repair response characterized by attenuation of inflammatory and oxidative stress responses during the early repair stage and enhancement of regenerative responses during tissue remodeling. These antioxidant responses were consistent with Nrf2-associated cytoprotective signaling, while inflammatory modulation was associated with suppression of IL-17/TNF-associated pathways. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of PI3K-Akt-associated signaling pathways, together with regenerative phenotypes including relief of G0/G1 cell cycle arrest and enhanced proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis activity of relevant cellular models. Combined with the practical advantages of liquid fermentation, TFB-EVs represent a promising fungal-derived bioactive nanotherapeutic platform with potential for future translational development. This work provides a cross-kingdom therapeutic strategy for wound repair and highlights the potential of scalable biomanufacturing approaches for future EV-based therapies.
papers.authors: Yu Q, Gu Z, Chen S, Chen Y, Chen F, Zhai H, Zhou L.

papers.title: A Systems View of Ganoderma Triterpenoids Biosynthesis: Signals, Transcription, and Biosynthetic Remodeling.
papers.abstract: Ganoderma triterpenoids (GTs), the major bioactive metabolites of Ganoderma lucidum , are widely known for their pharmaceutical versatility. However, their natural biosynthesis ability is insufficient to meet industrial demands, so it is urgently required to clarify the metabolic network of GTs and develop new strategies to increase the total GTs production. Recently, the complex multi-tiered regulatory framework, which includes the sequential integration of environmental perception, signal transduction, and transcriptional reprogramming, has been fully dissected. This review synthesizes recent breakthroughs that illustrate how environmental stimuli are transduced through independent or intricate spatiotemporal interactions involving reactive oxygen species (ROS), calcium ions (Ca 2+ ), and nitric oxide (NO). Such interplays give rise to oscillatory or feedback loops that precisely modulate metabolic production. Moreover, we systematically examine various transcription factors that control metabolic fluxes by either directly targeting the rate-limiting enzymatic steps of the mevalonate (MVA) pathway and downstream CYP450-modification networks, or via epigenetic and complex-mediated pathways. Importantly, we consider the application of gene editing, AI/ML-guided enzyme engineering, and subcellular compartmentalization as innovative ways to overcome their yield bottlenecks. Successful heterologous construction of biosynthetic pathways highlights the continuing trend towards predictability in biomanufacturing. In summary, this review presents a holistic translational approach from foundational regulatory mechanisms to synthetic assembly, establishing G. lucidum as a viable and intelligent bio-manufacturer for producing high valuable GTs.
papers.authors: Cui M, Gao X, Zhao W, Wang J, Wu Y, Zhang X.

papers.title: A transient expression platform for rapid metabolic engineering of artemisinin biosynthesis in Artemisia annua .
papers.abstract: Artemisinin, a sesquiterpene lactone produced in glandular trichomes of Artemisia annua , remains a key compound for artemisinin-based combination therapies against malaria. Although stable transformation has been widely used to enhance artemisinin production, rapid in planta systems for testing metabolic engineering strategies in A. annua remain limited. In this study, we developed a transient expression system based on vacuum agroinfiltration of whole A. annua plants, providing a fast and flexible tool to explore the engineering potential of the artemisinin pathway. Using GFP as a reporter, we established experimental conditions that support reproducible transient expression, identifying in vitro -grown plants as the most suitable material. We then assembled five key genes of the artemisinin biosynthetic pathway into a single multigene construct and tested its ability to redirect metabolism in both Nicotiana benthamiana and A. annua . While heterologous expression in N. benthamiana did not lead to detectable artemisinin-related metabolites, transient expression in A. annua produced a measurable, although temporary, shift in the specialized metabolome. At 2 dpi, targeted LC-HRMS analysis showed that artemisinin content increased from 0.086 ± 0.015 to 0.123 ± 0.012 mg/g fresh weight, while deoxyartemisinin and several putative sesquiterpenoid compounds also increased in relative abundance, suggesting that the introduced pathway genes influenced metabolic flux. These effects faded over time, revealing the strong endogenous regulatory constraints that shape artemisinin accumulation in its native plant host. Overall, this work establishes a rapid in planta platform for probing and modulating specialized metabolism in A. annua . Beyond artemisinin, it highlights the value of transient expression as a bridge between molecular design and plant-based production, supporting the broader vision of plants as dynamic biofactories for health-relevant natural products.
papers.authors: Pietrolucci F, Valesi V, Sgaravatti E, Guzzo F, Negri S, Avesani L.

papers.title: Auxiliary glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenases shape central carbon metabolism in Pseudomonas putida .
papers.abstract: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenases (GapDHs) are key enzymes in central carbon metabolism, yet their functional diversity extends beyond canonical glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. The soil bacterium Pseudomonas putida KT2440 encodes four GapDH isoenzymes (i.e., GapA, GapB, GapC, and GapD). GapA and GapB have been recently described as gatekeepers of metabolic segregation, with GapA driving glycolysis and GapB associated with gluconeogenesis. However, the physiological roles of GapC and GapD remain poorly defined. In this work, we combined targeted mutagenesis, growth phenotyping, in vitro biochemical analysis, proteomics, and metabolomics to dissect the functions of these lesser-studied GapDH isoforms. GapC and GapD have distinct structural features, diverging from the canonical GapA and GapB enzymes. Physiological characterization of gap -deletion mutants of P. putida across multiple glycolytic and gluconeogenic substrates showed that GapC and GapD exert substrate-specific effects and contribute to network-wide redox balancing. Proteomic and metabolomic profiling further indicated that GapC and GapD are integrated into specialized metabolic modules, supporting auxiliary functions that complement the dominant roles of GapA and GapB. This case of metabolic redundancy at the GapDH node highlights the versatility of central carbon metabolism in bacteria adapted to changing environmental conditions. Importance Bacteria often carry multiple isoenzymes for the same metabolic step, yet the reasons for such redundancy remain poorly understood. By dissecting the roles of GapDH isoforms in P. putida , we show that these enzymes are not functionally equivalent but rather partition their activity across glycolytic, gluconeogenic, and auxiliary functions. GapC and GapD provide secondary capacity under specific conditions that complement the known roles of GapA and GapB, which dominate glycolysis and gluconeogenesis, respectively. Growth phenotyping, together with proteomic and metabolomic analyses, revealed that isoenzyme specialization is reflected in both substrate-dependent abundance patterns and metabolite profiles. This study underscores the evolutionary diversification of central metabolic enzymes in environmental bacteria and their coordinated regulation across nutritional states. Furthermore, our findings provide a framework for engineering carbon flux in Pseudomonas and related bacteria, with implications for metabolic engineering applications targeting diverse feedstocks.
papers.authors: Dekker NK, Partipilo M, Jeeva P, Nieto-Domínguez M, de Jong I, McNaught KJ, Carroll AL, Krink N, Guss AM, Aristilde L, Nikel PI.

papers.title: Biochemical characterization of the mannojirimycin biosynthetic enzymes reveals metal ion- and pH-dependent catalysis in Bacillus atrophaeus MBLB1156 isolated from red fermented bean curd (Hong fu ru).
papers.abstract: 1-Deoxynojirimycin (DNJ) and its C2 epimer, 1-deoxymannojirimycin (DMJ), are pharmaceutically relevant iminosugars. Although the gabT1-yktc1-gutB1 gene cluster has been implicated in the biosynthesis of mannojirimycin (MJ), a common precursor of DNJ and DMJ, the coordinated biochemical properties of the pathway enzymes remain poorly understood. Here, we isolated a DMJ-producing strain, Bacillus atrophaeus MBLB1156, from Hong fu ru and identified a gabT1-yktc1-gutB1 cluster by whole-genome sequencing. Comparative genomic analysis of 99 Bacillus genomes further revealed that the cluster of MBLB1156 belongs to a distinct evolutionary lineage. Biochemical analyses showed that rBatGabT1 preferentially aminated fructose-6-phosphate using L-glutamate, while rBatYktc1 exhibited metal ion- and pH-dependent phosphatase activity. rBatGutB1 was characterized as a Zn 2+ -binding NAD(P)-dependent dehydrogenase with an alkaline pH optimum. The assembled three-enzyme cascade synthesized MJ, which was subsequently converted to DMJ by chemical reduction, providing biochemical evidence for the proposed biosynthetic pathway. Cell extract assays further showed that DMJ production was favored under neutral to mildly alkaline conditions despite the more alkaline pH optima of rBatGabT1 and rBatGutB1, indicating that the distinct biochemical properties of the three enzymes collectively influence pathway activity. These findings advance our biochemical understanding of MJ biosynthesis of B. atrophaeus and provide a foundation for metabolic engineering and biocatalytic production of iminosugars.
papers.authors: Lim HJ, Chun J, Baek S, Lee S, Jung JH, Seo MJ.

papers.title: Cucurbitacins as multitarget pharmacological modulators: chemistry, biosynthesis, molecular targets, regulated cell death, and translational challenges, with emphasis on cucurbitacin B and I.
papers.abstract: Cucurbitacins are highly oxidized tetracyclic triterpenoids with context-dependent pharmacological effects. This review focuses primarily on cucurbitacin B (CuB) and cucurbitacin I (CuI)-the most extensively characterized family members-while surveying the wider structural diversity of the cucurbitacin family. We integrate their chemistry, biosynthesis, and structure-activity relationships with structural interpretations of molecular target engagement and translational feasibility. We highlight how the electrophilic α,β-unsaturated ketone, C-17 side chain, acetylation, and glycosylation may influence potency and selectivity. Mechanistically, we evaluate Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 signaling, ferroptosis involving solute carrier family 7 member 11 and glutathione peroxidase 4, PTEN-induced kinase 1-Parkin-dependent mitophagy, allosteric modulation of insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 1, and NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 inflammasome inhibition. We consider anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective effects, tumor-associated macrophage repolarization, and sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade. Experimentally determined protein structures inform proposed covalent and allosteric interactions, but these models require direct target validation and biomarkers. We distinguish compound-specific findings from family-wide interpretations. Effects may vary with compound, dose, and disease context. By connecting these pathways to wax gourd genomic resources and synthetic-biology approaches, we consider opportunities for sustainable cucurbitacin production. However, low aqueous solubility, rapid clearance, hepatotoxicity, and a narrow therapeutic index constrain clinical translation. We assess nanoparticle formulations, solid dispersions, and structure-guided analog development as possible solutions. Distinct from cucurbitacin B-centered reviews, this synthesis integrates structural pharmacology, regulated cell death, immunomodulation, and biosynthetic engineering within a research roadmap prioritizing target validation, biomarkers, and preclinical assessment.
papers.authors: Li S, Fang T, Mao Q.

papers.title: Genetic Biosensors for High-Throughput Biomedical Applications: Challenges and Advances.
papers.abstract: Genetic biosensors represent a particularly promising class of bioengineered instruments designed to enable accurate, real-time monitoring of cellular and molecular processes, with especially strong relevance to high-throughput biomedical workflows. In this review, we provide a systematic, clearly structured overview of the field, covering the fundamental design principles that form the basis of today's platforms. We focus in particular on DNA-based, RNA-based, and CRISPR-based architectures while also examining engineered synthetic biology circuitry, and we place these foundational concepts in the context of more recent advances. These developments encompass improved sensitivity, increased scalability, and broader functionality for multiplexed detection. Beyond summarizing technological progress, we critically evaluate challenges that remain deeply embedded at both technical and biological levels, including limitations driven by signal-to-noise ratio constraints, practical difficulties in delivering probes into cells, and relatively restricted dynamic ranges. Taken together, these issues continue to hinder widespread, routine clinical adoption. Importantly, rather than presenting the topic only as a catalog of improvements, we argue for a unifying framework: the convergence of artificial intelligence and synthetic biology is actively reshaping biosensor engineering, moving it away from a largely empirical, trial-and-error approach toward a more reliable, data-driven discipline. To convert this conceptual shift into tangible outcomes, we also outline a practical implementation framework aimed at reducing the distance between research activities and real-world deployment. This framework emphasizes the need for scalable manufacturing processes, robust and reproducible clinical validation, and regulatory pathways capable of evolving as new evidence emerges. An integrated strategy of this kind is therefore essential for fully realizing the potential of real-time, multichannel biosensing platforms in both complex clinical diagnostics and point-of-care environments.
papers.authors: Ahvaraki A, Teimouri M, Shirvani-Farsani Z, Omidfar K.

papers.title: Methyl jasmonate induces the biosynthesis and accumulation of triterpenoid saponins in Polygala tenuifolia hairy roots.
papers.abstract: Polygala tenuifolia Willd. is an important medicinal plant widely applied in traditional Chinese medicine. Its pharmacological activities are primarily derived from triterpenoid saponins and other specialized metabolites. Nevertheless, the regulatory mechanisms governing methyl jasmonate (MeJA)-triggered accumulation of bioactive constituents in P. tenuifolia remain poorly characterized. In this study, to evaluate corresponding changes in biomass and characteristic metabolite production, hairy root cultures of P. tenuifolia were subjected to MeJA treatment at concentrations spanning 0-400 µM over a 1-6 day period. MeJA modulated hairy root growth and secondary metabolite accumulation in a concentration-dependent and time-dependent manner. Compared with the control group, the contents of onjisaponin B and polygalasaponin III increased by 1.81-fold and 2.60-fold, respectively, following treatment with 50 µM MeJA for 3 days. A total of 447 differentially expressed transcription factors (TFs) that belonged to 64 families were identified through transcriptome analysis. MeJA suppressed the expression of most TF families, whereas the NAC family exhibited a global upregulation trend. The above results indicated that MeJA activated transcriptional reprogramming of secondary-metabolism-associated genes via targeted regulation of specific TFs. Correlation analysis involving ten key enzyme genes and six characteristic metabolites demonstrated that the majority of biosynthetic genes were positively associated with bioactive metabolite levels. Of these genes, UGT74B1 and UGT73B2 showed strong positive correlations with multiple saponin components; CYP94A2 served as a critical node responsible for oxidative modification. In contrast, MK and HDS displayed negative correlations with saponins, which suggested precursor competition across distinct terpenoid pathways. As indicated by RT-qPCR validation for ten candidate biosynthetic genes, MeJA time-dependently upregulated key genes participating in the MVA/MEP pathways, squalene cyclization, CYP450-mediated oxidation, and UGT-catalyzed glycosylation, thereby facilitating precursor supply and subsequent structural modification. Accordingly, triterpenoid saponin biosynthesis and accumulation in P. tenuifolia hairy roots were enhanced. This study offers fresh understanding of the molecular basis underlying MeJA-modulated secondary metabolism in P. tenuifolia, and identifies candidate genes applicable to metabolic engineering for elevating yields of bioactive compounds in hairy root cultures.
papers.authors: Ji H, Yang B, Lai N, Zhang L, Yang Y, Zhao X, Wang F, Peng L.
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology

papers.title: Microbial CO 2 bioconversion: integrating carbon fixation pathways and sustainable biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: The continued rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations has intensified the need for sustainable technologies capable of mitigating greenhouse gas emissions while generating value-added products. In this context, microbial CO 2 bioconversion has emerged as a promising biological strategy within broader carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) frameworks, particularly through biological carbon capture and utilization (bio-CCU). These approaches enable the conversion of inorganic carbon into fuels, chemicals, biomaterials, proteins, and other value-added products. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent advances in microbial CO 2 bioconversion by bridging biological, technological, and industrial perspectives. Unlike previous reviews focusing on individual topics, such as carbon fixation pathways, gas fermentation, or metabolic engineering, this work presents an integrated framework connecting natural and synthetic carbon fixation pathways, microbial production platforms, metabolic engineering strategies, product diversification, and techno-economic considerations. To support this analysis, we conducted a systematic bibliometric assessment of 913 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, revealing sustained growth in scientific output, increasing interdisciplinarity, structured collaboration networks, and strong thematic interconnections across microbial ecology, carbon fixation, metabolism, and carbon utilization. Recent advances in synthetic biology, systems-level metabolic engineering, microbial electrosynthesis, bioelectrochemical systems, synthetic microbial consortia, and artificial intelligence-assisted strain engineering are discussed as important drivers of microbial carbon utilization. The review also critically examines major barriers to industrial implementation, including CO 2 mass transfer, carbon fixation efficiency, energy constraints, process scale-up, downstream processing, and economic feasibility. By integrating systematic bibliometric evidence with a critical assessment of microbial CO 2 biomanufacturing, this review identifies the convergence of microbial physiology, metabolic engineering, bioprocess development, renewable energy, and data-driven approaches as central to advancing biological CO 2 conversion toward scalable, sustainable biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: de Souza Sevalho E, da Silva DS, de Sousa Gomes K, da Conceição L, Okamura LA, Medina-Gallardo JC.

papers.title: Ortho -alkyl phenylalkenoyl natural products: structural diversity, bioactivities and biosynthesis.
papers.abstract: Covering: up to 2026. Ortho -alkyl phenylalkenoyl-containing natural products, including cinnamoyl-containing nonribosomal peptides (CCNPs) and ortho -alkyl phenylalkenoic acids (APAs), are structurally and biologically diverse bacterial metabolites that have become a major focus of natural product research. These metabolites exhibit broad bioactivities, including antimicrobial, antiangiogenic, cytotoxic, anti-inflammatory, and nematicidal effects. Biosynthetically, CCNPs and APAs share a conserved, highly reduced (HR) type II polyketide synthase (PKS)-derived framework, featuring characteristic isoenzymes (ISOs) and specialised cyclases that assemble the ortho -alkyl phenylalkenoyl core. They diverge fundamentally in pathway architecture: CCNPs contain NRPS-synthesised peptide backbones, whereas APAs lack NRPS components and possess expanded KS/CLF pairs. Biosynthetic studies have revealed novel mechanisms ( e.g. , isomerization, 6π-electrocyclisation) and multifunctional enzymes, providing valuable biocatalysts for synthetic biology. Although their biological activities depend strongly on structural context, emerging evidence highlights these metabolites as a promising source of lead compounds. Continued interdisciplinary efforts integrating natural product chemistry, biosynthesis, and medicinal chemistry are expected to unlock their therapeutic potential.
papers.authors: Huang Q, Chen X, Ma S, Li Z, Sun P.

papers.title: Reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages in breast cancer: from myeloid plasticity and tumor-promoting programs to CAR-macrophage therapy.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer develops within spatially organized, multicellular microenvironments in which particular tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) states can influence immune access and stromal remodeling. Conventional M1/M2 classification and total macrophage density fail to capture the developmental, transcriptional, metabolic, and spatial heterogeneity that determines TAM function. This macrophage-focused review examines breast cancer within its multicellular microenvironment, integrating lineage-tracing, single-cell, spatial, mechanistic, and clinical evidence while distinguishing breast-specific findings from hypotheses extrapolated from other tumors. We examine how tissue-resident and monocyte-derived macrophages are recruited, retained, expanded, and reprogrammed across primary and metastatic sites, emphasizing interactions with malignant cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, vasculature, adipose tissue, and lymphoid populations. In defined breast-tumor contexts, TAM programs have been implicated in immune exclusion, invasion, metastatic dissemination, and adaptation to systemic treatment, although evidence strength varies across mechanisms and therapeutic modalities. Small and heterogeneous clinical studies have not established a benefit from broad CSF1/CSF1R-axis targeting in breast cancer, despite encouraging preclinical findings. Accordingly, we highlight a shift toward state-selective, spatially resolved, and temporally coordinated targeting. Emerging approaches include restoring phagocytosis, disrupting chemokine and fibrotic circuits, metabolic reprogramming, and converting suppressive TAMs into inflammatory, antigen-presenting effectors. A major focus is chimeric antigen receptor macrophage (CAR-M) therapy, which combines antigen-directed phagocytosis with tumor infiltration, matrix remodeling, antigen presentation, and recruitment of endogenous immunity. Although early clinical data support manufacturing feasibility, tumor trafficking, and acceptable initial safety, limited antitumor activity underscores challenges involving antigen heterogeneity, persistence, metabolic fitness, biodistribution, and scalable production. We propose a translational roadmap integrating spatial biomarkers, quantitative target selection, macrophage-adapted CAR design, checkpoint-resistant phagocytosis, metabolic engineering, safety switches, and biomarker-guided combination therapy. This framework positions macrophage reprogramming as a context-dependent strategy for modifying selected breast-tumor niches, with therapeutic targets chosen according to the macrophage program and its surrounding cellular architecture.
papers.authors: Heydari F, Derakhshani M, Naghinezhad J.

enrichment.titleZh: 乳腺癌肿瘤相关巨噬细胞重编程：从髓系可塑性和促瘤程序到 CAR 巨噬细胞治疗
enrichment.abstractZh: 乳腺癌发生于具有空间组织结构的多细胞微环境中，特定状态的肿瘤相关巨噬细胞（TAM）可影响免疫细胞进入及基质重塑。传统 M1/M2 分类和总巨噬细胞密度，无法充分描述决定 TAM 功能的发育、转录、代谢及空间异质性。本综述以巨噬细胞为中心，整合谱系追踪、单细胞、空间、机制和临床证据，并区分乳腺癌特异性发现与从其他肿瘤外推的假设。文章考察组织驻留及单核细胞来源巨噬细胞如何在原发和转移部位被募集、保留、扩增和重编程，强调其与癌细胞、癌相关成纤维细胞、细胞外基质、血管、脂肪及淋巴细胞群的相互作用。在特定乳腺肿瘤背景中，TAM程序与免疫排斥、侵袭、转移播散及系统治疗适应有关，但不同机制和治疗方式的证据强度不一。尽管临床前结果令人期待，规模较小且异质性较大的临床研究尚未证实广泛靶向 CSF1/CSF1R 轴对乳腺癌的获益。因此，文章强调向状态选择性、空间分辨及时间协调的靶向策略转变，包括恢复吞噬、干预趋化因子和纤维化回路、代谢重编程，以及将抑制性 TAM 转化为炎性抗原呈递效应细胞。重点介绍的嵌合抗原受体巨噬细胞（CAR-M）疗法结合抗原定向吞噬、肿瘤浸润、基质重塑、抗原呈递及内源免疫募集。早期临床数据支持制造可行性、肿瘤归巢和初步可接受安全性，但有限的抗肿瘤活性凸显抗原异质性、持续性、代谢适应、分布及规模化生产等挑战。作者提出整合空间生物标志物、定量靶点选择、适配巨噬细胞的 CAR 设计、抗检查点抑制吞噬、代谢工程、安全开关及生物标志物指导联合治疗的转化路线，将巨噬细胞重编程视为依赖具体情境、用于改变特定乳腺肿瘤生态位的策略。

papers.title: Synthetic biology as a game-changer for endangered medicinal orchids: biosynthesis, engineering and conservation.
papers.abstract: Covering: 2012 to 2026Medicinal orchids constitute a rich yet vulnerable reservoir of high-value bioactive metabolites. However, their sustainable exploitation is severely hampered by resource depletion and the inefficiency of traditional extraction. Synthetic biology emerges as a transformative game-changer to resolve this impasse. This review delineates how synthetic biology drives a paradigm shift in endangered orchid conservation. Through modular design of biosynthetic pathways, heterologous reconstruction in microbial or plant chassis, directed evolution of key enzymes, metabolic engineering, and scalable production, it offers a disruptive solution, fundamentally redefining sustainable utilization by decoupling supply from ecological extraction. We highlight the successful heterologous biosynthesis of representative compounds like gastrodin and dendrobine. Facilitated by pathway optimization, chassis engineering and synthetic consortia design, these efforts have established cell factories that demonstrate the potential for sustainable and non-plant-based production, offering a viable alternative to wild harvest. Furthermore, the research encompasses recent breakthroughs in decoding orchid metabolic networks, including the elucidation of biosynthetic pathways, identification of core enzyme repertoires and discovery of regulatory switches involving transcription factors and miRNAs. Insights from evolutionary genomics and endophyte symbioses are also discussed as critical guides for pathway optimization. We explore the translational impact of these innovations, highlighting how the integration of multi-omics, artificial intelligence and gene editing accelerates the Design-Build-Test-Learn cycle. In summary, synthetic biology represents an essential paradigm shift, transitioning orchid resource management from a narrative of scarcity to one of predictable engineering creation and thereby securing a robust and sustainable supply chain for these prized medicinal plants.
papers.authors: Qiu L, Chen X, Luo Z, Jiang M, Chen H, Hou B, Yu H, Li N, Zhang L.

papers.title: Alginate-methacrylate-RGD microspheres (Alg-MR-MS) for cell expansion and delivery in tissue engineering.
papers.abstract: Clinically relevant cell numbers are essential for many tissue engineering applications, requiring scalable expansion platforms. Microcarrier-based bioreactor systems address this demand; however, conventional non-dissolvable carriers require harsh enzymatic or mechanical detachment, reducing cell viability and integrity. Although dissolvable microcarriers improve recovery, most are designed only for harvesting and lack functionality for downstream tissue engineering. Here, we present a sequential dual-crosslinkable alginate-methacrylate-RGD microsphere system (Alg-MR-MS) that integrates scalable cell expansion with scaffold formation in a single platform. The workflow involves: (1) microsphere fabrication via calcium-mediated ionic crosslinking; (2) three-dimensional cell expansion in a microcarrier culture system; (3) controlled phase change through calcium chelation with sodium citrate, enabling efficient cell recovery while preserving viability and phenotype; and (4) photocrosslinking to form a stable, cell-laden hydrogel suitable for bioprinting and tissue engineering. This sequential dual-crosslinking strategy supports expansion, dissolution, and structural stabilisation within one system. Human adipose-derived stem cells cultured on Alg-MR-MS showed ∼5-fold increased metabolic activity over 7 d, comparable to 2D controls, with high viability and strong attachment. Compared with other dissolvable carriers, Alg-MR-MS offers efficient expansion, rapid phase transition, and simplified single-step fabrication, bridging biomanufacturing and functional tissue engineering.
papers.authors: Mendes AX, Duchi S, Onofrillo C, Zhou Y, Gambhir S, do Nascimento AT, O'Connell C, Posniak S, Mukherjee P, Wallace GG, Choong PF, Moulton SE.

papers.title: Anabaena , a multicellular model for cyanobacterial cell biology and biotechnology.
papers.abstract: Heterocyst-forming cyanobacteria (order Nostocales) are a monophyletic group of organisms that grow as filaments usually made of dozens to hundreds of cells (termed vegetative cells) that can perform oxygenic photosynthesis. Under combined nitrogen deficiency, some cells in the filament differentiate into N 2 -fixing heterocysts, which do not produce oxygen and, indeed, keep a microoxic environment appropriate for the expression and functioning of the N 2 -fixing enzyme, nitrogenase. Thus, in the diazotrophic filament, oxygenic photosynthesis and N 2 fixation are segregated into two different cell types, vegetative cells and heterocysts, which require intercellular molecular exchange to feed each other with fixed nitrogen and reduced carbon, respectively. The current understanding of heterocyst biology, including regulation of heterocyst differentiation, which also involves intercellular signaling, is the result of studying mainly a few strains of the genus Anabaena . Here, we review the classical studies that established Anabaena as a model for the Nostocales and clarified the basics of N 2 fixation in these organisms. Then, we show how molecular genetics came into the scene and how it was complemented by genomic analysis. This, together with the introduction of modern cell biology approaches, led to a renewed understanding of cellular differentiation and unraveled a system for intercellular communication that is unique in the biological world. In turn, the new accumulated knowledge on Anabaena physiology and genetics makes these organisms an excellent system for the development of new synthetic biology tools that will be crucial for their use in biotechnology.
papers.authors: Flores E, Luque I, López-Igual R.

papers.title: Catalysis and allostery in bacterial ATP phosphoribosyltransferases.
papers.abstract: ATP phosphoribosyltransferase (ATPPRT) catalyses the first reaction of L-histidine biosynthesis: the condensation of ATP and 5-phospho-α-d-ribose 1-pyrophosphate to form N 1 -(5-phospho-β-d-ribosyl)-ATP with the release of inorganic pyrophosphate. L-Histidine allosterically inhibits ATPPRT as a mechanism to regulate this energy-intensive pathway in histidine-synthesising organisms, such as bacteria, archaea and plants. Absent in humans and essential in many disease-causing bacteria, such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Acinetobacter baumannii, ATPPRT is a promising drug target for novel antibiotic development. Furthermore, ATPPRT is a target of synthetic biology efforts to maximise L-histidine production in bacteria. Here we provide a brief overview of allosteric concepts and review the structure, catalysis and allosteric mechanism of bacterial ATPPRTs, which exist in two forms in nature, a long and a short form. We highlight recent findings on ATPPRT catalysis, allosteric regulation, inhibition and activation, discuss open questions in the field, and possible industrial and biomedical applications.
papers.authors: Bates LG, da Silva RG.

papers.title: De novo production of mandelic- and 3-phenyllactic acid from lignocellulosic feedstock through Phlebia radiata IBWF-87241.
papers.abstract: Background Phlebia radiata is a white-rot basidiomycete that secretes a repertoire of oxidative enzymes making it a promising organism for the sustainable bio-production of aromatic compounds during lignocellulose-containing cultivation. Here, we investigate the association between wood supplementation and extracellular production of aromatic α-hydroxy acids by P. radiata IBWF 87241 under defined axenic conditions, while accompanying changes in extracellular oxidative enzyme activity and residual wood fibres were characterized using enzyme assays and ATR-FTIR spectroscopy. Results GC-EI-MS analysis of culture filtrate extracts, confirmed by authentic standards, revealed two aromatic α-hydroxy acids produced exclusively under wood-containing conditions. Mandelic acid and 3-phenyllactic acid were produced by P. radiata in ½ soy medium supplemented with 1% (w/v) spruce wood powder, but were absent from un-supplemented and uninoculated controls across repeated cultivation experiments. Continuous monitoring of the cultivation shows that extracellular laccase activity increased throughout fermentation and reached a maximum on day 7, whereas H₂O₂-dependent ABTS oxidation remained low throughout the experiment, while esterase activity showed a minor transient increase. ATR-FTIR analysis of recovered wood powder revealed reproducible treatment-associated spectral differences relative to untreated controls in regions assigned to lignin- and carbohydrate-associated functional groups. Scale-up cultivation in a 20 L stirred-tank bioreactor yielded preliminary titers of 0.79 mg/L mandelic acid and 4.11 mg/L 3-phenyllactic acid, establishing baseline production levels under controlled process conditions. Conclusions These findings establish P. radiata IBWF 87241 as a non-engineered fungal host for the production of aromatic α-hydroxy acids under wood-containing cultivation conditions and provide a quantitative baseline for future metabolic engineering and bioprocess optimisation strategies targeting mandelic acid and 3-phenyllactic acid production. To our knowledge, this is the first report of production of mandelic acid and 3-phenyllactic acid by P. radiata under defined cultivation conditions. The combined characterization of extracellular oxidative activity, FTIR spectral differences in recovered wood, and aromatic α-hydroxy acid production provides a framework for future investigations of extracellular oxidative metabolism, substrate-associated spectral alterations, and aromatic metabolite formation during fungal lignocellulose conversion.
papers.authors: Dulaj A, Völlger IM, Zoth J, Akpan E, Wetzel B, Grünewald C, Jacob S, Antelo L, Thines E.

papers.title: Efficient fucoxanthin production by fed-batch photo-fermentation cultivation of genetically engineered heterotrophic-growth Phaeodactylum tricornutum.
papers.abstract: The marine diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum is considered a promising platform for commercial fucoxanthin production due to its naturally high fucoxanthin content. However, its industrial application remains limited by low biomass productivity and high production costs associated with conventional photoautotrophic cultivation. To address these challenges, metabolic engineering was employed to convert the obligate photoautotrophic strain into a glucose-utilizing strain capable of heterotrophic growth, thereby enabling high-density cultivation. In this study, the wild-type P. tricornutum Pt1 was genetically engineered, and the transformant Glut1-45 was identified as the superior strain based on its enhanced growth performance compared with other transformants. Subsequently, an efficient photo-fermentation process was developed through systematic optimization of cultivation conditions for Glut1-45. The results demonstrated that light supplementation, together with a mixed nitrogen source containing inorganic sodium nitrate and organic tryptone, markedly enhanced glucose utilization and cell growth. Moreover, Glut1-45 exhibited no significant growth inhibition at glucose concentrations below 10 g L -1 , whereas concentrations exceeding 20 g L -1 significantly inhibited cell proliferation. By maintaining glucose concentrations below 5 g L -1 during fed-batch photo-fermentation, high-cell-density cultivation and enhanced fucoxanthin production were successfully achieved. The maximum biomass concentration reached 10.05 g L -1 , while the maximum fucoxanthin content reached 14.87 mg g -1 dry cell weight, yielding the highest fucoxanthin titer of 146.58 mg L -1 . These results demonstrate the potential of integrating metabolic engineering for glucose utilization with fed-batch photo-fermentation to achieve high-cell-density cultivation and enhanced volumetric fucoxanthin production, providing a feasible strategy for efficient P. tricornutum-based fucoxanthin biomanufacturing.
papers.authors: Jin H, Hu Z, Hao X, Li C, Pan Y, Hu H.

papers.title: From genome editing to chromosome engineering in plants.
papers.abstract: Engineering large genomic segments is rapidly expanding the scope of plant genome manipulation from individual genes to chromosome-scale redesign. Recent advances in double-strand break-, prime-editing-, recombinase-, and transposase-based technologies now enable programmable deletion, insertion, replacement, duplication, inversion, and translocation of DNA fragments ranging from kilobases to megabases. In this review, we summarize the major strategies for large-fragment genome engineering in plants, compare their strengths and limitations, and discuss their applications in both fundamental plant biology and crop breeding. We further highlight that the integration of artificial intelligence is catalyzing the rapid optimization of large-fragment genome engineering. The ongoing transition from genome editing to chromosome engineering promises to revolutionize crop breeding and plant synthetic biology, ultimately enabling rational design of plant genomes.
papers.authors: Lei Y, Wu J, Gao C.

papers.title: Host physiological constraints limit microbial production of partially acetylated chitooligosaccharides.
papers.abstract: Chitooligosaccharides (COS) are versatile biomolecules with applications across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic industries. Expanding the COS portfolio, particularly with partially acetylated COS (paCOS) possessing defined structural characteristics, including degree of deacetylation and pattern of acetylation, is essential for advancing structure-function studies and enabling tailored applications. This study investigates the heterologous co-expression of chitin deacetylases (CDAs) with a chitin oligosaccharide synthase (oCS) RhNodC in Escherichia coli for the in vivo production of paCOS. Although this approach enables paCOS formation, co-expression of NodC and CDAs results in reduced COS yields and incomplete conversion of fully acetylated COS into paCOS. To identify potential cellular bottlenecks underlying these limitations, stress responses were monitored using a stress promoter-based fluorescent reporter system. CDA co-expression activated protein quality control and membrane-associated stress responses. Furthermore, confocal microscopy revealed altered intracellular localization of both RhNodC and CDAs compared to individual expression, with enzymes detected in the cytoplasm, membrane and inclusion bodies. Co-expression also resulted in pronounced cellular elongation, further indicating cellular stress during pathway implementation. Together, these findings reveal cellular bottlenecks associated with enzyme co-expression and highlight the need for deeper exploration of RhNodC-CDA co-expression and approaches to mitigate cellular stress to improve in vivo paCOS production.
papers.authors: Snoeck S, Malik H, Demeester W, Duchi D, Lips W, Guidi C, Moerschbacher BM, De Mey M.

papers.title: Interaction between the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway and chlororespiration sustains high-rate algal exoelectrogenesis.
papers.abstract: Photosynthetic microorganisms enable the conversion of sunlight into electricity via exoelectrogenesis - the export of electrons to the extracellular environment. However, current strategies to enhance this process often rely on nutrient deprivation, such as iron limitation, which inevitably compromises the photosynthetic apparatus and arrests cell growth. Here, we investigate the physiological basis of the inherently enhanced exoelectrogenesis in the green microalga Parachlorella kessleri MACC-38 - a strain that exhibits tenfold higher electric current production than the model alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii without requiring stress treatments. We propose that upon exposure to ferricyanide as an extracellular electron sink, the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway (OPPP) is upregulated - specifically via glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase - to supply NADPH as the primary reducing power for exoelectrogenesis. Furthermore, we suggest that while the OPPP supports electron export, it simultaneously induces a transient over-reduction of the photosynthetic electron transport chain. Our data indicates that chlororespiration, mediated by the plastid terminal oxidase (PTOX), is essential to maintain redox homeostasis by re-oxidizing the plastoquinone pool, while sustaining exoelectrogenesis. These results may find application in the rational design of highly exoelectrogenic microorganisms with synthetic biology tools for sustainable, high-efficiency biophotovoltaic systems.
papers.authors: Petrova NZ, Kuntam S, Szabó M, Shaikh KM, Kajner G, Zlámal T, Zavřel T, Galbács G, Tóth SZ.

papers.title: Multienzyme cascades for non-grain carbon feedstocks valorization: Recent advances and perspectives.
papers.abstract: Biomanufacturing is increasingly transitioning toward sustainable non-grain carbon feedstocks, including gaseous C1 compounds, liquid C1 substrates, and solid non-grain biomass. However, the efficient utilization of these feedstocks remains hindered by mass-transfer limitations, thermodynamic constraints, substrate and intermediate cytotoxicity, and the inherent physical limitations of macromolecular catalysts. Intracellular multienzyme cascade catalysis offers a promising solution by organizing highly coordinated catalytic networks within living cells, thereby enhancing metabolic efficiency and overcoming multiple bioconversion barriers. In this review, we systematically analyze the mechanisms and engineering strategies underlying whole-cell cascade systems from the integrated perspectives of material, energy, and information flows. Based on these principles, we propose a generalizable diagnostic and design framework for the bioconversion of non-grain carbon feedstocks. We further illustrate how these general design rules can be tailored and implemented at the systems level for the efficient conversion of specific substrate classes. In addition, we highlight the emerging role of artificial intelligence in enabling predictive system reconstruction through generative design, global pathway optimization, and automated design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles. Collectively, this review establishes a unified theoretical and practical framework for the rational design of next-generation biomanufacturing platforms based on intracellular multienzyme cascade catalysis.
papers.authors: Wang X, Chen H, Ma CJ, Zhang JJ, Cheng F, Xue YP, Zheng YG.

papers.title: Overexpression of endogenous aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductase genes enhances ethanol biosynthesis in Clostridium autoethanogenum.
papers.abstract: Bioethanol is a promising renewable fuel that mitigates dependence on fossil resources. As a potential candidate for bioethanol production, the homoacetogen Clostridium autoethanogenum is capable of metabolizing diverse carbon substrates, such as syngas components (CO and/or CO 2 /H 2 ) and xylose. Since acetate formation is energetically favored over ethanol synthesis in acetogens, reassimilation of acetate through the aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (AOR) pathway offers a feasible approach to enhance ethanol production. To improve AOR activity, two endogenous aor genes (CAETHG_0092 and CAETHG_0102) were individually overexpressed in C. autoethanogenum under the control of two separate constitutive promoters, P thl and P pta , generating four engineered strains: Ca(pta92), Ca(pta102), Ca(thl92), and Ca(thl102). Fermentation performance of the engineered strains was evaluated with xylose as the substrate. Compared to the wild-type strain, all engineered strains showed less acetate accumulation and higher ethanol yield. Moreover, the highest ethanol yield, specific productivity, and ethanol-to-acetate molar ratio were achieved in strain Ca(pta102), reaching 3.19-fold, 2.86-fold, and 11-fold of those in the wild-type strain, respectively. Engineered strains also exhibited elevated AOR activity in crude extracts, ranging from 2.52 to 4.74 times that of the wild-type strain. Results demonstrated that overexpressing either of the endogenous aor genes shifted product distribution toward ethanol in C. autoethanogenum, which provides a promising metabolic engineering strategy to boost ethanol biosynthesis.
papers.authors: Lin S, Zhou Y, Chen X, Xu H, Fang C, Ruan Z, Guo Y.

papers.title: A Review on the Microbial Synthesis of Cadmium-Based Quantum Dots and Their Applications.
papers.abstract: Cadmium (Cd)-based quantum dots (QDs), noted for their size-tunable optoelectronic properties and remarkable photoluminescence, have attracted considerable interest and found widespread commercial applications. Preparation methods for Cd-based QDs typically involve harsh, environmentally hazardous chemical and/or physical processes, whereas microbial biosynthesis offers a sustainable, green alternative. This review provides an overview of microbial production of Cd-based QDs (cadmium sulfide (CdS), cadmium selenide (CdSe), and cadmium telluride (CdTe)) using wild-type and genetically engineered bacteria, fungi, and viruses, with particular attention to the underlying biosynthesis mechanisms. Key proteins and peptides implicated in catalyzing or promoting QD biosynthesis include cystathionine γ-lyase, threonine dehydratase, sulfide-quinone reductase, phytochelatin (oligoglutathione peptides), and other metal-binding proteins such as metallothionein. The roles of capping agents (e.g., phosphates, L-cysteine, and glutathione), Cd (II) efflux genes, and extracellular polymeric substances are discussed. The application of this process in hazardous waste bioremediation, whereby Cd- or sulfur-containing waste is converted into valuable Cd-based QDs, is also addressed. Diverse applications are summarized, including QD-sensitized solar cells, fluorescent labeling, photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants, and CdS-bacterial hybrid systems enabling photosynthetic production of organic compounds. This review contributes to a better understanding of Cd-based QD biosynthesis, although further efforts are needed to control synthesis and address biosafety concerns.
papers.authors: Li X, Lin J.

papers.title: Expanding photosynthesis through biosolar oxic N 2 fixation: toward a sustainable BioNitrogen Economy.
papers.abstract: Atmospheric dinitrogen (N 2 ) is far more abundant than carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), yet photosynthesis has been studied and harnessed predominantly for photosynthetic carbon fixation (PCF), underpinning the global biocarbon economy. In contrast, biological N 2 fixation-the natural gateway for atmospheric nitrogen into the biosphere-remains comparatively underexploited. Modern agriculture and industry consequently depend heavily on the fossil-fuel-intensive Haber-Bosch process, with substantial energy and environmental costs. Diazotrophic cyanobacteria offer a fundamentally different paradigm by coupling oxygenic photosynthesis to nitrogenase-mediated N 2 fixation. We term this process photosynthetic nitrogen fixation (PNF), which uses solar energy to convert water and atmospheric N 2 into bioavailable nitrogen. Beyond its ecological significance, PNF expands the functional scope of photosynthesis beyond carbon fixation and provides a biological foundation for sustainable nitrogen production, biofertilization, and N 2 -based biosolar manufacturing. Recent advances in cyanobacterial physiology, ecology, evolution, synthetic biology, and AI-enabled multi-omics are accelerating efforts to harness this potential. This review examines the diversity of diazotrophic cyanobacteria, their strategies for protecting oxygen-sensitive nitrogenase, and emerging approaches for genetic engineering cyanobacteria as programmable platforms for nitrogen production and crop-associated nitrogen delivery. We further propose a roadmap toward a solar-powered BioNitrogen Economy encompassing bioprospecting, synthetic biology, genomic engineering, crop integration, and scalable agricultural and industrial deployment. By expanding photosynthesis from carbon fixation to the solar-powered capture of both carbon and atmospheric nitrogen, PNF could help drive the transition from a fossil-fuel-dependent chemo-nitrogen economy toward a sustainable BioNitrogen Civilization.
papers.authors: Nawaz T, Gu L, Young J, Fahad S, Klein N, Sani R, Zhou R.

papers.title: Metabolic Engineering and Bioprocess Optimization Strategies Promote l‑Azidohomoalanine Biosynthesis in Fed-Batch Bioreactor Culture
papers.authors: Lacombe C, Striedner G, Wiltschi B.

papers.title: Microbiota-Associated Metabolites as Immunometabolic Regulators of Glomerular Inflammation: Disease-Specific Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Background Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN), membranous nephropathy (MN), and lupus nephritis (LN) are immune-mediated glomerular diseases in which dysregulated adaptive immunity converges with innate inflammatory and filtration-barrier injury. Clinical relapse and incomplete recovery despite upstream immune control motivate investigation of additional injury modifiers. Main body This review evaluates five microbiota-associated metabolite families-short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan-derived metabolites, aromatic amino acid-derived uremic solutes, trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), and bile acids-across three modules: immune-tolerance failure, innate inflammatory amplification, and filtration-barrier disruption. In IgAN, multi-omics data showing preserved or elevated systemic acetate with reduced glomerular free fatty acid receptor 2/3 (FFAR2/FFAR3)-associated signaling suggest impaired renal SCFA sensing, but do not establish receptor competence as the dominant target. In MN, disease-specific studies support podocyte injury mediated by complement C3a and its receptor (C3a/C3aR) and complement-associated NOD-, LRR- and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3)-caspase-1-gasdermin D (GSDMD) pyroptosis as related injury processes, whereas proposed SCFA-regulatory T cell (Treg)-B-cell and SCFA-inflammasome interactions remain largely hypothesis-generating; experimental Lactobacillus-indole-aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) data provide preliminary evidence. In LN, microbiota-dependent tryptophan pathway perturbation and treatment-associated metabolomic changes support the kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio as a readily measurable candidate biomarker requiring prospective validation. Across diseases, interpretation requires separating microbial production from renal retention, metabolite abundance from receptor signaling competence, and total from unbound exposure for protein-bound solutes. Conclusion Microbiota-associated metabolites constitute a plausible immunometabolic layer rather than established causal pathways in immune-mediated glomerular disease. Priorities include disease-specific longitudinal phenotyping, compartment-resolved metabolite measurement, target-engagement studies, and biomarker-embedded clinical trials before therapeutic claims are advanced.
papers.authors: Hou F, Yang L, Liu W, Liu W, Cui Y, Rui H, Liu B.

papers.title: Multiplexed mammalian gene control via modular splicing riboswitches
papers.abstract: Precise, multiplexed gene regulation in mammalian cells remains constrained by a heavy reliance on heterologous protein regulators, whose associated immunogenicity and strict cargo-size limits impede clinical translation. Here, we introduce SpliceRACER (Splice-based R iboswitch A rray for C ombinatorial E xpression R egulation), a multiplexed RNA switch platform that achieves scalable, orthogonal, and combinatorial control of gene expression in mammalian cells through alternative splicing, eliminating the need for exogenous protein co-expression. SpliceRACER independently orchestrates three orthogonal channels to regulate fluorescent reporter outputs, yielding 3³ = 27 discrete combinatorial expression states, vastly exceeding the capacity of conventional binary gene switches. Furthermore, we engineered three generalizable strategies to effectively suppress the basal leakage inherent to synthetic riboswitches, thereby enabling tight OFF-state control of the potent pyroptotic effector GSDMD-NT for precise cell-death induction. This work offers broad utility in synthetic biology and therapeutic applications. Graphical abstract
papers.authors: Jiang J, Ma T.
