papers.title: Metabolic engineering of Klebsiella oxytoca for highly selective meso-2,3-butanediol production with minimized byproducts.
papers.abstract: Producing enantiopure meso-2,3-butanediol (meso-2,3-BDO) with minimal organic acid byproducts is critical for its commercial applications in specialized polymers and cosmetics. In this study, we developed a highly selective and robust Klebsiella oxytoca platform using stepwise metabolic engineering and bioprocess optimization. Starting with a lactate- and formate-deficient parent strain (Δldh/ΔpflB), we sequentially deleted poxB and frdBC to suppress acetate and succinate byproducts. To resolve recalcitrant succinate accumulation caused by NADH surplus during micro-aerobic fed-batch fermentation, we implemented dynamic redox control strategies (nutrient supplementation and agitation shifts) and permanently sealed the reductive TCA branch by deleting mdh. Furthermore, to achieve ultra-high stereoisomeric purity, we disrupted the isomer interconversion network by knocking out dar and gldA. The resulting engineered strain (GSC-P8) was cultivated using the optimized redox-control bioprocess. This integrated scale-up fermentation completely abolished undesired stereoisomers, strictly maintaining meso-2,3-BDO selectivity at approximately 97.9%. We achieved a prominent meso-2,3-BDO titer of 125.2 g/L and a volumetric productivity of 2.84 g/L/h, while restricting each acidic byproduct to below 2.0 g/L. This study demonstrates a commercially viable strategy for pure meso-2,3-BDO production through rigorous intracellular redox homeostasis.
papers.authors: Song CW, Bal J, Park JM.

papers.title: Therapeutic Horizons of CRISPR/Cas9 Genome Editing in Overcoming Bacterial Antimicrobial Resistance: A Comprehensive Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Bacterial antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a global public health crisis that threatens to render conventional antibiotic regimens obsolete. The clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats-associated protein 9 (CRISPR/Cas9) system has emerged as a revolutionary tool in molecular biology, offering unmatched sequence-specific genome-editing capabilities. By leveraging custom single-guide RNAs (sgRNAs), CRISPR/Cas9 can precisely target, cleave, or modify specific genomic and plasmid-borne resistance determinants, thereby neutralizing resistance pathways or directly inducing lethal double-strand breaks in pathogenic bacteria. Beyond simple gene disruption, CRISPR-based tools can eliminate resistance-carrying plasmids, block horizontal gene transfer (HGT), impair virulence pathways, and dismantle biofilm architectures while preserving commensal microflora. This narrative review provides a rigorous, updated synthesis of the structural and mechanical framework of CRISPR/Cas9, its targeted application across major multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, a side-by-side analysis of various delivery systems, and the current balance of therapeutic promise against biological, ecological, and translational safety risks. Furthermore, we outline synergistic integrations with advanced nanocarriers, bacteriophage platforms, synthetic biology, and antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), laying out a prospective roadmap toward publishable clinical translation.

papers.title: 13 C-Metabolic Flux Analysis of Substrate Co-Metabolism in the Methylotrophic Acetogen Eubacterium limosum
papers.abstract: Acetogens are promising microbial catalysts for the sustainable production of fuels and chemicals, metabolizing a range of renewable single-carbon (C1) compounds with high energetic efficiency. The major challenge is their energy-limited anaerobic lifestyle, which results in slow growth and a limited product spectrum on individual C1 substrates. We previously showed in the acetogen Eubacterium limosum that co-metabolism of glucose-methanol or CO-methanol mixtures results in substantial improvements in growth and acetate productivity. To investigate the underlying mechanism(s), here we conducted 13 C metabolic flux analysis ( 13 C-MFA) of E. limosum grown on a glucose-methanol mixture, as well as in single-substrate controls. The results suggest that the main benefit of glucose cofeeding is not provision of additional ATP, but rather a reduction of flux through the ferredoxin-dependent and kinetically challenging reactions of the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway. Subsequent RNAseq analysis showed no significant differences in the expression level of genes involved in methanol metabolism between cofeeding and methanol-only controls, suggesting this reduction of flux is controlled post-transcriptionally. Most surprisingly, we found that under all growth conditions, flux through pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) was in the oxidative direction, with cysteine (added as a reducing agent) providing all required gluconeogenic carbon flux under CO 2 -fixing conditions. This work provides critical insights into the metabolic network of an emerging model acetogen that will facilitate future metabolic engineering efforts to channel flux to value-added products, and highlights the under-appreciated role of cysteine as a carbon source in acetogenic fermentations. Highlights 13 C MFA was conducted for E. limosum grown on methanol, glucose, or cofed. Cultures reached metabolic and isotopic stationarity in the AneVO chemostat. Flux distributions showed significant contributions of carbon from cysteine reducing agent. Cofactor analysis reveals cofeeding benefit is not simply additional ATP

papers.title: Biomanufacturing vascular matrix-mimetic hydrogels from quantified arterial micromechanics and microstructure.
papers.abstract: The microstructural and micromechanical properties of the arterial extracellular matrix (ECM) are central to vascular cell behavior but are disrupted by disease and aging. Elastin and fibrillar collagens provide essential cues, yet the effects of disease-associated ECM remodeling on smooth muscle function remain poorly defined. Here, we imaged fibrillar ECM components across layers of healthy and hypertensive arteries in a large animal model and quantified their stiffness with submicron and piconewton resolution. These animal-derived data guided the fabrication of artery-mimetic hydrogels using image-derived 3D projection micro-stereolithography (µSTL) and thiol-ene clickable bioinks. The resulting hydrogels replicated fibril features down to 2 µm with emulated curvatures and tunable stiffness spanning physiological to pathological ranges (1-35 kPa). Systematic optimization of printing parameters, including light intensity, exposure time, monomer concentration, crosslinker type, optical configurations, and hydrogel swelling solutions, ensured high-fidelity structural replication. Vascular smooth muscle cells cultured on these hydrogels revealed that diseased ECM conditions promoted hypertrophy, impaired contractility, and reduced calcium responsiveness. Quantitative PCR showed reduced expression of contractile markers (MYH11, SMTN) and marked upregulation of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase) on hypertensive-mimetic matrices, implicating focal adhesion-dependent mechanotransduction in this response. This image-guided biofabrication platform enables precise engineering of vascular microenvironments for mechanistic studies of remodeling, therapeutic testing, and modeling of complex vascular disease states. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Arterial extracellular matrix stiffens and reorganizes in hypertension, yet in vitro models rarely reproduce these micron-scale changes. We measured layer-specific stiffness and fibrillar architecture in arteries from normotensive and hypertensive steers, a large animal model with fattening-induced hypertension. These data were directly translated into projection micro-stereolithography of thiol-ene hydrogels. The resulting matrices, high-fidelity 3D hydrogel prints, reproduced fibrillar features down to 2 µm with emulated curvatures and tunable stiffness spanning 1-35 kPa. Vascular smooth muscle cells cultured on hypertensive-mimetic matrices exhibited hypertrophic morphology, reduced calcium responsiveness and agonist-induced contractility, altered contractile-marker expression, and increased PTK2 expression, linking disease-associated matrix remodeling to altered mechanotransduction. This measurement-to-fabrication workflow provides a physiologically informed platform for mechanistic studies of vascular remodeling and evaluation of therapeutic responses.

papers.title: Cyanobacterial conversion of CO 2 to bio-based diols and downstream valorization: biological basis, upgrading strategies, and applications.
papers.abstract: Cyanobacteria have attracted growing interest as photosynthetic cell factories for the conversion of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) into renewable chemicals because they directly use solar energy and inorganic carbon under mild aqueous conditions. Recent advances in chassis development, genome engineering, carbon-partition control, and photobioreactor design have expanded the scope of cyanobacterial CO 2 -to-chemical biomanufacturing. Among the reported diols, 1,2-propanediol (1,2-PDO), 1,3-propanediol (1,3-PDO), and 2,3-butanediol (2,3-BDO) represent distinct development cases. In particular, 1,3-PDO provides an established benchmark for fermentative diol production from organic feedstocks, whereas 2,3-BDO offers additional opportunities for stereochemistry-sensitive upgrading but requires further validation in several downstream applications. These stages are often studied separately, and their interdependence remains a major challenge for process integration. This review summarizes the biological and engineering basis of cyanobacterial diol production, product recovery and purification, major upgrading strategies, and application prospects in pharmaceuticals, energy-storage materials, hydrogels, fuels, polymers, and related functional products. Key challenges in biological productivity, selective upgrading, catalyst stability, feed quality, and process sustainability are also discussed. The review distinguishes demonstrated cyanobacterial production from downstream transformations reported for other feedstocks and identifies the requirements for connecting them.
papers.authors: Pan C, Chen H, Zhang M, He S, Lin Z.

papers.title: Elucidating the molecular mechanism of tryptophan-derived indole metabolite biosynthesis in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum DPUL-S164.
papers.abstract: Background Our previous research has revealed that the Lactiplantibacillus plantarum DPUL-S164 metabolizes tryptophan (Trp) to produce indole-3-lactic acid (ILA), indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and indole-3-carboxaldehyde (I3C). This study systematically elucidated the molecular regulatory mechanism of this strain for the metabolism of Trp to produce ILA, I3C and IAA through genome-wide functional annotation, bioinformatics analysis, high-performance liquid chromatography, and real-time fluorescence quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Results Under Trp-enriched conditions, the three indole derivatives showed significant time-dependent cumulative effects, with ILA biosynthesis exhibiting the most significant up-regulation. Molecular mechanistic studies have shown that the metabolic pathway involves synergistic regulation of multiple gene modules. The genes involved in Trp metabolism of DPUL-S164 was found to include genes encoding aromatic amino acid transaminases (AraT), genes encoding lactate dehydrogenase (ldh or ldhA) and genes encoding aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALD). During the process of DPUL-S164 metabolizing Trp to produce ILA, I3C, or IAA, the key candidate genes for AraT, ldh, ldhA, and ALD were significantly up-regulated over 3-24 h. In addition, this study identified gene0696 and gene0697 as a functional metabolic gene cluster in DPUL-S164 and involved in the regulation of its metabolic Trp-producing ILA pathway, which may be involved in the regulation of Trp metabolism as a key candidate gene cluster. Conclusion This discovery not only provides a new theoretical basis for elucidating the molecular mechanism of Trp metabolism in Lactobacillus, but also lays an important foundation for the subsequent metabolic engineering and synthetic biology research by identifying the core functional genes. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

papers.title: Metabolomics: A Unique Approach for Chemical Profiling of Plants-Derived Secondary Metabolites and Its Application in Plant Sciences.
papers.abstract: Introduction In-depth profiling of plant-derived metabolites is essential for unraveling chemically diverse group of bioactive compounds that play essential roles in plant defense, adaptation, ecological interactions, and human health. Comprehensive profiling of these metabolites is important for understanding their biochemical diversity and exploring their pharmaceutical, agricultural, and industrial potentials. Metabolomics is an emerging platform for qualitative and quantitative assessment of metabolites, employing GC-MS, LC-MS, and NMR. Objective To compare and critically assess the extraction, data acquisition, and data-processing protocols including chemometric analysis and applications of metabolomics. Methodology Metabolomics studies largely depend on optimized sample collection, extraction procedures, analytical platforms, and data-processing workflows for the chemical profiling of plant-derived metabolites. Following metabolite extraction from different plant parts, analytical data generated by GC-MS, LC-MS, and NMR are further analyzed, employing chemometric statistical approaches for identification of metabolic signatures, classification of plant samples, and to reveal biochemical variations associated with genetic and environmental factors. Results This review focuses on several applications of metabolomics in plant sciences, including elucidating plant responses to abiotic and biotic stresses, evaluating the effects of nutrient availability on metabolite biosynthesis, investigating genetic and phenotypic diversity among wild-type, cultivated, and transgenic plants, supporting crop improvement and metabolic engineering, authenticating medicinal plants, ensuring quality control, and accelerating the discovery of bioactive natural products. Conclusion This review provides comprehensive comparison of various extraction and characterization techniques of secondary metabolites, which will provide valuable insights as well as further directions to researchers working in allied field.
papers.authors: Prakash C, Rime P, Bahuguna A, Uniyal S, Anthwal A, Mahar R.

papers.title: Semi-Artificial Photosynthesis Enables Light-Driven Biomanufacturing in Non-Photosynthetic Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Semiconductor biohybrid systems integrate microbial biosynthesis with semiconductor light harvesting to sustainably power energy-intensive chemical production. Although such systems have been widely explored in photosynthetic bacteria, extending them to non-photosynthetic biomanufacturing chassis such as Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis) remains substantially more challenging, owing to peptidoglycan-induced nanoparticle aggregation and mass-transfer limitations, cytotoxicity, and inefficient interfacial electron transfer from loose adsorption between inorganic semiconductors and cells. Here, we propose a non-invasive enhancement strategy that leverages the endogenous hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) pathway of the B. subtilis host and couples it with semiconductor materials to construct a semi-artificial photosynthetic biohybrid system. This system harnesses light energy to enhance endogenous nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate hydrogen (NADPH) regeneration, thereby augmenting microbial production without genetic modification of the target biosynthetic pathways. Applied to engineered B. subtilis for 2'-fucosyl lactose (2'-FL) and surfactin production, the biohybrid system increases product titres by two- to three- fold. This strategy, integrated with metabolic engineering, is effective for rapid and enhanced chemical synthesis in B. subtilis, with potential applicability to other non-photosynthetic bacteria harboring endogenous H 2 S pathways.

papers.title: The Potential of Self-Maintainable Living Materials.
papers.abstract: Engineered living materials (ELMs) are emerging as a new class of autonomous and self-maintainable systems that integrate metabolically active organisms within structural scaffolds to create materials capable of sensing, self-repair, adaptive response, and long-term functional persistence. Unlike conventional smart materials, which remain externally programmed and limited in regenerative capacity, ELMs leverage the intrinsic capabilities of microorganisms, fungi, algae, and mammalian cells to support continuous environmental interaction and feedback-regulated behavior. These systems retain metabolically active biological components that can grow, sense, communicate, adapt, and, in some cases, self-repair and self-regenerate, positioning autonomy as the defining capacity of these next-generation materials. Recent advances in synthetic biology, including programmable gene circuits, quorum-sensing communication, and metabolic engineering, enable living components to execute closed-loop decision-making and maintain functionality with minimal external input. These capabilities are driving innovations across construction, agriculture, environmental remediation, bioenergy, and biomedicine, where ELMs enable functions such as damage-triggered mineralization, adaptive pollutant degradation, and therapeutic self-regulation. Despite this promise, key challenges remain in evolutionary stability, biocontainment, long-term viability, and scalable manufacturing. This Review examines the design principles, current challenges, and translational pathways toward self-maintainable and autonomous living materials capable of sustained operation in real-world environments.
papers.authors: Nadimifar M, Eufrásio-da-Silva T, Maeso L, Orive G, Dolatshahi-Pirouz A.

papers.title: A Biomanufacturing Digital Twin for Consistent N-1 Seed Bioreactor Transfers for Commercial Monoclonal Antibody Production.
papers.abstract: Process consistency in biomanufacturing, particularly for commercial products, is critical for achieving consistent yield and product quality. The N-1 seed bioreactor stage, where cells grow before the transfer to a production bioreactor, often faces variability in final viable cell density (VCD), which leads to variable seeding densities in the production bioreactor and subsequent variability in total protein output per batch. In this study, we address the challenge of precise batch transfer by developing an upstream, stage-specific, level-2 digital twin (digital shadow). Here we show that a cell growth process model predicts growth accurately and updates forecasts using off-line and in-line measurements, enabling precise determination of the final sample time. Deployment of this seed transfer digital twin led to all N-1 to production transfers falling within acceptable limits and resulted in statistically significant increases in harvest yield relative to historical batches. This improvement is attributed to significantly higher on-target accuracy of final N-1 VCDs and significantly higher working volumes in the production bioreactors. Our findings demonstrate that such digital twins ensure consistent cell density during transfer, improve overall upstream process consistency, and lay a foundation for more advanced process control strategies.
papers.authors: Luo Y, Pareek S, Zhang C, Sarnese K, Ritz D, Talwar S.

papers.title: Chalcone Synthase in Flavonoid Biosynthesis: Structural Features, Regulatory Mechanisms, and Functions in Plant Defense.
papers.abstract: Chalcone synthase (CHS, EC 2.3.1.74) is a key entrance enzyme in the biosynthesis of flavonoids from the common phenylpropanoid precursor into a specific flavonoid branch. Beyond its catalytic role, CHS functions as a metabolic hub linking flavonoid production, hormone signaling, and biotic stress defense, and contributes to pigmentation, ultraviolet protection, plant growth, development, and environmental adaptation. Recent structural studies further suggest that chalcone isomerase-like proteins can modulate CHS catalytic efficiency and product specificity, although the physiological significance of this interaction remains incompletely understood across plant species. This review summarizes recent advances in CHS structure and function, with emphasis on metabolic regulation, gene family evolution, disease resistance, and metabolic engineering. Future research should prioritize metabolic flux quantification, functional validation of CHS family members, causal analysis of disease resistance, and precision breeding applications.
papers.authors: Liu R, Ding G, Zhao C.

papers.title: Design-for-scale: Engineering strategies for robust microbial chassis to ensure good performance in industrial application.
papers.abstract: What does microbial robustness mean in the context of industrial bioprocesses, and which cellular design principles are required to maintain strain performance from laboratory to industrial scale? This review addresses these questions by presenting an integrated systems metabolic engineering perspective on microbial chassis design. Robust production hosts must maintain viability, metabolic function, production capacity, and population stability throughout the entire process trajectory, including the seed train, biomass formation, production, product accumulation, and late-stage stress exposure. The relevant engineering target is therefore not an isolated gene or pathway, but the coordinated cellular system as a whole. Genome architecture, expression control, stress regulation, metabolic flux distribution, membrane physiology, product export, and population stability must be aligned with the intended process and evaluated under dynamic, process-relevant conditions. Accordingly, robustness engineering should begin with the industrial objective in mind while remaining centered on the microbial host.
papers.authors: Sihler N, Takors R.

papers.title: Multi-omics analyses reveal environmentally adaptive cell-state remodeling during human iPSC biomanufacturing
papers.abstract: Abstract Human induced pluripotent stem cells can retain conventional markers of pluripotency while acquiring environmentally dependent molecular states that may influence their developmental competence. Yet, how biomanufacturing conditions reorganize the interconnected networks governing cell state remains poorly characterized. Here, we first examined compensation of hiPSCs to static aggregation and dynamic agitation by proteomics. We then examined hiPSCs during single-passage culture in stirred-suspension bioprocesses under varying oxygen and agitation conditions. Intracellular metabolomic and transcriptomic profiling revealed distinct responses across culture configuration, hydrodynamic exposure, and oxygenation. Transition into dynamic culture broadly remodeled mitochondrial organization, carbon allocation, mechanotransduction, proteostasis, and developmental regulation. Increasing agitation produced a persistent response involving cellular architecture, growth-factor signaling, genome maintenance, and Epiblast- and lineage-aligned programs, whereas oxygenation elicited a smaller and more transient metabolic and transcriptional response. Through comparison with a human gastrulation reference, we show that these adaptations intersect with natural developmental programs without reproducing coherent epiblast state or lineage commitment. These findings demonstrate that bioprocess conditions can preserve core pluripotent identity while remodeling broader molecular states associated with developmental responsiveness, providing perspective on evaluating and optimizing hiPSC quality in biomanufacturing beyond restricted marker panels.

papers.title: Optogenetic-enabled biomanufacturing of long-projecting motor tracts for neural reconstruction.
papers.abstract: Tissue-engineered spinal tracts (TE-STs), a subclass of micro-tissue-engineered neural networks, are designed to replace long-range axonal pathways but are limited by the slow intrinsic growth of many neuronal subtypes, particularly spinal motor neurons. Optogenetic stimulation provides cell-type-specific, precise control of activity that may accelerate neurite extension during biofabrication. Accordingly, this study evaluates whether integrating optogenetic stimulation into the biomanufacturing process enhances motor axonal outgrowth within tailored hydrogel micro-columns in vitro. Motor neuron aggregates from embryonic rat spinal cord were generated by forced aggregation and encased within agarose micro-columns (701 µ m OD, ∼300 µ m ID; 3-12 mm length) to create TE-STs. Neurons were transduced to express the red-shifted channelrhodopsin ChrimsonR. Stimulation parameters were first optimized in planar cultures, where a 1-hour red-light train at 10 Hz (625 nm) maximized neurite outgrowth without significant heating. TE-STs were then stimulated at 10 Hz for 1 h at 7 d in vitro (DIV) and then fixed at 21 DIV. Groups included transduced and non-transduced neurons, each with and without light stimulation. Axonal extension was quantified within the micro-column lumen, and two-way analysis of variance was used for analysis. TE-STs exhibited robust axonal growth with organized tract architecture, preserved neuronal health, and stable motor neuron phenotype. Transduced neurons with and without light stimulation extended axons faster than non-transduced controls, whereas no differences were observed between non-transduced neurons with or without light. Notably, transduced neurons exposed to a single round of optogenetic stimulation at 7 DIV reached ∼5.5 mm of growth by 21 DIV, representing a ∼2.5-fold increase over baseline controls. Brief, targeted optogenetic activation is sufficient to accelerate axonal growth of engineered spinal motor tracts during in vitro biomanufacturing. These findings establish optogenetic stimulation as a programmable biomanufacturing input that accelerates axonal assembly through activity-dependent mechanisms while remaining compatible with scalable three-dimensional tissue fabrication.
papers.authors: Burrell JC, Tien VJ, Vu PT, Clizbe DR, Spadola M, Ghenbot Y, Ozturk AK, Cullen DK.

papers.title: PrimeStack editors enable efficient and site-specific integration of large multigene cargos in plants.
papers.abstract: Precise, site-specific integration of large DNA sequences into plant genomes is a long-standing goal of crop biotechnology and synthetic biology, yet remains constrained by random insertion, inefficient homologous recombination, and gene targeting. Here, we present PrimeStack, a DSB-independent platform that integrates PE with the unidirectional large serine integrase Bxb1, leveraging evolved variants for enhanced activity, to achieve the programmable insertion of multigene, multikilobase cargos at predefined genomic safe harbors (GSH) in rice (Oryza sativa). Optimized prime editors first install attP landing sites with high fidelity and heritability followed by Bxb1-mediated recombination that generates irreversible integration of genetic information. PrimeStack enabled targeted large-cargo integration in regenerated rice plants with efficiencies of up to 45%, as determined by junction-specific PCR analyses. No obvious morphological differences from WT plants were observed at 5 weeks after transfer to soil under the evaluated conditions. We validate its utility by achieving targeted insertion of a carotenoid cassette at an experimentally confirmed genomic safe harbor. PrimeStack delivers a modular, site-specific gene stacking platform that enables predictable, multigene trait pyramiding and pathway construction at GSH, thereby accelerating the development of improved and resilient crop varieties, as well as scalable plant-based biomanufacturing and a powerful chassis for synthetic biology.

enrichment.titleZh: PrimeStack编辑器实现植物中大型多基因载荷的高效、位点特异性整合
enrichment.abstractZh: 将大型DNA序列精确、定点地整合到植物基因组中，是作物生物技术和合成生物学长期追求的目标，但随机插入、同源重组效率低以及基因靶向方面的限制仍然存在。本研究提出PrimeStack，这是一种不依赖双链断裂（DSB）的平台，将先导编辑（PE）与单向大型丝氨酸整合酶Bxb1相结合，并利用进化所得的变体增强活性，从而在水稻（Oryza sativa）预先指定的基因组安全港（GSH）中，实现多基因、数千碱基载荷的可编程插入。优化后的先导编辑器首先以高保真性建立具有高遗传性的attP着陆位点，随后通过Bxb1介导的重组，实现遗传信息的不可逆整合。根据连接位点特异性PCR分析，PrimeStack在再生水稻植株中实现了大型载荷的定点整合，效率最高达45%。在所评估的条件下，移栽入土5周后，未观察到这些植株与野生型（WT）植株之间存在明显的形态学差异。研究者通过在一个经实验确认的基因组安全港中定点插入类胡萝卜素基因盒，验证了该平台的实用性。PrimeStack提供了模块化、位点特异性的基因堆叠平台，使基因组安全港中的多基因性状聚合与途径构建具有可预测性，从而加快改良型、抗逆作物品种的开发，并推动可规模化的植物生物制造及强大合成生物学底盘的构建。

No obvious morphological differences from WT plants were observed at 5 weeks after transfer to soil under the evaluated conditions. We validate its utility by achieving targeted insertion of a carotenoid cassette at an experimentally confirmed genomic safe harbor. PrimeStack delivers a modular, site-specific gene stacking platform that enables predictable, multigene trait pyramiding and pathway construction at GSH, thereby accelerating the development of improved and resilient crop varieties, as well as scalable plant-based biomanufacturing and a powerful chassis for synthetic biology.

papers.title: Recent progress in microbial succinic acid production: integrating genome engineering and fermentation strategies.
papers.abstract: Succinic acid is a four-carbon dicarboxylic acid and important platform chemical with diverse applications in food and feed, pharmaceutical, textile, and bio-based polymer industries. Growing demand for sustainable and economically viable production routes has stimulated increasing interest in microbial routes for succinic acid biosynthesis as an alternative to conventional petrochemical processes. This mini-review summarizes recent advances in microbial succinic acid production, with particular emphasis on strain development, metabolic engineering, and fermentation-process optimization. Significant progress has been achieved through engineering of both native producers, Actinobacillus succinogenes, Mannheimia succiniciproducens, and Corynebacterium glutamicum and non-native production hosts, such as Escherichia coli, Klebsiella oxytoca, and several yeast species, leading to marked improvements in succinate concentration, yield, and productivity. Emerging approaches, including adaptive-laboratory evolution, systems-level omics, and CRISPR-Cas9, have enabled more precise control of carbon flux toward succinic acid biosynthesis while improving cellular tolerance to low pH and elevated succinic acid concentrations. In parallel, advances in fermentation and bioprocess strategies, particularly low-pH fermentation and enhanced CO₂ fixation, together with the valorization of renewable feedstocks such as lignocellulosic hydrolysates, offer promising opportunities to improve process feasibility and sustainability. However, their economic competitiveness remains strongly influenced by feedstock pretreatment, hydrolysis, detoxification, fermentation performance, and downstream processing requirements. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for industrial-scale succinic acid production are discussed, highlighting the importance of integrating strain engineering with innovative bioprocess design to develop robust, economically competitive, and environmentally sustainable production platforms.
papers.authors: Phosriran C, Jantama SS, Cheng KC, Jantama K.

papers.title: Identification and Functional Characterization of UbiA-Type Terpene Synthases in Inonotus obliquus.
papers.abstract: Inonotus obliquus (Chaga mushroom) is a medicinal basidiomycete rich in structurally diverse terpenoids, yet the biosynthetic enzymes responsible for sesquiterpene formation remain poorly understood. Here, we identified six UbiA-type terpene synthases (IoUbiA1-6) from the I. obliquus genome and functionally characterized them through heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae. GC-MS and NMR analyses demonstrated that IoUbiA1-4 catalyze the biosynthesis of bisabolane-type sesquiterpenes, including (+)-Z-α-bisabolene (1), (-)-β-curcumene (2), and (6R,7E)-α-bisabolene (3). Sequence alignment and mutational analyses revealed two highly conserved catalytic motifs, NQXXXXXXXED and QDXXDXXXD, that are essential for enzymatic activity, as alanine substitution of key residues completely abolished product formation. These results experimentally establish the catalytic significance of the conserved motifs in fungal UbiA-type terpene synthases. In addition, metabolic engineering of the mevalonate pathway in the A. oryzae expression host significantly increased 1 production from 3.99 to 61.13 mg/kg. This study expands the functional diversity of fungal UbiA-type terpene synthases, uncovers the molecular basis for bisabolane-type sesquiterpene biosynthesis in I. obliquus, and provides a foundation for the biotechnological production of valuable sesquiterpenoids.
papers.authors: Zhang L, Duan Y, Zhang Y, Wang C, Li C, Liu C.

papers.title: Metabolic engineering strategies for sustainable de novo isobutylamine production by Corynebacterium glutamicum.
papers.abstract: Background Short-chain primary amines are a versatile group of molecules in biological systems, derived from the decarboxylation of amino acids or the transamination of carbonyl-containing molecules. Isobutylamine, the decarboxylation product of L-valine, has applications in chemical synthesis of pharmaceuticals, herbicides, fungicides and specialized chemicals, where it is especially interesting as a substitute for petrochemical compounds. Since the chemical synthesis of short-chain primary amines is hazardous and environmentally unsustainable, we established an efficient biosynthetic approach in this work. Results The natural amino acid producer Corynebacterium glutamicum is an ideal chassis for the production of amino acid-derived molecules. In this study, we assessed the toxicity of several relevant short-chain primary amines on C. glutamicum. A crude extract assay demonstrated the decarboxylation of L-valine to isobutylamine by the L-valine decarboxylase VlmD Sv from Streptomyces viridifaciens. This enzyme was instrumental to extend production of pyruvate in three engineered strains to yield L-valine and subsequently isobutylamine. To ensure intracellular L-valine supply, the extracellular L-valine accumulation was decreased up to 20-fold by deletion of the genes for the branched-chain amino acid exporter BrnFE Cg and/or overexpression of the L-valine importer gene brnQ Cg . Surprisingly, expression of the transhydrogenase genes pntAB Ec from Escherichia coli did not improve but drastically reduced isobutylamine production. Biochemical analysis revealed that pntAB Ec expression depolarized the membrane potential. Conclusions This study demonstrated the highest production of isobutylamine and the highest production of any microbial short-chain primary amine in minimal medium. In shake flask cultivation, an isobutylamine titer of 12.1 g/L and a yield of 0.74 mol isobutylamine/mol glucose were obtained. Transfer to a 3 L fed-batch bioreactor fermentation was successful and a titer of 33.2 g/L was reached within 64 h with a yield of 0.47 mol/mol and a volumetric productivity of 0.52 g/l/h. Moreover, isobutylamine production on a second-generation feedstock was shown, highlighting the potential of sustainable bio-based production of isobutylamine.
papers.authors: Prasun T, Müller S, Stegelmann F, Blombach B, Wendisch VF.

papers.title: AICAR-induced energy supply and paracrine activity of endothelial cells accelerate chronic diabetic wound healing by promoting angiogenesis and modulating macrophage reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Chronic diabetic wound healing is severely hampered by endothelial cell (EC) dysfunction, defective angiogenesis, and a persistent inflammatory microenvironment, yet the crosstalk between EC energy metabolism and macrophage polarization in this process remains poorly understood. Here, we identified an AMPK-dependent metabolic pathway in ECs that orchestrated both angiogenic restoration and macrophage immune reprogramming for diabetic wound repair, and translated this mechanism into a functional three-dimensional (3D) scaffold (MEWs + GelMA@AI) fabricated by melt electrospinning writing technology. Acadesine (AICAR) efficiently induced a high-energy state in ECs by activating AMPK, preserving mitochondrial ultrastructure, enhancing respiratory-chain complex activity, and increasing VEGF expression and angiogenic potential. Notably, we discovered that AI-EXO, secreted by these metabolically activated ECs, delivered GAS6 to macrophages as a key paracrine factor, thereby triggering activation of the MER/AKT pathway and driving M1-to-M2 polarization. To our knowledge, this is the first report identifying exosomal GAS6 as a mediator of EC-macrophage crosstalk in diabetic wound healing. The MEWs + GelMA@AI scaffold, characterized by a porous structure and sustained AICAR release, exhibited excellent cytocompatibility and proangiogenic activity in vitro . In vivo , the scaffold significantly accelerated diabetic wound closure by promoting neovascularization, reducing inflammatory infiltration, and increasing the M2/M1 macrophage ratio, without detectable systemic toxicity in major organs. These findings establish a critical link between EC energy metabolism and immune microenvironment remodeling, providing a potentially translatable metabolic-engineering strategy for chronic diabetic wounds. This study opens new avenues for regenerative therapies targeting metabolic-immune interactions.
papers.authors: Su H, Liu C, Cheng Y, Cheng W, Xu A, Hu D, Shi H, Huang M, Yuan H, Huang C, Huang Y, Su S, Duan C, Feng X.

papers.title: Engineering microbial platforms for diversified biosynthesis of antidepressant tryptophan-derived neuroactive compounds.
papers.abstract: Tryptophan-drived neuroactive compounds, including serotonin, melatonin, 5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP), psilocybin, and related indole derivatives, represent an important class of therapeutics for depression and other neuropsychiatric disorders. However, conventional production through chemical synthesis or natural extraction remains limited by low sustainability, poor selectivity, and high manufacturing costs. Advances in synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, and enzyme engineering have enabled the development of microbial cell factories for the efficient biosynthesis of these high-value compounds. This Review highlights recent progress in engineering microbial platforms for antidepressant tryptophan derivatives, focusing on tryptophan overproduction, hydroxylation biocatalysts, downstream biosynthetic pathways, and cofactor engineering. We further discuss the emerging roles of bacterial heme-dependent tryptophan hydroxylases and AI-assisted enzyme and pathway engineering in expanding the biosynthetic toolbox. Finally, we outline current challenges and future opportunities for integrating intelligent strain design with advanced bioprocess engineering to advance the biomanufacturing of tryptophan-derived neuroactives.
papers.authors: Xu R, Yang F, Zhang L, Du G, Li J, Chen J, Kang Z.

papers.title: Innovative Applications of The Coumarin Scaffold In Medicinal Chemistry: Design Strategies and Therapeutic Potential.
papers.abstract: Coumarin (1,2-benzopyran-2-one) is a naturally occurring benzopyrone that serves as the core scaffold of a diverse class of bioactive compounds produced by plants, fungi, and certain bacteria. Coumarin derivatives exhibit a broad spectrum of biological activities, including anticoagulant, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and anticancer effects. Structural modifications such as hydroxylation, glycosylation, methoxylation, and prenylation improve their pharmacokinetic and therapeutic properties. Progress in synthetic chemistry, metabolic engineering, and biotransformation methods has enabled the production of new coumarin derivatives with greater solubility, bioavailability, and therapeutic relevance across multiple disease domains. This review highlights innovative strategies employed in the rational design of coumarin derivatives to enhance potency, selectivity, and pharmacokinetic properties. Emphasis is placed on structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies that underpin the development of coumarin hybrids with anticancer, antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anticoagulant, and neuroprotective activities. This review highlights recent advances in the rational design, synthesis, biocatalytic modification, metabolic engineering, structure-activity relationships, and therapeutic applications of coumarin derivatives.
papers.authors: Sharma M, Talwan P, Dalwal V, Gautam D, Kumar S.

papers.title: MINT: Predicting Enzyme-Cofactor Specificity by Multimodal Knowledge Transfer from Protein–Ligand Interactions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Protein-cofactor selectivity prediction is important for enzyme annotation, metabolic engineering, and biocatalyst discovery, but it remains challenging because experimentally supported associations are limited and unevenly distributed, and because biologically relevant differences can be subtler than those captured by general protein-ligand interaction models. Here, we present MINT (Multimodal Interaction Network with Teacher supervision), a multimodal framework for cofactor specificity prediction. MINT combines protein sequence features with cofactor sequence and graph representations and is trained with a gradual adaptation strategy that transfers useful information from a pretrained protein-ligand interaction model to the cofactor prediction task. On a fixed balanced held-out test set, MINT achieved the best overall performance among all compared methods (AUC = 0.932), and this ranking was reproduced in an independent family-stratified evaluation at the natural positive rate (pooled AUC = 0.939). Further analyses suggest that the pretrained model provides transferable structural information, while the gradual training scheme helps adapt that information to cofactor specificity. In a case study of the chemically near-identical NAD/NADP pair, MINT recovered 95.0-98.6% of true binders and resolved a single-phosphate-level distinction with direct relevance to engineering enzyme cofactor specificity. These results show that gradual transfer learning is an effective approach to cofactor specificity prediction when annotation is limited. TOC

papers.title: Mapping the proteome landscape in Euglena gracilis : global, phospho, and ubiquitin proteomes under anaerobic response.
papers.abstract: The photosynthetic flagellate Euglena gracilis (Euglena) exhibits a remarkable metabolic flexibility, enabling the dynamic coordination of energy production and resource partitioning during anaerobic adaptation. While the wax ester synthesis under hypoxia is well-documented, the regulatory interplay between protein abundance and post-translational modifications (PTMs) remains unexplored. A definitive understanding of this metabolic remodeling is hindered by the lack of high-depth proteomic resources and the fragmented genome annotations, which fail to capture Euglena's proteomic diversity and plasticity. Here, we provide a comprehensive Euglena proteome landscape through advanced LC-MS/MS analysis. By leveraging the recently refined proteome annotation, we identified 9,122 protein groups, 12,027 phospho-peptides, and 3,346 ubiquitinated peptides, establishing a comprehensive Euglena's proteome reference. Our results demonstrate that anaerobic adaptation is characterized by distinct phosphorylation and ubiquitination signatures that often occur independently of changes in global protein abundance, revealing a layer of PTM-mediated control over central metabolism during anaerobic adaptation in Euglena. This study provides a foundational resource that bridges the gap between genomic potential and functional metabolic in Euglena. By resolving the interplay between protein levels and PTM-driven regulation, our work offers a new resource for investigating environmental adaptation and provides a rigorous framework for future metabolic engineering in Euglena.
papers.authors: Yosua, Tamaki S, Nishino K, Ezoe A, Minami A, Kim JS, Firdaus ARR, Subroto T, Kosako H, Mochida K.
